  Measure ps_shifts(group). Measure ps_shiftDay(group).
  // The Office pays a Crow by the shift to sort, and a Crow who sorts two shifts has the rhyme in her hands.
  Action ps_work_shift(actor: group, site: place) "Take a shift at the sorting-tables, for the Office's four coin" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, dlo_sorting) and ps_sacks_at(dlo_sorting) and wears(actor, face_crow) and publicHours() and ps_shiftDay(actor) < day(clock).
    Time 24.
    On success { Set ps_shiftDay(actor) to day(clock). Increase ps_shifts(actor) by 1. Increase quantity(actor, gold) by 4. Increase goodwill(face_crow) by 1. }
    Result "Four hours at a sorting-table in a Crow, among Crows, who do not talk. A clerk puts a stack in front of you and you do what they do: read the direction, find the line, flick. The Office does not ask who you are; it asks only that you are not slow. By the end the rhyme is going in your head to the movement of your wrist, and you are paid four coin out of a tin, in pennies, by a hand that does not look up.".
  }
  Rule ps_shifts_teach when ps_shifts(party) >= 2 and not knows(party, ps_filing) says "By the second shift you are not reading the rhyme any more. Your hand knows it: a drowned man's letter goes to the first line, a Hill crest to the second, and the third sack of any line is where a parcel goes. It is simply how the Office is made." teaches ps_filing { }

  // ── The sacks ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // The search, an hour a sack. Going through a line sack by sack, you meet the Book at the third; going straight to the
  // parcels' sack of a line takes the Filing, and knowing the line takes a person who filed it or hid it or read the
  // drawer. Mabel's help halves the time. Any of it can be done in the burning-room until noon on the ninth.
  Action ps_dig(actor: group, rack: ps_rack, site: place) "Go through the next sack of {rack}" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and ps_sacks_at(site) and ps_may_search(actor) and ps_dug(rack) < 5
      and not ps_book_found(actor).
    Time 6.
    On success { Increase ps_dug(rack) by 1. }
    Result "You take a sack down off its hook, or stand it up off the iron floor, tip it on a table and go through it a piece at a time, as the Office does, reading directions and not letters. It takes an hour. The paper is damp, and gives off the smell of every house it ever went to.".
  }
  Action ps_dig_with(actor: group, rack: ps_rack, site: place) "Go through the next sack of {rack} with Mabel's quick hands" {
    Speaker strake.
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(strake, site) and ps_mabel_trusts(actor) and ps_sacks_at(site) and ps_may_search(actor)
      and ps_dug(rack) < 5 and not ps_book_found(actor).
    Time 3.
    On success { Increase ps_dug(rack) by 1. }
    Result "Mabel takes the other end of the table. She reads directions at a speed you would not have believed, and passes you what you ought to be looking at, and puts back what you ought not, and does it without ever looking as if she were doing anything. It takes half an hour. 'Practice,' she says.".
  }
  Action ps_open_parcels(actor: group, rack: ps_rack, site: place) "Open the parcels' sack of {rack} directly" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and ps_sacks_at(site) and ps_may_search(actor) and (knows(actor, ps_filing) or ps_rack_known(actor)) and not ps_pdone(rack)
      and not ps_book_found(actor).
    Time 6.
    On success { Assert ps_pdone(rack). Increase ps_dug(rack) by 1. }
    Result "You go straight to the third sack of the line, as the second verse says, three for a parcel, and tip it out. It takes the hour it takes. The thing about knowing the Office's rhyme is that it is a great deal shorter than the Office.".
  }
  // The Book turns up when its sack is gone through. It is in the third sack of whatever line it is in.
  Rule ps_book_turns_up within post_office when ps_book_in(?r) and (ps_dug(?r) >= 3 or ps_pdone(?r)) and not ps_book_found(party) and not ps_book_burned(party) and not carries(party, book_of_faces) says "The sack gives up a parcel the size of a breadboard, wrapped in oilcloth, tied with the tape the Registry uses, and in the corner of the wrapper, in a clerk's hand that has spent thirty years being careful: TO NOBODY, NOWHERE. Under the oilcloth, a ledger in white vellum gone grey at the corners, a brass lock that has been forced, and over the lock the Registrar's seal: a bare oval, with nothing in it. The Book of Faces has been lying in a sack among eleven thousand other pieces of paper, and nobody has looked." teaches ps_book_located {
    Assert ps_book_found(party). }
  Observe ps_book_wrapper at dlo_sorting when ps_book_found(party) and knows(party, ps_pell_is_pell) and not carries(party, book_of_faces) "The tape on the wrapper is tied in a clerk's knot, a Chapel knot, the kind the Clerk of the Book ties on a lectern's ribbon, and you know whose fingers it was. Somebody has tried, more than once, to untie it, and stopped.".
  Rule ps_wrapper_teaches within post_office when ps_book_found(party) and knows(party, ps_pell_is_pell) and not knows(party, pell_hid_book) says "You put the Chapel knot together with the Crow at the counter who squares forms that are square, and the parcel that came in the night the Registrar died, and it makes a single shape. Tomas Pell did not carry the Book out of the Chapel. He posted it, to the one address in Ombra that has never been delivered to, and went to work for the Post." teaches pell_hid_book { }
  Observe ps_hall_disturbed at dlo_sorting when ps_pell_moved_it(party) and ps_sacks_at(dlo_sorting) and (ps_dug(ps_rack_wanting) >= 3 or ps_pdone(ps_rack_wanting)) and not ps_book_found(party) "The third sack of the seventh line has been opened and retied since the first night. The knot is a Chapel knot, and the sack is lighter than it should be. Whoever sat beside it put something in another sack, and somebody has taken it for a place to hide.".

  // Reading the rhyme: heard from the clerks, understood by lore or insight, or read from the card in the drawer, or told by Mabel.
  Action ps_read_rhyme(actor: group, site: place) "Work out what the clerks' rhyme is sorting by" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, dlo_sorting) and ps_sacks_at(dlo_sorting) and knows(actor, ps_rhyme_heard) and not knows(actor, ps_filing)
      and ps_rhymeDay(actor) < day(clock) and ps_may_search(actor).
    Time 3.
    Resolve check(actor, lore, dc_fair).
    On success { Assert knows(actor, ps_filing). }
    On failure { Set ps_rhymeDay(actor) to day(clock). }
    Result "You stand in the aisle with your eyes on the sacks and your ears on the clerks, and it comes apart in your hands as a good riddle does: eight lines for eight ways of being lost, five sacks to a line, and a second verse that tells the clerk which sack by what the thing is. One for a letter, two for a card, three for a parcel. 'Nobody's own' is the last line because it is the bottom of the rhyme, and also, by the Office's lights, the bottom of the world.".
    Otherwise "You listen until the rhyme goes round and round in your head and means nothing but its own tune, as a nursery rhyme does. The hall has not told you what it is sorting by.".
  }
  Action ps_read_rhyme_wit(actor: group, site: place) "Follow the clerks' hands, not the clerks' words, to see where each piece goes" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, dlo_sorting) and ps_sacks_at(dlo_sorting) and knows(actor, ps_rhyme_heard) and not knows(actor, ps_filing)
      and ps_rhymeDay(actor) < day(clock) and ps_may_search(actor).
    Time 6.
    Resolve check(actor, insight, dc_hard).
    On success { Assert knows(actor, ps_filing). }
    On failure { Set ps_rhymeDay(actor) to day(clock). }
    Result "You give up the rhyme and watch the hands. A letter to a drowned man goes to the first line; a card with a Hill crest goes to the second; the clerk's wrist turns for a thing of a certain weight and the sack she takes is always the third on its hook. It is a system for hands, and the words are only how they hold it in their heads.".
    Otherwise "An hour of watching the clerks' wrists, and you are sure of one thing: they are very fast, and they are not thinking.".
  }
  Action ps_pick_drawer(actor: group, site: place) "Pick the lock of the Postmaster's drawer" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, dlo_office) and not at(dunnage, dlo_office) and not ps_drawer_open(actor) and knows(actor, ps_drawer_known).
    Time 12.
    Resolve check(actor, lockwork, dc_fair).
    On success { Assert ps_drawer_open(actor). }
    Result "It is a good lock for its age, and an honest one: it expects to be asked politely. A little oil from the taper-stand and twenty minutes of patience, and the drawer comes out on its runners with the sound of a deep breath.".
    Otherwise "The lock keeps its own counsel. It has been picked by experts, you gather, and has outlasted them.".
  }
  Action ps_read_card(actor: group, site: place) "Read the Filing, on its card in the Postmaster's drawer" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, dlo_office) and ps_drawer_open(actor) and not knows(actor, ps_filing).
    Time 3 minutes.
    On success { Assert knows(actor, ps_filing). }
    Result "A card in the Postmaster's own hand, with the rhyme on it, a line to a line, and by every line, in a smaller hand, what it means: THE DROWNED AND THE DEAD. REFUSED BY THE HILL. NO NUMBER IN THE DRIP. SHIPPED. UNSIGNED. RETURNED UNCLAIMED. NO NAME AND NO DOOR. NOBODY AT A DOOR. Below it, the second verse, and at the foot, in a clerk's hand, much older than hers: Do not put it on a card. A rhyme learned off a card is learned wrong.".
  }
  Topic ps_mabel_files with strake "Ask Mabel how the Office files what it cannot deliver" when ps_speaks(actor) and ps_mabel_trusts(actor) and not knows(actor, ps_filing) {
    Says "'It is a rhyme,' says Mabel, and sings it very quietly, with her finger tapping the table. 'Gone to the water, gone to the wall; and so on to the eighth. Eight lines, and five sacks to each line, and the second verse says which sack by what a thing is. Letter, card, parcel, bundle, bale. A parcel is always the third.' She looks pleased. 'You are not the first person who has asked me and had to be told it was a joke.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, ps_filing). Assert knows(actor, ps_rhyme_heard). }
  }

  // Getting in. A Crow is one of the Office's own, and walks through; anyone else is stopped at the hall door by whoever
  // is nearest. By night the hall is Pell's, and he turns a stranger out as gently as he would turn a cat.
  Rule ps_hall_challenged at dlo_sorting when at(party, dlo_sorting) and publicHours() and not ps_sacksMoved() and not ps_may_search(party)
    says "'Staff only,' says a Crow with a sack-hook, politely, and then four more say it, in the same voice, from the tables; and you are walked to the counter with the manners of an Office that has never once had to raise its voice." { Assert at(party, dlo_counter). }
  Rule ps_hall_challenged_night at dlo_sorting when at(party, dlo_sorting) and privateHours() and not ps_sacksMoved() and not ps_may_search(party)
    says "A lamp comes into the hall behind you. 'Go out, please,' says a man's voice, quite gently, from behind it; he does not say who he is, and does not need to. You go, and he goes with you, with the lamp, as far as the counter, and stands there until you are out of the door of the Office." { Assert at(party, dlo_counter). }
  Rule ps_furnace_cleared at dlo_furnace when at(party, dlo_furnace) and ps_sacksMoved() and not masked(party) and publicHours() and not ps_burn_done()
    says "The Office's clerks are in two lines along the wall, and a bare face is not a person, and at a Burning there is no room for something that is not. A Crow takes you by the elbow and walks you out to the counter, apologizing all the way." { Assert at(party, dlo_counter). }

  // The sacks are carried at ten on the ninth morning.
  Rule ps_sacks_carried at dlo_sorting when ps_sacksMoved() and ps_sacks_at(dlo_sorting)
    says "At ten the Office's clerks come into the hall in a line, eight of them, and take down the sacks without a word, two to a sack, and carry them out through the furnace door; and Mistress Dunnage stands at the head of the hall with her unlit taper and counts them out, forty, and the hooks swing a little, empty, as the last of them goes." { Retract ps_sacks_at(dlo_sorting). Assert ps_sacks_at(dlo_furnace). }

  // The Burning proper.
  Rule ps_burning_begins at dlo_furnace when ps_sacksMoved() and hour(clock) >= 12 and not ps_burning_begun(post_office) and not ps_flue_wet(party) and not ps_held(party) and not ps_flue_choked(party)
    says "The Postmaster takes down her taper. She has carried it unlit for a year. She lights it at the lamp on the lintel, once, and touches it to the kindling, and every Crow in the room takes one step back, all together, as if the room had breathed in. 'Noon,' says Mistress Dunnage, in the voice of a woman reading a will. The furnace takes. She picks up the first sack." { Assert ps_burning_begun(post_office). Set ps_burnStart(post_office) to watch(clock). }
  Rule ps_burning_wet at dlo_furnace when ps_sacksMoved() and hour(clock) >= 12 and not ps_burning_begun(post_office) and ps_flue_wet(party) and not ps_flue_choked(party) once
    says "The Postmaster touches the taper to the kindling, and the kindling hisses, and does not take. 'Wet,' says Mistress Dunnage, and for a moment she looks very old. She does not stamp or curse; she puts the taper back in its holder, and the clerks, who have seen her do it before and not for this reason, look at each other. 'The Rule says dry. We wait.'" { }
  Rule ps_burning_ends when ps_burning_begun(post_office) and not ps_burnt(post_office) and watch(clock) >= ps_burnStart(post_office) + 9 { Assert ps_burnt(post_office). }
  Rule ps_book_burns when ps_burnt(post_office) and not carries(party, book_of_faces) and not ps_book_burned(party) { Assert ps_book_burned(party). }
  Rule ps_book_burns_told at dlo_furnace when ps_burnt(post_office) and ps_book_burned(party) and not ps_burned_by_choice(party) and watch(clock) <= ps_burnStart(post_office) + 11 once
    says "The last sack goes into the fire, and the clerks say its number, forty, and the Postmaster shuts the furnace door on eleven thousand pieces of paper, one of which was the Book of Faces. The fire goes up the flue, and the Wet Post, for a moment, has the smell of every house in Ombra." { }
  Rule ps_burning_ends_told at dlo_furnace when ps_burnt(post_office) and carries(party, book_of_faces) once
    says "The last sack goes into the fire, and the clerks say its number, forty, and the Postmaster shuts the furnace door on eleven thousand pieces of paper. The Book of Faces is not among them: it is under your coat, and heavy, and slightly warm from the room." { }
  Rule ps_flue_dries when day(clock) == 9 and hour(clock) >= 17 and ps_flue_wet(party) and not ps_flue_choked(party) and not ps_burnt(post_office) { Retract ps_flue_wet(party). }
  Rule ps_flue_dried_told at dlo_furnace when day(clock) == 9 and hour(clock) == 17 and ps_wet_done(party) and not ps_flue_wet(party) and not ps_flue_choked(party) and not ps_burnt(post_office) once
    says "At five the boy comes in with a brazier on a pole, and stands it under the damper, and the Postmaster has the room cleared of everyone who is not a clerk. By six the flue has dried to a crackle. The Rule says dry, and the Rule says the Postmaster shall not hurry, and she has not hurried: she has only been very, very thorough." { }

  // ── Stopping the fire: a wet furnace, a choked one ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Action ps_turn_cowl(actor: group, site: place) "Turn the cowl of the furnace stack into the wind, so that the rain goes down it" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, dlo_roof) and day(clock) == 9 and hour(clock) < 12 and not ps_flue_wet(actor) and ps_roofDay(actor) < day(clock).
    Time 12.
    Resolve check(actor, climbing, dc_fair).
    On success { Assert ps_flue_wet(actor). Assert ps_wet_done(actor). }
    On failure { Set ps_roofDay(actor) to day(clock). Increase heat(actor) by 1. }
    Result "The cowl is iron, rusted on its pivot, and it takes both hands and your whole back to turn it a quarter, with the slates sliding and the pigeons going up round you in a clatter. It turns. The rain, which has been going past the stack all week, finds the open throat of it and goes in.".
    Otherwise "A slate goes out from under your boot and down the roof and off the edge and into the Cuff with a sound like a plate, and from the Post bridge a Crow stops, looks up at a bare face on the Office roof, and walks on very fast to find a Watch domino.".
  }
  Action ps_choke_flue(actor: group, site: place) "Ram the sweeps' wet sacking down the furnace stack with their long brush" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, dlo_roof) and day(clock) == 9 and hour(clock) < 12 and not ps_flue_choked(actor).
    Time 12.
    Resolve check(actor, trapwork, dc_hard).
    On success { Assert ps_flue_choked(actor). Assert ps_held(actor). Set ps_chokeAt(actor) to watch(clock). }
    On failure { Increase heat(actor) by 1. }
    Result "The sweeps leave their sacking and their long brush in the lee of the stack, and the rain has done the soaking for you. You take the cowl off the pivot, and feed the wet sacking into the throat of the chimney a fathom at a time, and ram it down with the brush until it will not go further and the draught coming up thins to a whisper and stops. It will be Mr. Penn the sweep, on the tenth, with his rods. Nobody is going to burn anything today.".
    Otherwise "The brush catches in the cowl's iron and jars out of your hands, and goes down the stack end-first with a noise like a bell. From the Post bridge a Crow stops, looks up at a bare face on the Office roof, and goes very fast to find a Watch domino.".
  }
  Rule ps_corbin_blamed at dlo_furnace when ps_flue_choked(party) and not ps_boy_dismissed(ps_corbin) and not ps_own_up(party) and watch(clock) >= ps_chokeAt(party) + 6
    says "Mistress Dunnage says nothing to the furnace. She says nothing to the line. She turns to the boy, who had the key to the roof and the poker, and says, in a voice with no edge in it at all, 'The Office has no use for a hand that cannot answer for a wet flue.' The boy takes off his Crow, which is too big, and puts it on the nearest sack, and goes out, and nobody stops him." { Assert ps_boy_dismissed(ps_corbin). Assert at(ps_corbin, offstage). }
  Action ps_own_up_act(actor: group, site: place) "Tell the Postmaster the flue was no work of the boy's" {
    Speaker dunnage.
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(dunnage, site) and ps_flue_choked(actor) and not ps_boy_dismissed(ps_corbin) and not ps_own_up(actor).
    Time 2 minutes.
    On success { Assert ps_own_up(actor). Increase heat(actor) by 1. }
    Result "Mistress Dunnage squares a stack of forms that is already square. 'The Rule,' she says at last, 'does not say who may be wrong.' She does not tell you to leave; she does not need to. 'The boy keeps his place,' she says. 'You will not come into this Office again with that face.' It is, you gather, as near to a courtesy as the Postmaster has.".
  }

  // ── Taking the Book: stealing, snatching, burning ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Action ps_take_night(actor: group, site: place) "Lift the Book out of its sack, and go" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and ps_sacks_at(site) and ps_book_found(actor) and privateHours() and not at(pell, site)
      and not carries(actor, book_of_faces) and not ps_book_burned(actor).
    Time 3 minutes.
    On success { Give book_of_faces to actor. Assert ps_pell_robbed(actor). }
    Result "You take it out of the oilcloth, which you leave in the sack for the next man to find, and fold your coat over it. It is heavier than a book has any right to be; ninety years of other people's lives. The sack is lighter by two pounds, and in a sack of eleven thousand pieces nobody will weigh it. Somebody will notice, in the end. He keeps the lamp.".
  }
  Action ps_take_day(actor: group, site: place) "Lift the Book out of its sack under your Crow's cloak, with the clerks about" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and ps_sacks_at(site) and ps_book_found(actor) and publicHours() and ps_lawful_hour() and ps_stealDay(actor) < day(clock)
      and not carries(actor, book_of_faces) and not ps_book_burned(actor) and ps_may_search(actor).
    Time 3 minutes.
    Resolve check(actor, stealth, dc_fair).
    On success { Give book_of_faces to actor. Assert ps_pell_robbed(actor). }
    On failure { Set ps_stealDay(actor) to day(clock). Increase heat(actor) by 1. Assert at(actor, dlo_counter). }
    Result "A Crow is passing a sack across the table to the next Crow; you are at the end of the line with your back to the room, and for the length of the sack's journey nobody is looking at you. It is a very long journey. When it is over the Book is under your cloak and the hall has not noticed.".
    Otherwise "A hand comes down on the sack as you lift the oilcloth, and a voice says, 'We do not take from the Nobodies.' You are walked out through the counter with the Book left in its sack and a Crow's hand under each elbow, and the Wet Post sees you go.".
  }
  Action ps_burn_book(actor: group, site: place) "Put the Book into the furnace yourself" {
    Grave "The fire does not give things back. Whoever the Book has been kept for, it is gone when it is gone.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, dlo_furnace) and carries(actor, book_of_faces) and ps_sacksMoved() and not ps_burnt(post_office) and not ps_flue_wet(actor)
      and not ps_flue_choked(actor) and not ps_book_burned(actor).
    Time 2 minutes.
    On success { Spend book_of_faces from actor. Assert ps_book_burned(actor). Assert ps_burned_by_choice(actor). }
    Result "You open the furnace door, and the heat takes the skin of your face like a hand. The Book goes in without a sound. The vellum curls first, then lifts, then goes up the flue as a bright fold that you watch until it is only air. Ninety years of who wore what, and the Lie that was kept by hand, and the proof of it: gone, as everything else posted to Nobody has gone. The Postmaster, who has seen you do it, does not say a word. It is not hers to say.".
  }
  Action ps_snatch_brawn(actor: group, site: place) "Wrest the third sack of the seventh line from the line as it is carried to the fire" {
    Grave "A sack taken from the Burning is not a Nobody's any more. If it goes wrong, the sack goes in with the Book in it.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, dlo_furnace) and ps_burning() and (ps_rack_known(actor) or ps_book_found(actor)) and not carries(actor, book_of_faces)
      and not ps_book_burned(actor) and masked(actor).
    Time 2 minutes.
    Resolve check(actor, brawn, dc_hard).
    On success { Give book_of_faces to actor. Assert ps_snatched(actor). Assert ps_pell_robbed(actor). Increase heat(actor) by 2. }
    On failure { Assert ps_book_burned(actor). Increase heat(actor) by 1. }
    Result "You go in between the Postmaster and the fire with a sack on your shoulder, and the Crows along the wall do not move, because the Rule does not tell them what to do about this. You tear the oilcloth open on the iron floor and the Book is in your arms, and somebody says, in a voice that is nothing to do with the Office, 'Thief,' and somebody else, 'It is not a Nobody's; it was only ever posted to one,' and you are through the door.".
    Otherwise "The sack is heavier than it looks and the Crow who has it does not let go; there is a brief and entirely silent tug of war, which the Rule wins. The sack goes into the fire in the Crow's hands, and the Book goes up with it, and Mistress Dunnage says its number, as she has said all the others.".
  }
  Action ps_snatch_slip(actor: group, site: place) "Slip the third sack of the seventh line out of the line while Mabel spills a table of letters" {
    Grave "A sack taken from the Burning is not a Nobody's any more. If it goes wrong, the sack goes in with the Book in it.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, dlo_furnace) and at(strake, dlo_furnace) and ps_mabel_trusts(actor) and ps_burning() and (ps_rack_known(actor) or ps_book_found(actor))
      and not carries(actor, book_of_faces) and not ps_book_burned(actor) and masked(actor).
    Time 2 minutes.
    Resolve check(actor, stealth, dc_fair).
    On success { Give book_of_faces to actor. Assert ps_snatched(actor). Assert ps_pell_robbed(actor). Increase heat(actor) by 1. }
    On failure { Assert ps_book_burned(actor). Increase heat(actor) by 1. }
    Result "Mabel knocks a whole table of the morning's returns on the floor, with a cry of such perfect, practised clerkly dismay that every Crow in the room turns to look at it, including the Postmaster. You are on your knees among the letters in the one place in the room where nobody is looking. When you stand up you have a parcel the size of a breadboard under your cloak, and Mabel has not looked at you once.".
    Otherwise "Mabel drops the table, and the clerks turn, and Pell, at the Postmaster's elbow, does not: he is looking at you. He does not say anything. The Crow with the sack takes it to the fire before you can reach it, and Mabel sinks to her knees among the letters, and does not look at you.".
  }
  Rule ps_pell_saw_it within post_office when ps_snatched(party) and not ps_pell_robbed_told(party) says "Tomas Pell, at the Postmaster's elbow, closes his eyes as you go, the way a man does when someone has lifted a weight off his back and he has not yet found out whether he can stand." { Assert ps_pell_robbed_told(party). }
  Relation ps_pell_robbed_told(group).

  // ══ TOMAS PELL ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  // The Clerk of the Book, hiding at the Office's counter in a Crow and a false name. He will not give the Book up to
  // evidence, because he has no doubt of what it proves; he is a man who cannot take a thing out of a sack because then it
  // would be he that had done it. What moves him is not an argument: being forgiven (by Pip, who saw), being asked as a
  // penitent, or the Registrar's own hand. Short of those, he can be watched, pressed, lied to, frightened or sat with, and
  // each gets a different Pell.
  Topic ps_pell_cold_day with pell "Speak to the clerk" when ps_cold_day(actor) and ps_pell_home() {
    Says "'The counter serves faces,' says the Crow, to the rail, and squares a form that is already square. He has said it so often that it has worn smooth, like the rail.".
  }
  Topic ps_pell_cold_night with pell "Speak to the man on the stool" when ps_cold_night(actor) and ps_pell_home() {
    Says "'Not with that on,' says the man on the stool, very quietly, not looking up. 'At night the Office answers a face it can see. I will not talk to a mask in my own lamp.'".
  }
  Topic ps_pell_office with pell "Ask the clerk what the Office does with what it cannot deliver" when ps_speaks(actor) and ps_pell_home() {
    Says "'Keeps it,' says the clerk. 'A year. Forty sacks, and eleven thousand pieces by the last count; I counted twice. Then on the ninth day, at noon, Mistress Dunnage burns it.' He squares a form. 'It is the one day in Ombra when something is allowed to be finished.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, ps_nobodies). }
  }
  Topic ps_pell_crow with pell "Speak to him as one Crow to another" when wears(actor, face_crow) and publicHours() and ps_pell_home() and not ps_sacksMoved() once {
    Says "'Colleague,' he says, and for the first time he looks at the beak of your mask and not at the middle of the counter. 'There is a shelf behind my head. Unclaimed. A parcel, nearly a year, directed to whoever wore the Cockle at the fifth bell on Michaelmas Eve. Every Cockle on the Wet Post has held it and put it down. A kind Crow might take it round.' He looks at the forms. 'I find that I cannot. I do not go round.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, ps_parcel_known). }
  }
  Topic ps_pell_parcel with pell "Take the parcel off the Unclaimed shelf" when ps_speaks(actor) and knows(actor, ps_parcel_known) and not ps_parcel_given(actor) and not ps_sacksMoved() and ps_pell_home() once {
    Says "'Sign for it,' says Pell, and pushes the book across. You sign. He does not read what you have signed; it is perhaps the only thing in the Office he has not read. 'It is the lightest thing we have,' he says. 'Not by weight.'".
    On discuss { Give ps_parcel to actor. Assert ps_parcel_given(actor). }
  }

  // Seeing who he is. The Clerk of the Book has ink on the wrong finger and a Chapel knot in his mask-string.
  Action ps_pell_watch(actor: group, site: place) "Watch the clerk's hands while you ask him about the Registrar" {
    Speaker pell.
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(pell, site) and ps_speaks(actor) and not knows(actor, ps_pell_is_pell) and ps_pellDay(actor) < day(clock).
    Time 4 minutes.
    Resolve check(actor, insight, dc_fair).
    On success { Assert knows(actor, ps_pell_is_pell). }
    On failure { Set ps_pellDay(actor) to day(clock). }
    Result "'The Registrar,' you say, as if idly. The hands go on squaring the forms; it is the little finger that gives him away, the one that stops, in the middle of a stroke, and stays stopped. It is the ink-callus of a man who has written one hand for thirty years, and the knot in the string of his domino is no post-clerk's knot: it is the one they tie on a lectern's ribbon. You know who he is before he has finished not looking at you.".
    Otherwise "'The Registrar,' you say. The clerk squares a form. 'Is dead,' he says. 'It was in the Sleeves.' He goes on squaring, and you have nothing to show for it but a clerk who has noticed that you were looking.".
  }
  Action ps_pell_press(actor: group, site: place) "Tell him you know whose clerk he was, and ask what he did with the Book" {
    Speaker pell.
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(pell, site) and ps_speaks(actor) and knows(actor, ps_pell_is_pell) and not ps_pell_admits(actor) and ps_pellDay(actor) < day(clock).
    Time 6 minutes.
    Resolve check(actor, persuasion, dc_hard).
    On success { Assert ps_pell_admits(actor). Assert knows(actor, pell_hid_book). Assert knows(actor, ps_rack_told). Assert ps_rack_known(actor). }
    On failure { Set ps_pellDay(actor) to day(clock). }
    Result "You say it quietly, as one would to someone on a ledge. The clerk's hands stop. He does not deny it; he looks at them, at the ink on the wrong finger, as at something that has been betraying him for a week. 'It is in the Wanting,' he says. 'The third sack of the seventh line. I did not put it in Nobody's own, because that would have been a joke, and she would not have had it joked about.' He takes a breath that seems to go a long way down. 'I will not take it out. I have told you where it is. I would be glad,' he says, 'if you would not ask me to do more.'".
    Otherwise "'There is no Pell in the Office,' says the clerk, and for a moment he looks at you with his whole face, and you see that it is the face of a man who would very much like to be believed. 'There is a Dacre. He is at the counter. If you would like to post something, Dacre will see it posted.' He has said it very steadily, and you have not moved him an inch.".
  }
  Action ps_pell_lie(actor: group, site: place) "Tell him the Chaplain has sent you for the Book, as the Registrar's executor" {
    Speaker pell.
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(pell, site) and ps_speaks(actor) and knows(actor, ps_pell_is_pell) and not ps_pell_admits(actor) and ps_pellDay(actor) < day(clock).
    Time 4 minutes.
    Resolve check(actor, deception, dc_hard).
    On success { Assert ps_pell_admits(actor). Assert knows(actor, pell_hid_book). Assert knows(actor, ps_rack_told). Assert ps_rack_known(actor). Assert ps_pell_lied_to(actor). }
    On failure { Set ps_pellDay(actor) to day(clock). }
    Result "The clerk reads your face as he would a bill of lading, and you watch him decide to believe it, which is a different thing from believing it. 'Father Ansel would have written,' he says. 'He writes to everyone.' But he has put the forms down. 'The third sack of the seventh line. If the Chaplain wants it, the Chaplain may come and take it out of the sack himself, and I will stand beside him.' It is a sentence he has been waiting a week to be asked to say, and you have taken it with a lie.".
    Otherwise "'The Chaplain,' says the clerk, 'does not send people to a counter.' He says it with real regret, as a man tells a boy that the trick is not going to work. 'Good day.'".
  }
  Action ps_pell_threaten(actor: group, site: place) "Tell him you will say his name aloud in the Wet Post, at noon, from the bridge" {
    Speaker pell.
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(pell, site) and ps_speaks(actor) and knows(actor, ps_pell_is_pell) and not ps_pell_admits(actor) and not ps_pell_threatened(actor).
    Time 3 minutes.

  // Whoever has the Book at the ninth night, and whoever has not: the fates are with the closing news (below).

  // ══ THE CLERK WHO READS ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  // Mabel Vickery reads the dead letters the Rule leaves to burn and takes the ones that matter round by night, by hand,
  // to doors on the Post-lodgings stair: a kindness, and Unfacing too, since to deliver a letter you must know whose
  // street it is. Mistress Dunnage has found that somebody does it, and will have found who by noon on the seventh day.
  // She keeps three in her satchel. A company may carry them, read them, decide which not to deliver; may tell Dunnage,
  // stop Mabel, or argue her case in the Office's own words; and each of these leaves a woman in or out of a place.
  Discovery ps_mabel_reads "Mabel Vickery, a clerk of the Dead Letter Office's sorting-hall, reads the dead letters that matter and takes them round by night, by hand, to doors she could only know by reading them; Mistress Dunnage will have found her out by noon on the seventh day.".
  Discovery ps_l1_text "A letter from Piers Roke, now master of a ferry at Valmere, to his sister Aveline at the Wet Post: nine years since their father's funeral and the quarrel over the boat; he has kept the boat, and a place at his table, and writes that a loaf sent by anyone would do for an answer.".
  Discovery ps_l2_text "A letter from the late Master Corley, a chandler, to Teodor Wick, a baker: the forty crowns Wick owed him are written off in the book, he was sorry for what he said at the christening, and Wick is to buy the boy boots.".
  Discovery ps_l3_text "A letter from Hal Corry to Lucia Brandt on the Post-lodgings stair: if she marries Gerrit Hale on the eighth, he will stand on the Post bridge at the Fifth Bell and say her name aloud, both of them, the one she wears on Tuesdays and the one she was christened with.".

  Kind ps_brandt_kind "a letter to Lucia Brandt" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A letter on good paper, heavily blotted, in a hand pressed so hard that it has come through on the back. It is directed to the first door on the Post-lodgings stair.".

'The Rule is a thing a person does not choose, Madam, nor, I find, Sir; I have found it has been choosing me for twenty-six years.' She has the girl sent for. You do not stay for it. When you are at the door she says, without turning, 'The Office does not forget a service. Whatever you wish to see in the hall, you may see. The Filing is in this drawer; I give it to you to read.'   Action ps_plead_clause(actor: group, site: place) "Show the Postmaster that the Rule's own clause lets a clerk redeem a letter for its addressee, for a penny" {
    Speaker dunnage.
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(dunnage, site) and wears(actor, face_crow) and publicHours() and knows(actor, ps_redeem_clause) and knows(actor, ps_mabel_reads)
      and not ps_mabel_kept(actor) and not ps_mabel_dismissed(strake) and ps_pleadDay(actor) < day(clock).
    Time 10 minutes.
    Resolve check(actor, lore, dc_fair).
    On success { Assert ps_mabel_kept(actor). Assert ps_mabel_redeems(actor). Assert ps_mabel_trusts(actor). Assert ps_mabel_leave(actor). Increase goodwill(face_crow) by 1. }
    On failure { Set ps_pleadDay(actor) to day(clock). }
    Result "You do it as a colleague, in the Office's own words. No piece shall be kept back, you say, save such as be redeemed before the stroke by any person that will pay its carriage and put a name to it; the Rule does not say what the person redeems it for; it says only that she pays. 'A clerk who pays a penny and puts the name of the addressee to a letter is redeeming it,' you say, 'and the Rule says no piece shall be kept back from her.' Mistress Dunnage's face does something that is very rare for it. 'Twenty-six years,' she says, 'I have read that clause for the money in it.' She takes the taper from its stand and puts it in again. 'Vickery will pay a penny a piece, and sign the Redemptions. In the day. In the Office. As an agent.' It is, you see, the first time in forty-one Postmasters that the Rule has been used to deliver anything.".
    Otherwise "You say it, and mean it, and the Postmaster hears it out, and says, 'That is not what the clause is for.' She does not say what it is for. 'I should be glad to be shown,' she says, which is, from her, an invitation to a better argument than yours.".
  }

  Action ps_deliver_roke(actor: group, site: place) "Take the letter to the third door on the stair" {

    Result "You knock three times on the third door, as a person knocks who has a thing to put in a hand. A woman of fifty opens it in a nightgown and a shawl with a kettle in her other hand, bare-faced, not at all surprised, because at night a knock is only a knock. You give her the letter. She reads it on her threshold in the lamp from the stair, and you watch her do the sum of nine years: the funeral, the boat, the quarrel about the oars. She does not cry. She says, to the letter, 'He kept the boat.' Then she says, to you, 'Whoever you are, come in and have the tea. I shall not be able to sit still.' You do not stay. When you go down she is reading it again.".
  }
  Action ps_deliver_wick(actor: group, site: place) "Take the letter to the second door, where the baker lodges" {

    Result "Wick opens the second door in his shirt, with a candle, bare-faced and larger than he looks by day, and sees nothing he knows. You tell him the letter is for him, from the late Master Corley, and he takes it as a man takes a summons. He reads it with his lips moving. There is a long silence on the stair. 'Written off,' he says. 'He said at the christening that it was forgotten. He said it in front of everybody, and I took it for a thing to be remembered. I have gone round the Wet Post by the canal for three years to keep out of sight of his shop.' He turns the page. 'Boots,' he says, in a different voice. 'He remembered the boy.'   Action ps_deliver_brandt(actor: group, site: place) "Slide the third letter under the door on the first landing" {

Behind you the chain comes off, and you hear her read it, and stop, and read it again, and say, quietly, with no one to say it to, 'He means it.' She does not thank you.   // ══ DELIVERY TO A MASK ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  // On the Unclaimed shelf a parcel has waited nearly a year, directed to whoever wore the Cockle at the fifth bell on
  // Michaelmas Eve. The Office delivers to faces, not to hours, and two hundred wear the Cockle; and to ask who wore it
  // is to Name. A sailor's mother sewed a wedding-dress to the look of a woman at a bakehouse counter, whose name he
  // never learned. Four Cockles work the Wet Post bakehouse. The recipient may be deduced, asked for (as a Cockle, when
  // the trade has been worked beside), guessed, or Named; handed the parcel by day in the street, or by night on her
  // own stair; and the parcel is burnt with the Nobodies at noon on the ninth if nobody takes it.
  Kind ps_parcel_kind "a brown-paper parcel" is gear worth 0 weighing 1 described "A parcel in brown paper tied with kitchen string, soft in the middle, smelling of cedar. The direction is in block capitals: TO WHOEVER WORE THE COCKLE AT THE FIFTH BELL ON MICHAELMAS EVE, AT THE BAKEHOUSE ON THE WET POST. It has been dusted.".
  Item ps_parcel "a brown-paper parcel" is ps_parcel_kind at offstage.
  Discovery ps_note_text "The parcel holds a wedding-dress of cream wool, cut short in the hem to keep out of the flour, and a note: from a sailor, who met a Cockle at the bakehouse at the fifth bell on Michaelmas Eve, bought bread, was promised she would wait, and has not been able to come back; he says to burn it if she has married, and to find him at the ferry-stairs at Valmere if she has not.".
  Discovery ps_clue_left "The Cockle at the bakehouse counter on Michaelmas Eve gave the sailor his change with her left hand.".
  Discovery ps_clue_blue "The Cockle's mask-string had broken, and was mended with a blue thread.".
  Discovery ps_clue_bread "The Cockle told the sailor that bread is a promise kept warm.".
  Relation ps_parcel_read(group). Relation ps_parcel_delivered(group). Relation ps_odile_night(group). Relation ps_wrong_handed(group). Relation ps_kneaded(group). Relation ps_odile_ruined(group).

  Action ps_open_parcel(actor: group, site: place) "Open the parcel" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and carries(actor, ps_parcel) and not ps_parcel_read(actor).
    Time 5 minutes.
    On success { Assert ps_parcel_read(actor). Assert knows(actor, ps_note_text). Assert knows(actor, ps_clue_left). Assert knows(actor, ps_clue_blue). Assert knows(actor, ps_clue_bread). }
    Result "Under the brown paper, cedar shavings; in the shavings, folded in tissue gone soft, a wedding-dress of cream wool: not silk, a dress for a woman who works, high at the neck, and cut a little short in the hem so as not to trail in the flour. A paper is pinned to the bodice. 'To whoever wore the Cockle at the fifth bell on Michaelmas Eve at the bakehouse on the Wet Post. I do not know your name; you do not know mine; that was the beauty of it. You gave me my change in your left hand and said bread was a promise kept warm, and when I laughed you said it was not mine to laugh at. You had a blue thread in your mask-string where it had broken and flour to the elbows. I said I would come back in the spring and you said you would wait. The ship is held. My mother sewed this to the look of you. I was a fool to think a man could marry a mask. If you have married, burn it and be happy. If not, I am at the ferry-stairs at Valmere. J.'".
  }

She opens it there, under the stair-lamp, the cedar and the tissue and the wool, and she reads the note, which does not take long, and stands. 'I married Hobart Ollerton at the Annunciation,' she says. 'He is a chandler and he is kind and he does not know that anything was ever said.'   Relation ps_thanks_taken(group). Relation ps_thanks_delivered(group).
  Action ps_take_thanks(actor: group, site: place) "Take the bundle of thanks addressed To Nobody out of the sack" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and ps_sacks_at(site) and ps_may_search(actor) and ps_dug(ps_rack_nobody) >= 1 and not ps_thanks_taken(actor) and ps_lawful_hour().
    Time 3 minutes.
    On success { Give ps_thanks to actor. Assert ps_thanks_taken(actor). }
    Result "By the Rule a Nobody is nobody's, and nobody is going to miss a bundle of thanks. You tie the nearest hundred and some in their string and put them inside your coat, where they sit against your ribs like a small warm animal.".
  }
  Topic ps_nobody_thanks with nobody "Give Sister Nobody the bundle of thanks the Post could not deliver" when carries(actor, ps_thanks) once {
    Says "She does not take them. She looks at the bundle and at the hand that holds it, and then she puts her own hands behind her back like a child at a shop. 'They are not for me,' she says. 'There is nobody here to thank.' She is silent. 'Leave them on the shelf by the ladle. If anybody should ever read them, it would be an accident.'".
    On discuss { Spend ps_thanks from actor. Assert ps_thanks_delivered(actor). }
  }

  // ── What the Office does to those who have lost the Book from it ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe ps_pell_robbed_day at dlo_counter when ps_pell_robbed(party) and ps_pell_home() and not ps_pell_free(party) and publicHours() "The forms on the rail are not square. For the first time since you came, one of them has been left crooked, and the clerk has not noticed. He is looking at the sorting-hall door.".
  Observe ps_pell_robbed_night at dlo_sorting when ps_pell_robbed(party) and ps_pell_home() and not ps_pell_free(party) and privateHours() and not ps_sacksMoved() "The stool in the aisle between the seventh line and the eighth has been pushed back against the wall, and the coat that was on it is gone. The sack you took the Book from has been hung straight, and tied, with a clerk's knot, by someone who knew that it was light.".

  // ── Milestones ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Milestone ps_m_rhyme "learned the Office's rhyme" worth 25 when knows(party, ps_filing).
  Milestone ps_m_found "found the Book of Faces among the Nobodies" worth 75 when ps_book_found(party).
  Milestone ps_m_vigil "sat up with Tomas Pell on the Chapel steps" worth 25 when ps_vigil_kept(party).
  Milestone ps_m_pell "had Tomas Pell put the Book down himself" worth 75 when ps_pell_free(party).
  Milestone ps_m_fire "kept the Nobodies from the fire at noon" worth 50 when ps_wet_done(party) or ps_held(party).
  Milestone ps_m_mabel "kept Mabel Vickery her place in the Office" worth 50 when ps_mabel_kept(party).
  Milestone ps_m_letter "put a dead letter in a living hand" worth 25 when ps_roke_delivered(party) or ps_wick_delivered(party) or ps_brandt_delivered(party).
  Milestone ps_m_cockle "found whom the wedding-dress was for" worth 50 when ps_parcel_delivered(party).
  Milestone ps_m_thanks "carried the Drip's thanks to Nobody" worth 25 when ps_thanks_delivered(party).

  // ── The closing news ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // Pell: who he was to the Book at the end of the ninth night.
  Rule ps_news_pell_free when newsHour() and ps_pell_free(party) and not ps_book_burned(party) once
    says "Of Tomas Pell: he sat on the Chapel steps until Father Ansel came out with a lamp and a bench, and he has taken off the Crow and has not put it on again. He is said to be teaching the novices to square their forms, and to have been seen laughing once, at something the Chaplain said about the Rule." { }
  Rule ps_news_pell_free_burned when newsHour() and ps_pell_free(party) and ps_book_burned(party) once
    says "Of Tomas Pell: he was told that the Book had gone into the fire after all, by the hand that had carried it out of his. He said that it was the first thing that had come right since the night, and would not say what he meant. He has taken a room over the Candle bridge and keeps the Registrar's lamp trimmed." { }
  Rule ps_news_pell_boy when newsHour() and ps_pell_free(party) and ps_pell_child_asked(party) once
    says "Of Tomas Pell, also: he has sent a pair of boots down to the cisterns, by the lamp-boys' ladder, a size too large, with no note. A boy grows into them." { }
  Rule ps_news_pell_lied when newsHour() and ps_pell_lied_to(party) once
    says "Of Tomas Pell, and the Chaplain: Father Ansel has had it from him that a stranger once said the Chaplain had sent them, and that he had known it was not so, and had chosen to believe it. The Chaplain, who had sent nobody, said that it was a very good lie and that he would have believed it himself. Pell says he is not angry. He mentions it only to people who might have done it." { }
  Rule ps_news_pell_robbed when newsHour() and ps_pell_robbed(party) and not ps_snatched(party) and not ps_pell_free(party) and not ps_pell_chapel(pell) and not ps_pell_fled(pell) once
    says "Of Tomas Pell: he is at the counter of the Dead Letter Office still, under another man's name, with the forms squared, and the third sack of the seventh line hung straight. He has not asked who took it. He is observed, now and then, to look at the hall door as a man looks at a window he has left open for somebody." { }
  Rule ps_news_pell_stayed when newsHour() and ps_burnt(post_office) and ps_book_burned(party) and not ps_pell_free(party) and not ps_burned_by_choice(party) and not ps_pell_fled(pell) and not ps_pell_chapel(pell) once
    says "Of Tomas Pell: at noon on the ninth day he stood at Mistress Dunnage's elbow with the Crow on, and watched the third sack of the seventh line go into the fire, and said its number with the clerks. He has not been seen at the counter since. It is said that a man sits under the lamp-room window of the Chapel at night, and that nobody has gone out to ask him in." { }
  Rule ps_news_pell_held when newsHour() and (ps_held(party) or ps_flue_choked(party)) and not ps_burnt(post_office) and not carries(party, book_of_faces) and not ps_pell_free(party) and not ps_pell_fled(pell) and not ps_pell_chapel(pell) and not ps_pell_robbed(party) once
    says "Of Tomas Pell: the Burning did not come. He stood at Mistress Dunnage's elbow in front of a furnace that would not be lit, with the Crow on, and was seen, for the first time since he came, to smile, as a man does who has been reprieved from a thing he had arranged for himself. He is going to have to decide, now, and has not yet understood that it was only a day's delay he was given, and not the answer." { }
  Rule ps_news_pell_snatched when newsHour() and ps_snatched(party) and not ps_pell_free(party) once
    says "Of Tomas Pell: he watched it lifted out of the line at the fire by a masked stranger, and closed his eyes, and did not cry out. At the Chapel they say that a man in a clerk's coat came to the steps on the ninth night and asked to be heard, and was told that there was a bench." { }
  Rule ps_news_pell_chose when newsHour() and ps_burned_by_choice(party) and not ps_pell_free(party) and not ps_pell_fled(pell) and not ps_pell_chapel(pell) once
    says "Of Tomas Pell: he was told that the Book had gone into the furnace by a hand that was not the Rule's. He has not said whether it is better. He is at the counter, under another man's name, and his forms are square again, with the care of someone who has been spared a decision and does not know whether to be grateful." { }
  Rule ps_news_pell_fled when newsHour() and ps_pell_fled(pell) once
    says "Of Tomas Pell: he walked out of the Dead Letter Office on the day he was frightened, bare-faced, in the rain, and nobody on the Wet Post has seen him since. A man in a clerk's coat was taken across the Cuff on the Gull's ferry that evening, who paid in pennies, and would not say where to." { }
  Rule ps_news_pell_named when newsHour() and named(pell) once
    says "Of Tomas Pell: the Office has dismissed him, as Dacre, and the Chapel has taken him in, as Pell. He sits in the cloister with his name on him like a coat that does not fit, and is brought his dinner, and is not spoken to by the Bare Brothers, who have taken a vow, but is passed the salt." { }
  Rule ps_news_book_redeemed when newsHour() and ps_redeemed(party) and not ps_pell_free(party) once
    says "Of the Redemptions of the Dead Letter Office: the book for the year has one line in it, in the Postmaster's hand, which she shows to nobody. A parcel, grey, directed To Nobody, Nowhere. Redeemed. Pell, they say, was at the counter that morning and did not look up when it was done; and put his forms straight, for the first time in some days, as the Rule had put the thing straight for him." { }
  // Dunnage and the Burning.
  Rule ps_news_fire_done when newsHour() and ps_burnt(post_office) and not ps_held(party) and not ps_wet_done(party) once
    says "Of Mistress Dunnage: she burned the Nobodies at noon on the ninth day, or as near as the furnace would let her, by her own hand, in a dry furnace, and the Rule was kept. She went home at the Ninth Bell and sat in the dark with her taper, which she lit for the first time in a year, at the wrong fire, to see what it was like." { }
  Rule ps_news_fire_late when newsHour() and ps_burnt(post_office) and ps_wet_done(party) and not ps_held(party) once
    says "Of the Dead Letter Office's chimney: it drew at last, at six in the evening, after a brazier and a boy and a great deal of Mistress Dunnage's patience, and she burned the Nobodies by the Rule's own clause and not a minute before. It is the first time in forty-one Postmasters that the Burning has been late, and it is entered in the Office's book as 'by the Rule'." { }
  Rule ps_news_fire_stopped when newsHour() and ps_held(party) and not ps_dunnage_yielded(party) once
    says "Of the Nobodies: they stand in the burning-room still, forty sacks in the order of the rhyme, with a hundredweight of wet sacking in the flue above them, and Mr. Penn the sweep is to come on the tenth with his brushes. Mistress Dunnage has said nothing to anyone. She has been seen to stand in front of the furnace with her taper for a quarter of an hour, not using it." { }
  Rule ps_news_fire_asked when newsHour() and ps_dunnage_yielded(party) once
    says "Of the Nobodies: the Burning has been put off to the tenth, by the Postmaster's own hand, on a request she says she has never had. She has entered it in the Office's book in the margin, with a mark that the clerks cannot read and that is, Mabel Vickery thinks, a question." { }
  Rule ps_news_boy when newsHour() and ps_boy_dismissed(ps_corbin) once
    says "Of Dickon, the Office's boy sorter: he has been let go for a wet flue, and has been taken on by the bakehouse across the way, where he cannot read the sacks and is excellent with the buns. He says that Wick has promised to teach him the knot." { }
  Rule ps_news_boy_kept when newsHour() and ps_own_up(party) and not ps_boy_dismissed(ps_corbin) once
    says "Of Dickon: he keeps his place, and does not know why. He has asked Mr. Dacre, who has told him that sometimes the Rule does not say who may be wrong. He has written that on the inside of his Crow." { }
  // Mabel and the stair.
  Rule ps_news_mabel_redeems when newsHour() and ps_mabel_redeems(party) once
    says "Of the Dead Letter Office: the Redemptions has a new column. Mabel Vickery pays a penny a piece in the day, in the Office, as an agent, and signs; and the letters that mean something go out in the morning under the Postmaster's own seal, which has a crow on it. Mistress Dunnage has had the clause cut on a slate and hung it over the sorting-hall door." { }
  Rule ps_news_mabel_warrant when newsHour() and ps_mabel_warranted(party) once
    says "Of Mabel Vickery: she reads the Office's dead letters under the Warrant of the Watch, in the open, and has delivered eleven. The Warrant lapses with the Drawing. Mistress Dunnage has said that she will think of something by then, and has been seen to take down the Rule and read it standing up." { }
  Rule ps_news_mabel_kept when newsHour() and ps_mabel_kept(party) and not ps_mabel_redeems(party) and not ps_mabel_stopped(party) and not ps_mabel_warranted(party) once
    says "Of Mabel Vickery: she keeps her place, and has stopped doing it in the dark, mostly. The letters that mean something go into the satchel in the day now, under the nose of the Postmaster, who has learned to look the other way at the right moment. It is, Mabel says, the same crime done by a better-behaved criminal." { }
  Rule ps_news_mabel_stopped when newsHour() and ps_mabel_stopped(party) once
    says "Of Mabel Vickery: she sorts a hundred and ten pieces an hour and does not open any of them, and the Office has never been so quiet. She is reading, on her own time, a very long novel, and has been seen to cry at it. She has asked after the stair." { }
  Rule ps_news_mabel_told when newsHour() and ps_told_dunnage(party) once
    says "Of Mabel Vickery: she was dismissed on the seventh day, on the word of a stranger, and has taken a room over the road, and does not say whose word it was. She is taking in letters-to-be-written at the arcade, three a day, and reading all of them." { }
  Rule ps_news_mabel_clock when newsHour() and ps_mabel_dismissed(strake) and not ps_told_dunnage(party) and not ps_mabel_kept(party) once
    says "Of Mabel Vickery: she was dismissed on the seventh day, and has since been found by three households in the Drip, who say that a young woman with ink on her sleeves called at their doors with a letter and nothing to lose, and that they would like her to do it again." { }
  Rule ps_news_roke when newsHour() and ps_roke_done() once
    says "Of Aveline Roke: she has taken the ferry to Valmere to see whether the boat has been kept. It has. The oars are another matter, and are being discussed." { }
  Rule ps_news_roke_not when newsHour() and not ps_roke_done() and not ps_burn_done() once
    says "Of Aveline Roke: she keeps a kettle on the third landing, and does not know that there is a letter in a sack at the Dead Letter Office with her name on it, which will be ash by noon." { }
  Rule ps_news_roke_burnt when newsHour() and not ps_roke_done() and ps_burn_done() once
    says "Of Aveline Roke: there was a letter from her brother, in a sack of the Nobodies, which went in with the rest. She does not know. She sets two cups on the table in the evenings, out of a habit she cannot account for." { }
  Rule ps_news_wick when newsHour() and ps_wick_done() once
    says "Of Teodor Wick: he goes up the Wet Post by the front way now, past the late Master Corley's shop, and takes his hat off. He has bought the boy a pair of boots, and has been seen to put them on the boy's feet in the street, in public, in the rain." { }
  Rule ps_news_brandt_delivered when newsHour() and ps_brandt_delivered(party) once
    says "Of Lucia Brandt: she married Gerrit Hale at the Chapel on the eighth with a Watch domino in the front pew, and Hal Corry stood on the Post bridge at the Fifth Bell for an hour with his mouth open and said nothing to anybody. She is said to have sent him a loaf, by the common post, with no note. He has not been seen since." { }
  Rule ps_news_brandt_named when newsHour() and ps_hal_named(party) once
    says "Of Lucia Brandt: she was Named on the Post bridge on the eighth day, by a man in a Moth's half-mask whose letter nobody delivered, and married Gerrit Hale anyway, bare-faced, at the Chapel, with the whole of the Wet Post watching, and the Wet Post was not unkind. It is never unkind, about what it has already been told." { }
  // The Cockle's parcel and the Michaelmas bride.
  Rule ps_news_odile_night when newsHour() and ps_odile_night(party) once
    says "Of Odile Ollerton: she has not worn the dress, and has not burnt it. It lies in its tissue in a drawer over the bakehouse. On the ninth night she walked as far as the Post bridge in her Cockle with a loaf under her arm, and stood there until the Ninth Bell, for nobody, and Hobart Ollerton came out of the chandler's with a lamp and stood beside her, and did not ask." { }
  Rule ps_news_odile_day when newsHour() and ps_parcel_delivered(party) and not ps_odile_night(party) once
    says "Of the Cockle at the bakehouse with the left hand: a parcel has gone home under her coat. She has told nobody, and the bakehouse has asked nobody. Bram Cutter says she has been folding dough more slowly, and that he does not mind." { }
  Rule ps_news_odile_burnt when newsHour() and not ps_parcel_delivered(party) and ps_burn_done() and not ps_parcel_given(party) once
    says "Of the parcel on the Unclaimed shelf: it went into the furnace with the rest, with its direction to whoever wore the Cockle, and the clerk who fed it in said that it smelt of cedar. Nobody on the Wet Post knows that anything was sent." { }
  Rule ps_news_odile_named when newsHour() and ps_odile_ruined(party) once
    says "Of Odile Ollerton: Named, and nobody unkind about it. Hobart Ollerton opened the chandler's again on the third day. They are seen walking, in their Cockles, a foot apart, on the Wet Post, at the hour when nobody is looking." { }
  Rule ps_news_thanks when newsHour() and ps_thanks_delivered(party) once
    says "Of the letters to Nobody: they stand on a shelf in the Anonymous Saint's kitchen, by the ladle, a hundred and some, tied in tens, and nobody has been seen to read them. The soup is, by common consent, a little better." { }
}
