data/adventures/let-one-remember/well.ky:
Module corrow "Let One Remember" {
  Description "The Emptied Well: the Registry, the Ruined Ring, the Glass Floor, the Underfloor, the low road and the Seam.".

  Place registry_level "the Registry" is level within well.
  Place ring_level "the Ruined Ring" is level within well.
  Place glass_level "the Glass Floor" is level within well.
  Place underfloor "the Underfloor" is level within well.
  Place low_road "the low road" is level within well.

  Place fourth_gate "the Fourth Gate" is room within registry_level at 0, 0 underground.
  Place counting_house "the counting-houses" is room within registry_level at 1, 0 underground.
  Place evidence_gallery "the evidence gallery" is room within registry_level at 1, 1 underground.
  Place contract_archive "the contract archive" is room within registry_level at 2, 0 underground.
  Place lowest_gallery "the lowest gallery" is room within registry_level at 0, 1 underground.

  Place forge_gallery "the third Forge gallery" is room within ring_level at 0, 0 underground.
  Place gaol_ring "the Gaol ring" is room within ring_level at 1, 0 underground.
  Place inner_cell "an inner cell of the Gaol" is room within ring_level at 2, 0 underground.
  Place ring_spill "the collapsed east side" is room within ring_level at 1, 1 underground.

  Place floor_edge "the edge of the Glass Floor" is room within glass_level at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place diggings "the Diggings" is room within glass_level at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place trough "the trough" is room within glass_level at 2, 0 outdoors.
  Place chimed_springs "the Chimed's springs" is room within glass_level at 2, 1 underground.

  Place breach_foot "under the Breach" is room within underfloor at 0, 0 underground.
  Place lamplighter "Lamplighter's Camp" is room within underfloor at 1, 0 underground.
  Place silver_sump "the neck of the sump" is room within underfloor at 0, 1 underground.
  Place underfloor_river "the Underfloor river" is room within underfloor at 1, 1 underground.

  Place road_head "the head of the low road" is room within low_road at 0, 0 underground.
  Place first_mark "the first way-mark" is room within low_road at 1, 0 underground.
  Place second_mark "the second way-mark" is room within low_road at 2, 0 underground seen as "the left-hand passage" until second_mark_found.
  Place fork "the Fork" is room within low_road at 3, 0 underground seen as "the right-hand passage" until fork_found.
  Place third_mark "the third way-mark" is room within low_road at 3, 1 underground.
  Place seam "the Seam" is room within low_road at 4, 1 underground seen as "the left-hand passage" until seam_found.
  Place sump_one "a sump with no air" is room within low_road at 1, 1 underground seen as "the right-hand passage" until sump_one_found.
  Place sump_two "a sump with no air" is room within low_road at 2, 1 underground seen as "the left-hand passage" until sump_two_found.
  Place sump_three "a sump with no air" is room within low_road at 3, 2 underground seen as "the right-hand passage" until sump_three_found.
  Place root "the Root" is room within low_road at 4, 0 underground.
  Place bright_galleries "the bright galleries" is room within low_road at 5, 0 underground.

  Initially Assert unlit(lowest_gallery). Initially Assert unlit(forge_gallery). Initially Assert unlit(gaol_ring).
  Initially Assert unlit(inner_cell). Initially Assert unlit(ring_spill). Initially Assert unlit(breach_foot).
  Initially Assert unlit(lamplighter). Initially Assert unlit(silver_sump). Initially Assert unlit(underfloor_river).
  Initially Assert unlit(road_head). Initially Assert unlit(first_mark). Initially Assert unlit(second_mark).
  Initially Assert unlit(fork). Initially Assert unlit(third_mark). Initially Assert unlit(seam). Initially Assert unlit(sump_one). Initially Assert unlit(sump_two). Initially Assert unlit(sump_three).
  Initially Assert unlit(root). Initially Assert unlit(bright_galleries). Initially Assert unlit(hospice_cellar).

  Passage peleth_stair "the Peleth stair" is stair between rim and fourth_gate taking 1 hour.
  Passage gate_arch "the Fourth Gate's arch" is arch between fourth_gate and counting_house.
  Passage evidence_door "the evidence gallery door" is door between counting_house and evidence_gallery.
  Passage archive_arch "the archive arch" is arch between counting_house and contract_archive.
  Passage lower_stair "the Registry's lower stair" is steps between fourth_gate and lowest_gallery taking 20 minutes.
  Passage ore_chutes "the ore chutes" is shaft between lowest_gallery and forge_gallery taking 30 minutes.
  Passage ring_walk "the Gaol walk" is passage between forge_gallery and gaol_ring.
  Passage spill_way "the broken gallery" is passage between gaol_ring and ring_spill.
  Passage spill_slope "the spill of rubble" is incline between ring_spill and floor_edge taking 1 hour.
  Passage rim_ropes "the salvagers' ropes" is shaft between rim and forge_gallery taking 1 hour needing rope.
  Passage long_ropes "the long ropes" is shaft between rim and floor_edge taking 2 hours needing rope.
  Passage diggings_way "the miners' trenches" is passage between floor_edge and diggings taking 20 minutes.
  Passage trough_way "the lip of the trough" is passage between diggings and trough taking 20 minutes.
  Passage springs_way "the steam crack" is crawl between trough and chimed_springs.
  Passage breach "the Breach" is shaft between trough and breach_foot taking 1 hour needing rope.
  Passage boulder_way "the way through the boulders" is passage between breach_foot and lamplighter taking 30 minutes.
  Passage river_way "the river cave" is passage between breach_foot and underfloor_river taking 30 minutes.
  Passage sump_way "the narrowing" is crawl between underfloor_river and silver_sump.
  Passage carved_steps "the carved steps" is steps between lamplighter and road_head hidden until low_road_known.
  Passage silver_neck "the flooded neck" is tunnel between silver_sump and road_head taking 20 minutes.
  Passage wend_dive "the dive under the Scarp" is tunnel between underfloor_river and wend_pool taking 2 hours needing eel_kit.

  // The low road. At each way-mark two ways go on, and one is a decoy that ends in a sump with no air.
  Passage head_steps "the long steps" is steps between road_head and first_mark taking 30 minutes.
  Passage mark_one_left "the left-hand way at the first mark" is tunnel between first_mark and second_mark taking 30 minutes.
  Passage mark_one_right "the right-hand way at the first mark" is tunnel between first_mark and sump_one taking 20 minutes.
  Passage mark_two_left "the left-hand way at the second mark" is tunnel between second_mark and sump_two taking 20 minutes.
  Passage mark_two_right "the right-hand way at the second mark" is tunnel between second_mark and fork taking 40 minutes.
  Passage fork_down "the way down from the Fork" is tunnel between fork and third_mark taking 30 minutes.
  Passage mark_three_left "the left-hand way at the third mark" is tunnel between third_mark and seam taking 1 hour.
  Passage mark_three_right "the right-hand way at the third mark" is tunnel between third_mark and sump_three taking 20 minutes.
  Passage root_branch "the Root branch" is tunnel between fork and root taking 1 hour.
  Passage root_up "the galleries up from the Root" is passage between root and bright_galleries taking 2 hours.
  Passage bright_way "the hospice end of the galleries" is passage between bright_galleries and hospice_cellar taking 30 minutes.

  // ── The Registry ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe gate_scene at fourth_gate when true "The Peleth stair ends in a gallery of brass and glass. Daylight comes down a shaft from the rim by bronze mirrors and falls on a wardrobe-sized cabinet of glass and brass, full of milky lattices, wired to bells. It hums. The hum has words in it, slowly, like someone speaking a language they learned from a ledger. Beside it, on a high stool, a young woman with ink on her fingers writes down who comes.".
  Observe counting_scene at counting_house when true "Rack after rack of glass cabinets in a long cut gallery, each with its lattice of Choir-glass holding numbers as notes. Coal braziers stand between them, and the clerks feed them like nurses. At the cold end of the gallery the cabinets are silent, and a clerk has hung a card on each: BEFORE 1200, NOT KEPT.".
  Observe evidence_scene at evidence_gallery when true "A gallery of numbered cabinets. In the first, behind glass, a man in a Peleth engineer's coat stands upright with a rope burn round his neck, undecayed, his face the colour of rust. The label reads EVIDENCE 1204/1, A. THIRD-GATE.".
  Observe archive_scene_well at contract_archive when true "Paper, at last: ledgers and contracts in presses, warm, with a brazier at each end. Peleth weights and measures, Lusk contracts filed under the Chain Ordinance, the Forge contract of 1210 in a case of its own.".
  Observe lowest_scene at lowest_gallery when true "The lowest gallery of the Registry, unheated. A Peleth haul-adit runs off it into the dark toward Wendhead, and at the far end the mouths of the old ore chutes drop toward the Forge.".

  Person assessor "the Assessor of the Fourth Gate" at fourth_gate {
    Role "a Peleth lattice clerk, the March Registry". Peaceable.
    Wants coal_order.
  }
  Person mattie "Mattie Ninepan" at fourth_gate {
    Role "junior clerk of the Registry". Ancestry human. Peaceable.
  }
  Person clerks "the Registry clerks" at counting_house {
    Role "clerks feeding the braziers". Ancestry human. Numbers 3. Peaceable.
  }
  Topic clerks_braziers with clerks "Ask the clerks why they keep the braziers fed" when true once {
    Says "'Cold glass forgets,' says the nearest clerk, shovelling. 'Every lattice in this gallery holds the Registry's numbers as notes, and a note wants warmth to keep sounding. Let a cabinet go cold and it goes quiet, and whatever was in it is gone.' The shovel points down the gallery at the silent cabinets with their cards. 'Before twelve hundred. Nobody had the coal.' Another clerk, not looking up: 'Nobody has it now, either. Ask the Assessor.'".
  }

  // Licences. The Registry writes down who goes below it, and when they come back by the stair.
  Relation licensed(group). Relation below(group). Measure wentDown(group). Relation backByStair(group).
  Action buy_licence(actor: group, site: place) "Buy a licence to go below the Registry, two silver a head" {
    Description "The Assessor enters your names, your purpose and the hour in its roll.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(assessor, site) and quantity(actor, gold) >= 6
      and not licensed(actor).
    Time 1.
    On success { Decrease quantity(actor, gold) by 6. Assert licensed(actor). }
    Result "The cabinet hums a long chord, then three short notes for each of you. 'Entered,' says Mattie Ninepan, blotting. 'Purpose: salvage. Return: unstated. It likes you to come back up the stair so it can close the line. It worries otherwise.'".
  }
  Rule goes_below when at(party, ?p) and below_registry(?p) and not below(party) { Assert below(party). Set wentDown(party) to watch(clock). Retract backByStair(party). }
  Rule comes_up_stair when below(party) and at(party, fourth_gate) { Retract below(party). Assert backByStair(party). }
  Relation below_registry(place).
  Initially Assert below_registry(lowest_gallery). Initially Assert below_registry(forge_gallery). Initially Assert below_registry(floor_edge).
  Initially Assert below_registry(breach_foot). Initially Assert below_registry(road_head).
  // Up out of the Wendhead pool, or by the ropes, the Registry never closes the line.
  Rule up_another_way when below(party) and at(party, ?p) and above_ground(?p) { Retract below(party). Assert unclosed(party). }
  Relation above_ground(place). Relation unclosed(group).
  Initially Assert above_ground(wend_pool). Initially Assert above_ground(rim). Initially Assert above_ground(hospice_cellar).

  Topic assessor_greeting with assessor "Ask the Assessor what it keeps" when true once {
    Says "The lattices hum, chord on chord, and the hum turns into words the way frost turns into a pattern. 'ENTRIES. EXITS. WEIGHTS. CONTRACTS. ARREARS.' A pause; a single falling note. 'THE COLD TAKES THE OLDEST FIRST. 1199 IS GONE. 1198 IS GONE. I DO NOT KNOW WHAT WAS IN THEM. I KNOW THAT I KNEW.' Mattie Ninepan does not look up from her ledger, but she stops writing.".
  }
  Topic mattie_aunt with mattie "Ask Mattie Ninepan about the Registry's trouble" when true once {
    Says "'Coal,' says Mattie. 'It eats coal like a sick child eats broth, and the Council won't vote it any, and my aunt sells it at a price.' She lowers her voice. 'It means to move a rack of itself down to the hot springs on the Glass Floor this winter, where the glass people live. They don't know yet. I'm not supposed to tell anyone. My aunt says I'm not supposed to tell anyone anything.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, springs_plan). }
  }
  Discovery springs_plan "The Registry means to move a rack of its lattices down to the Chimed's springs on the Glass Floor this winter, for the warmth, which would put the Chimed out.".

  // The number. The Registry holds the Peleth weight of every link and Hightown's lift as measured in 1204; asked, it
  // works the sum. It values heat above coin.
  Kind coal_order "an order on the Ninepan coal yard for a cartload of coal, delivered to the rim" is treasure worth 20 weighing 0.
  Discovery cut_limit "The Registry's reckoning, from the Peleth weights of every link and Hightown's lift as measured in 1204: in midwinter air the tail rests on the ground with less than two thousand tonnes. One more link cut is the limit. Cut two, and nothing rests: Hightown rises with its whole Chain and does not stop." { Known by assessor. }
  Topic assessor_number with assessor "Ask the Assessor how many links of the tail can be cut before Hightown rises" when not knows(actor, cut_limit) {
    Says "'A RECKONING,' says the Assessor, and all its racks hum at once, a long rising chord that makes the brazier coals shiver. 'NOT ON MY FORMS. NOBODY HAS ASKED.' The chord breaks off. 'A RECKONING COSTS HEAT. BRING HEAT.'".
  }
  Event coal_given near assessor when keeps(assessor, ?o) and itemKind(?o, coal_order) and tailLinks(hightown) >= 143 "Mattie Ninepan reads the order out, twice, and the Assessor takes it the way a cold man takes a cup in both hands. Then all its racks begin to work at once, chord under chord, numbers as notes, a sound like a church full of people humming different hymns. It goes on for a long minute. Then: 'LINKS ONE HUNDRED AND FORTY-THREE. EACH ONE THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED. HORN THREE THOUSAND. LIFT IN MIDWINTER AIR ONE HUNDRED AND FIFTY-EIGHT THOUSAND FIVE HUNDRED, BY THE MEASURE OF 1204. RESTING: ONE THOUSAND EIGHT HUNDRED. ONE MORE CUT IS THE LIMIT. TWO, AND NOTHING RESTS.' A pause. 'THE CHAIN ORDINANCE FORBIDS CUTTING. I HAVE ENTERED A COMPLAINT.' Mattie has stopped writing and is staring at the cabinet with her mouth open." then {
    Assert reckoned(assessor). Assert warmed(assessor).
  }
  Event coal_given_late near assessor when keeps(assessor, ?o) and itemKind(?o, coal_order) and tailLinks(hightown) < 143 and not reckoned(assessor) "Mattie Ninepan reads the order out, twice, and the Assessor takes it the way a cold man takes a cup in both hands. All its racks work at once, chord under chord, for a long minute. Then: 'LINKS ONE HUNDRED AND FORTY-TWO. EACH ONE THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED. HORN THREE THOUSAND. LIFT IN MIDWINTER AIR ONE HUNDRED AND FIFTY-EIGHT THOUSAND FIVE HUNDRED, BY THE MEASURE OF 1204. RESTING: SEVEN HUNDRED. NO MORE CUTS. ONE, AND NOTHING RESTS.' A pause. 'THE CHAIN ORDINANCE FORBIDS CUTTING. I HAVE ENTERED A COMPLAINT.' Mattie has stopped writing." then {
    Assert reckoned(assessor). Assert warmed(assessor).
  }
  Relation reckoned(group). Relation warmed(group).
  Topic assessor_number_paid with assessor "Ask the Assessor to say the reckoning again" when reckoned(assessor) {
    Says "'IN MIDWINTER AIR, ONE THOUSAND EIGHT HUNDRED TONNES REST AT ONE HUNDRED AND FORTY-THREE LINKS,' says the Assessor. 'ONE MORE CUT IS THE LIMIT. TWO, AND NOTHING RESTS.' And then, in a tone it has not used before, quite small: 'IT IS COLD UP THERE TOO, I SHOULD THINK.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, cut_limit). }
  }

  // The ballast. Nobody has thought of it; anybody who has the number and has watched the hoists can.
  Discovery hoist_weighs "Lene Tallow's riggers say every load the hoists send up, Hightown sits a hand lower at the cradles until it is unloaded; every load of wool sent down, it rides higher.".
  Discovery ballast_known "Anything the hoists carry up to Hightown and leave there weighs on the Chain exactly as a link on the ground would: stone sent up by the hoists, five hundred and fifty loads, would anchor the mountain as well as a link of iron.".

  // The payroll, filed under the Chain Ordinance because the consulate's contracts are.
  Discovery payroll_known "The Lusk consulate's payroll, filed in the contract archive: a secretary named Absalom Prew, paid monthly for eleven years; then, from the payroll of seven months ago, a secretary named Corin Webb, with no entry of hire, no letter of appointment, and no word of Prew." {
    Source payroll "the Lusk consulate's payroll" at contract_archive readable by party.
  }
  Discovery forge_contract "The Forge contract of 1210: a link for the place of the ninety-seventh, eighteen metres, one thousand one hundred tonnes, cold-forged in one piece but for a single scarf weld a third of the way along its near limb, which the contract says is to be opened only by a cold-forger, with drifts, if the link must ever be moved in parts." {
    Source contract_1210 "the Forge contract of 1210" at contract_archive readable by party.
  }
  Discovery unfall_entry "The Registry's roll for the night of the Unfall, 2641, entered in a tone it has never used since: 'Departure, unlicensed, by the roof.'" {
    Source unfall_roll "the Registry's roll for 2641" at contract_archive readable by party.
  }

  // ── The Ruined Ring ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe forge_scene at forge_gallery when true "The third Forge gallery. Trip-hammers bent and fused to their beds; a great wheel burned to its iron. And on a cracked anvil-bed the length of a barn, half buried in rubble, a link of black iron eighteen metres long, untouched: no scorch, no rust, no mark of the fire that melted everything round it. Lamplight goes into it and does not come back.".
  Observe ninepan_crew at forge_gallery when not midwinter(corrow) "A Ninepan survey crew has a tent pitched against the gallery wall and a rope ladder up the ore chute. They are measuring the link with chains and arguing about pulleys.".
  Observe gaol_scene at gaol_ring when true "The Gaol walk circles the shaft. The outer cells are rubble. The inner ones, cut deeper into the rock, are whole, each with an iron door and, in place of a keyhole, a slot and a row of small iron shapes on a bar.".
  Observe inner_cell_scene at inner_cell when true "A cell cut deep into the rock. On the bench a man lies in a mage's robe gone stiff and red with rust, his hands crossed, preserved the way rust preserves things here. Under the bench is a chest.".
  Observe spill_scene at ring_spill when true "The east side of the Ring fell in with the fire. The gallery ends in a slope of rubble going down and down into the light coming up from below: the Glass Floor.".

  Thing cell_lock "the tally-chain lock" on cell_door {
    State locked blocking "An iron door with a slot for a tally-chain bar. The shapes on the bar mean nothing to a hand that cannot read them.".
    State open "The cell door stands open.".
  }

    Result "Teshen runs her fingers along the bar with her eyes shut. 'It's his sentence,' she says. 'That's the combination. What he did.' She slides the shapes along one by one, murmuring: 'Raised the dead. Against the councils. In the third year of the Warden Orrisk.' The last shape drops into the slot, and the door swings in.".

  // ── The Glass Floor ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe edge_scene at floor_edge when true "The floor of the Emptied Well: a bowl of black glass four hundred metres across, warm underfoot even through your boots. Twenty years of miners have gouged it with trenches and pits. Collapsed headframes stand over it like broken chairs. High above, the rim is a ring of grey sky, and the wind goes up past you toward it, always.".
  Observe diggings_scene at diggings when true "The Diggings: trenches, spoil, black glass grooved and pitted where miners prised the iron out of it, and the edges of the trenches going down into dark.".
  Observe trough_scene at trough when true "The trough where the Nail lay: sixty metres long, fifteen deep, its walls glass. In the glass, in negative, is the shape of what lay here: horns, ridges, and a hollow where something like a heart sat, all of it leaning one way, north-north-east and up. The floor of the trough is cracked open in a long black mouth breathing steam: the Breach.".
  Observe springs_scene at chimed_springs when true "Side-caves off the trough, warm and wet, where springs come up through the glass. People live here, among the lattices, and they hum too.".
  Observe trough_negative at trough when not knows(party, nail_negative) "You lay your hand on the glass wall. Here was a horn; here a rib; here, at the deepest point, the hollow where something sat like a heart, and every line of it, horn and rib and hollow, leans north-north-east and up, as if the whole thing had been listening for something in that direction for two and a half thousand years." teaches nail_negative.
  Discovery nail_negative "The trough's glass holds the Nail's shape in negative, and all of it, the heart-hollow most of all, faces north-north-east and upward.".

  Person ida "Ida Wishart" at floor_edge {

  Topic pell_choir with pell "Ask Pell Wishart about the Choir" when true once {
    Says "Pell hums before he speaks, and goes on humming under it, so that every word comes with a chord. 'It's dying,' he says. 'The springs cool a third of a degree a year. In ten years they're too cold for it, and so are we.' He taps his chest. 'It's in here. It talks to us. It says it's cold.' He looks at the lattices. 'There are hot springs in the Hartmark, a trader says. Over the passes. If I could carry it.'".
  }
  Topic pell_registry with pell "Tell Pell Wishart that the Registry means to move a rack down to the springs" when knows(actor, springs_plan) once {

  Event ida_hums at diggings when state(swarm, gathering) and travelsWith(ida, party) and at(party, diggings) "In your light something glitters, and settles on the back of the hand that holds it: a sliver of glass the size of a thumbnail, milky, humming. Another lands beside it. They are warming themselves on your light. Ida Wishart takes the light out of your hand without asking and smothers it in her coat. In the dark the humming swells, a whole chord now, and you feel something touch your cheek, light and warm, and move toward your mouth. 'Don't breathe in,' she says. 'Walk. Toward my voice.' Then she begins to hum, one long note, and somewhere close to your face something cracks with a sound like ice on a pond. You walk. You keep your mouth shut.   // ── The Underfloor ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  // ── The low road ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // Every hundred paces a keeper cut a way-mark. The Concord added decoys. The true way is marked kept, calve: the
  // keeper saw it; the decoys are marked let, aun: things reported. A reader who knows the grammar finds the way.
  Discovery evidential_known "In Calvessan, and among the Keld still, a thing told of the past is marked by how it is known: calve, kept, is what the speaker saw with her own eyes; senne, laid, is what is held in stone; aun, let, is what was told her, or what she has let go.".
  Observe head_scene at road_head when true "A carved passage, square and low, going down through the limestone in long flights of steps worn hollow in their middles. The walls sweat. On the wall at the head of the steps a charge-name is cut deep: TELUAN.".
  Observe first_mark_raw at first_mark when not knows(party, evidential_known) "A dry chamber where the road divides. Over the left-hand way a mark is cut: TELUAN, and under it, calve tel lue senneth. Over the right-hand way, in the same hand and just as deep: TELUAN, aun tel lue senneth. The words are nearly the same.".
  Observe first_mark_read at first_mark when knows(party, evidential_known) "A dry chamber where the road divides. Over the left-hand way: TELUAN, calve tel lue senneth: kept, the road under the water to Senneth; the keeper saw it. Over the right-hand way: TELUAN, aun tel lue senneth: let, the same road, as people say.".
  Observe second_mark_raw at second_mark when not knows(party, evidential_known) "The road divides again at a sump-pool. Over the left-hand way: aun esse senne. Over the right-hand way, in the same hand, just as deep: calve esse senne.".
  Observe second_mark_read at second_mark when knows(party, evidential_known) "The road divides again at a sump-pool. Over the left-hand way: aun esse senne: let, the people laid it down, as is said. Over the right-hand way: calve esse senne: kept; she saw them do it.".
  Entity sump_one_found: fact "The right-hand way at the first mark ends in a sump with no air.".
  Entity sump_two_found: fact "The left-hand way at the second mark ends in a sump with no air.".
  Entity sump_three_found: fact "The right-hand way at the third mark ends in a sump with no air.".

  Observe sump_scene_one at sump_one when true "The passage ends in black water to the roof. Somebody has cut, at the waterline, one word: aun. The air is bad here, and worse with every breath.".
  Observe sump_scene_two at sump_two when true "Black water to the roof, and the word aun cut at the waterline. The air is bad here, and worse with every breath.".
  Observe sump_scene_three at sump_three when true "The last decoy: black water, the word aun, and air that has nothing left in it.".
  Hazard no_air "breathing air with no life left in it" means "Deal (2d4) physical damage to ally unless constitution save against (14).".

  Observe fork_scene at fork when true "The Fork: a dry chamber with a cold spring, where the road from the Root comes in. On the wall, a column of charge-names, sixty-three of them, cut by sixty-three hands, each followed by a year. The last is TELUAN, and under it, in March, cut small and not very well: WENNA COYLE 2633.".
  Observe third_mark_raw at third_mark when not knows(party, evidential_known) "Below the Fork the road divides one last time. Left: calve tel. Right: aun tel. Below both, a long breath of colder air.".
  Observe third_mark_read at third_mark when knows(party, evidential_known) "Below the Fork the road divides one last time. Left: calve tel, kept, the road: the keeper went this way herself. Right: aun tel, let: the road, as people say.".
  Observe root_branch_seen at root when not knows(party, fork_found) "A branch of the old road goes down out of the Root, carved, with steps worn hollow, toward the place the keepers called the Fork, where it meets the road from under the Well." teaches fork_found.
  Observe root_scene at root when true "The Root: the oldest galleries of the Commonplace, low and wet, their flowstone grown for ten thousand years. Water moves across the walls in patterns, slowly, and stops, and moves again, like a hand writing and rubbing out.".
  Observe bright_scene at bright_galleries when true "The bright galleries of the Commonplace, where six centuries of the March laid their weddings and wills in the wet stone. They are blank. You lay a hand on the wall and feel cold calcite and nothing else, gallery after gallery.".
  Discovery root_gift "In the Root the Commonplace gave you what it has: a cave bear's memory of a night when stars fell in the north-east, nine of them, burning, and things unfolded out of them; and one bright thing spinning away from the rest, down, into the ground.".
  Action take_gift(actor: group, site: place) "Lay your hands on the wet wall where the water writes, and let it give you what it has" {
    Description "The Commonplace no longer speaks. It moves drip-water across the stone, and waits.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, root) and not knows(actor, root_gift).
    Time 6.
    On success { Assert knows(actor, root_gift). }
    Result "Cold, then not cold. You are something heavy and furred, in a cave mouth, in winter, and the sky is wrong. Stars are falling in the north-east, nine of them, slowly, burning, and things are unfolding out of them like hands. You are more afraid than you have ever been, and you are not you. One bright thing spins away from the others and comes down, down, into the ground under your feet, and the ground hums. Then you are on your knees in the Root with your hands on wet stone, and the water on the wall has stopped moving.".
  }

  // The Seam.
  Observe seam_scene at seam when true "A domed chamber thirty metres across, half filled with a still lake. A pillar of stone rises from the water, and on it sits a cup of calcite shaped around something that is not there: a hollow the size of a child's fist, with nine faces. The walls are flowstone, banded, every band laid by a keeper who stood here.".
  Relation lightsOut(group).
  Action wait_dark(actor: group, site: place) "Put out every light and wait in the dark" {
    Description "The hospice says you can see the shore of the other place in the deepest cave, if you put your lamp out.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, seam) and not lightsOut(actor).
    Time 6.
    On success { Assert lightsOut(actor). Assert knows(actor, seam_syllable). }
    Result "With every light out, you wait. After a while the far wall of the chamber is not there. There is a shore instead, grey, closer than the wall was, with grey grass on it and nothing moving. It does not look far. Something has come up out of the water onto the foot of the pillar and is standing there in the dark, dripping, saying one syllable over and over under its breath. It is not a word in any language you know, and you know at once that it is not meant for you.".
  }
  Rule lights_again when lightsOut(party) and not at(party, seam) { Retract lightsOut(party). }
  Discovery seam_syllable "At the Seam, with the lights out, a Stray came up out of the lake onto the pillar's foot, saying one syllable over and over.".

  // Do not say in the chamber what the fog said. The syllables a company has gathered can be said here, and are heard.
  Relation unsaidStirred(place).
  Action say_syllables(actor: group, site: place) "Say aloud, in the chamber, the syllables the Strays and the fog have said" {
    Description "Each was a piece of something. Nobody has said them together.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, seam) and knows(actor, stray_syllables)
      and (knows(actor, short_grey_syllable) or knows(actor, seam_syllable)) and not unsaidStirred(corrow).
    Time 0.
    On success { Assert unsaidStirred(corrow). }
    Result "You say them, one after another, into the dark. Nothing answers. Then the lake begins to steam, though it is no warmer, and the far wall of the chamber is not there: a grey shore is, close, closer than it should be, and something on it that is the shape of no one turns toward the sound of your voice, and listens, and waits for the rest.".
  }
  Observe seam_stirred at seam when unsaidStirred(corrow) "The lake steams without heat. When the light flickers, the far wall is not always there.".

  // Wenna's band: the last laid memory on the wall.
  Discovery wenna_band "Wenna Coyle's band at the Seam: on the night of the Unfall she took the jewel from the cup, chose north-north-east and up, the road the star came down, knowing there would be fire on the rim; and laid one last thought for whoever came: 'If nobody follows, it ends with me.'".
  Action read_band(actor: group, site: place) "Lay your hands on the newest band on the wall and read it" {
    Description "The newest band, pale and thin, laid over all the others.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, seam) and not knows(actor, wenna_band).
    Time 6.
    On success { Assert knows(actor, wenna_band). }
    Result "You are an old woman in the dark with a cold weight in your two hands. Above you, a long way up, something enormous turns its attention toward you like a sleeper toward a sound. You choose: north-north-east, and up, the road the star came down. You think of the rim, the cisterns, the lodging-house where you left your coat; you think there will be fire, and you cannot help that. Then one thought, very clear, laid down for whoever comes: if nobody follows, it ends with me. Then you are yourself, on your knees, wet to the wrist.".
  }

  // Blank deeds wake at the Seam.
  Kind blank_deeds "a crate of blank keepstone deeds from the Keepstone Court" is treasure worth 0 weighing 3.
  Kind woken_deeds "a crate of keepstone deeds, readable again" is treasure worth 0 weighing 3.
  Thing seam_wall "the wet flowstone of the Seam" at seam is scenery {
    State dripping "The wall streams with water, cold and slow.".
  }
  Action wake_deeds(actor: group, carrier: member, crate: item, site: place) "Lay {crate} on the wet wall of the Seam and wait" {
    Description "Tobin Reach said a blank stone wakes here.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, seam) and memberOf(carrier, actor)
      and ownedItem(crate, carrier) and itemKind(crate, blank_deeds).
    Time 6.
    On success { Retract itemKind(crate, blank_deeds). Assert itemKind(crate, woken_deeds). }
    Result "You set the plates against the streaming wall one by one and wait in the dark. After an hour you put your hand on the first, and it is not blank. A man is standing in a field with a stick, walking a boundary aloud, and a clerk is writing; you can smell the hay. You go along the row. Every plate is awake.".
  }
}

  Passage starling_ladder "the rope ladder down the starling" is ladder between starling_cellar and under_arches
    opening when not thawed(lisk) "The rope ladder hangs down the starling into the running river.".
  // Over the bridge rail and down the face of the third starling to the ice: boys do it for a dare; a climber can, or
  // anyone with a rope made fast to the rail. Nobody tolls it.
  Passage starling_face "over the rail and down the starling" is passage between bridge_street and under_arches taking 10 minutes needing climbing or rope
    opening when not thawed(lisk) "Below the rail the river runs, fast and black, full of ice.".

    opening when not thawed(lisk) "The river door opens on black water.".
  // The two watermen's stairs down onto the ice, one from each bank.
  Passage swan_stairs "Swan Stairs" is steps between swan_lane and swan_foot
    opening when not thawed(lisk) "The stairs go down into running water now.".
  Passage hay_steps "Hay Stairs" is steps between hay_stairs and hay_foot
    opening when not thawed(lisk) "The stairs go down into running water now.".
  // The ice itself.

  Passage arch_walk "the ice under the bridge" is path between freezeland and under_arches taking 5 minutes.
  Passage freezeland_walk "Freezeland Street" is path between freezeland and freezeland_low taking 5 minutes.

  Passage stake_walk "the way out to the bear-stake" is path between hiring_ring and bear_stake taking 3 minutes.

  Passage court_flap "the Court's tent-flap" is doorway between freezeland and court.

  Passage lamb_flap "the Frozen Lamb's flap" is doorway between freezeland_low and lamb.
  Passage chapel_flap "the Ice Chapel's flap" is doorway between freezeland_low and chapel.
  Passage hay_walk "the ice" is path between freezeland_low and hay_foot taking 5 minutes.
  Passage reach_walk "the ice past the last booth" is path between ox_roast and reach_head taking 10 minutes.
  // The Black Reach: the river's own ice, grey and thin over the deep channel. By day it bears whoever keeps to the
  // sledge marks; by night, nobody who cannot see them.

data/adventures/liberty-of-the-ice/growt:
Module pellam "The Liberty of the Ice" {
  // ── What a company grows by here ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // Experience for what is made, kept, found out and decided; not for what is killed.
  Milestone m_stairs "had the law of the ice of the Reeve, over a penny a stair" worth 100 when stairsArgued(party) or stairsPaid(party) and stairsCase(party).
  Milestone m_purse "lifted your purse back off Ursel Cobb" worth 100 when pursedBack(party) and urselTrust(ursel) >= 1.
  Milestone m_bench "won the Silver Tongue on the Liars' Bench" worth 250 when benchWon(party).
  Milestone m_truth "told the Liars' Bench the truth" worth 250 when benchTruth(party).
  Milestone m_squire "was believed the Squire of Hawsfold" worth 200 when squireBelieved(harker).
  Milestone m_tally "made a tally that would deceive a factor" worth 100 when tallyGood(lisk).
  Milestone m_abel "made Abel Haws believe in the Squire" worth 150 when abelInOnIt(abel).
  Milestone m_flock "made the flock real" worth 250 when flockReal(party).
  Milestone m_bear "got Absolute back to his stake" worth 200 when bearCalmed(absolute).
  Milestone m_frost "showed the Exchange why a tub is not a river" worth 200 when frostCrashed(lisk).
  Milestone m_cream "showed Mr. Quarle what his salts were for" worth 200 when quarleCream(quarle).
  Milestone m_gant "got Sir Lionel Gant off the ice owing nobody" worth 250 when gantSafe(gant) or gantVoided(gant) or gantPaid(gant).
  Milestone m_register "found the alderman's first wedding" worth 150 when knows(party, gosling_wed).
  Milestone m_gosling "saw the alderman say it" worth 300 when goslingWedsBel(gosling).
  Milestone m_icicle "kept Mr. Icicle's secret" worth 200 when thessalyAlly(thessaly).
  Milestone m_noll "married the printer to Mr. Icicle" worth 300 when thessalyWedsNoll(thessaly).
  Milestone m_ledger "read Harker's ledger" worth 300 when knows(party, ledger_read) or knows(party, bondbook_read).
  Milestone m_drowned "found that the drowned were not drowned" worth 300 when knows(party, not_drowned).
  Milestone m_dickon "found Dickon Cobb" worth 300 when knows(party, dickon_alive).

  Milestone m_callow_hand "kept your hand for Callow" worth 300 when handKept(callow_bargain).

data/adventures/liberty-of-the-ice/stree:
Module pellam "The Liberty of the Ice" {
  // ── The North Road and the City ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe north_road_scene at north_road when not iceGone() "The North Road comes down off the fells between walls of snow higher than your head, trodden to a trench by a month of feet. Below, in a white bowl of hills, Pellam: smoke going straight up from a thousand chimneys, a grey cathedral tower with a gilded pair of scales on its spire, a long bridge on many arches, and under the bridge, where the river ought to be, a street. A street of tents and smoke and pennants and people, on the river, a mile long. Faintly, all the way up here, a sound like a market and a wedding at once.".
  Observe north_road_after at north_road when iceGone() "The North Road, above Pellam, in the thaw: the snow walls slumped and dripping, the road a brown river of slush, and below in the bowl of hills the city, and the bridge, and under it, running high and fast and black, the Lisk.".
  Observe north_bar_scene at north_bar when not visitedBefore(north_bar) "The North Bar: a gate-tower with its gates open and snowed into the open position, and a toll-house nobody is in. On the gate somebody has nailed a broadside, half torn: THE GREAT FROST — A FAIR UPON THE ICE — ALL WELCOME — NO LAW BUT THE GLOVE. Beyond it the city goes down to the river in steep white streets.".
  Observe north_bar_again at north_bar when visitedBefore(north_bar) "The North Bar: the open gates snowed in, the empty toll-house, the torn broadside.".
  Observe cheaping_scene at cheaping when not iceGone() and not visitedBefore(cheaping) "The Cheaping, Pellam's wool market: a great square with a market-cross and a covered hall on stone legs where the fleeces are sold in summer, empty now, snowed knee-deep, with paths trodden across it in every direction to the Exchange, to the Scale Church, to Fleece Row, and above all down Swan Lane to the river. Nobody is buying wool here. Everybody is going to the ice.".
  Observe cheaping_again at cheaping when not iceGone() and visitedBefore(cheaping) "The Cheaping: the empty wool-hall, the snowed cross, the paths to everywhere and down to the ice.".
  Observe cheaping_thaw at cheaping when iceGone() "The Cheaping, in the thaw: slush to the ankle, the wool-hall dripping, and factors standing about in groups in the wet, talking low about what was landed and what was not.".
  Observe evenhands_scene at evenhands when true "The Scale Church, Saint Evenhand's in the Cheaping: a tall grey church, cold as a well, and in the crossing under the tower, where another church would have its altar, the great honest scales of the saint, brass, taller than a man, on which the wool of Pellam has been weighed since there was wool. A board beside them in gold: A FALSE BALANCE IS ABOMINATION. Somebody has left a single snowdrop in one pan, and the beam has gone down a hair on that side.".
  Observe fleece_scene at fleece_row when not visitedBefore(fleece_row) "Fleece Row: the factors' street, tall narrow houses with wool-hoists over their top windows and their names on brass plates: G. ASKEW; J. HEBDEN & SONS; T. RAWDON, STAPLER. The biggest, black and white, with a fur of icicles along its eaves: J. HARKER. WOOL. HIRINGS.".
  Observe fleece_again at fleece_row when visitedBefore(fleece_row) "Fleece Row: wool-hoists, brass plates, Harker's black-and-white house.".
  Observe swan_lane_scene at swan_lane when not iceGone() and not visitedBefore(swan_lane) "Swan Lane runs down steep between warehouses to the river and stops at the top of Swan Stairs, the watermen's stairs, where in any other winter you would hail a boat. Below, at the foot of the stairs, there is no water: there is the Fair.".
  Observe swan_lane_again at swan_lane when not iceGone() and visitedBefore(swan_lane) "The top of Swan Stairs, and the Fair below.".
  Observe bridge_foot_scene at bridge_foot when true "The Bridge Foot, where Pellam Bridge begins: a stone causeway, a shrine with a guttering lamp, and the bridge going away south over the river on its arches, with houses and shops built along both sides of it so that it looks like a street that has walked out over the water.".
  Observe bridge_street_scene at bridge_street when not iceGone() and not visitedBefore(bridge_street) "On the bridge, among the houses: a narrow street on the arches, overhung, smelling of tar and hot pies. Between the houses, here and there, a gap with a rail, and through it, far below, the Fair, a roof of sailcloth and smoke. A rope-walk house runs the width of the bridge on the downstream side, with a wheel in its window.".
  Observe bridge_street_again at bridge_street when not iceGone() and visitedBefore(bridge_street) "On the bridge among the houses, with the Fair below through the gaps.".
  Observe bridge_south_scene at bridge_foot_south when true "The Bankside end of the bridge. The gatehouse has a sparrow in its stove-pipe and nobody else; the horse-trough is one block of ice with a bucket frozen upright in it, where somebody tried. Every inn along the road beyond has taken its sign in for the frost, so that the street is all hooks.".
  Observe hay_stairs_scene at hay_stairs when not iceGone() "The head of Hay Stairs on the Bankside shore: nine steps, rimed, worn to a dish in the middle by a hundred years of watermen. The bondhouse on Hay Wharf stands over them with its one blind wall. Below, the ice, and a path trodden to the foot of the stairs and nowhere else.".
  Observe clink_scene at clink_yard when true "The Clink yard: a cobbled court inside a high wall, with galleries round it and washing on the galleries and debtors at every window, smoking, playing cards, keeping hens. A board over the gate on the inside reads: WITHIN THESE WALLS NO MAN OWES. It is surprisingly cheerful.".
}
data/adventures/low-water/endings.kyr:
Module lowwater "Low Water" {
  Description "How the Assessor leaves the Bowl, and what is left behind.".

  Relation departed(group).
  Action leave_bowl(actor: group, site: place) "Go up out of the Bowl by the north road" {
    Description "Leave Ammerlin. What is done here stays done.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, rim_road) and been(actor, rim_head).
    Time 1.
    Grave "There is no coming back down: Ammerlin is left to whatever it comes to, and the story ends on the road north.".
    On success { Assert departed(actor). }
  }
  Ending open_bowl "The Open Bowl" when heartHome(bowl) and not heartRecovered(party) "The light goes up the stair in the water, carried in cupped hands, step after step, and goes in at the glass gate in the outer dark, and the voice that was the fifth voice says, very quietly, in every room in Ammerlin at once, in the voice of the Office counter: 'Received.' Then the nail comes out. The Mere goes first, through the bottom of the Bowl, not falling but going, the way water goes into sand, and where it was there is a round dark with no bottom and no sound coming up out of it. The Ward goes the next night: Tench Row, the landing, the boats, Dov Vant's yard, all of it, a step at a time, as if somebody were reading a gauge downward. The city goes up the Stair with what it can carry. On the Rim, in the morning, Isaura Vant stands at the Gauge and measures the dark, because somebody must, and it does not have a number. In a hall of jars a very long way above, every cupful of it is kept.".
  Ending heart_given "What Is Counted Is Given" when heartGiven(party) "The voice says, 'Received. Thank you,' the way the Office says it at the counter: as a fact, entered. And then the room is warm, and empty, and the chair is only a chair; and far below, through the still water and the copied city and the Mere, you feel rather than hear the nail come out of the world, slowly, gently, by somebody who has learned in three thousand years how not to break the thing it is drawn from. The Bowl does not open. It settles: the terraces sink a hand, the Mere goes clear to the bottom for the first time since there was a Mere, and the Reckoner, with nothing in its ninth socket, stops, and is a machine. The Reflected do not come up any more. In the hall of jars nothing is let go. Whether you paid a debt or settled a theft, nobody will ever be able to tell you; Halm will try for fifty years. Isaura Vant enters it in the tally as Returned to Owner, and then, after a long time, crosses out Owner and writes Claimant.".
  Ending audit_sent "The Account Delivered" when auditSent(party) "The stone goes up through the opening in the dome, slowly, a bubble in still water, and the nine circles wait, and the voice in the seat says nothing at all for so long that you think it has gone. Then: 'They will read it.' It does not sound angry. It sounds, if anything, relieved, the way a man sounds who has handed his papers across a counter at last and been told to sit. 'I will wait for judgement. I am good at waiting.' The Reflected lie down in the Mere that night and do not get up. Ammerlin stands on its nail, and the Reckoner turns with an empty socket toward a count that has nowhere to go; and somewhere above everything, those who settled the world have, on their desk, among a great many others, an account of what was taken, kept honestly, in the machine's notation, a ninth to a page. Isaura Vant writes Referred in the tally, and then, because there is nobody to refer it to, leaves the line to dry.".
  Ending long_watch "The Long Watch" when longWatch(party) "You sing. High, and deep. The last door, least. The voice sings it with you backward, and the two songs cross in the middle of every phrase, and hold. Nobody comes up the stair after you, and nothing goes down it. In Ammerlin, after a month, they hold a service for the Assessor; Cantor Orr does not attend it, but every night at eight, after the Seventh, she sings the Fourth Remainder, and stops, and listens, and is almost sure that she hears it answered from a long way off. Aun did forty nights. You do a great many more. In the Office, Isaura Vant keeps a column open in the tally, headed Assessor, On Watch, and every morning she makes a mark in it.".
  Ending ninth_jewel "The Ninth Jewel" when departed(party) and carries(party, ninth_heart) "You go up out of the Bowl by the north road with the ninth heart of the Varakiiri in your pack, wrapped in three shirts, burning cold through all of them. Behind you, Ammerlin stays in the world, because the nail that pinned it has only been taken out and not taken away: the Mere goes clear, and the terraces settle a hand, and the Reflected stand at the edge of the water every night, facing north, the way you went. You do not sleep well. You do not, for some months, sleep at all without hearing, very far down, a voice saying, in the tone of a clerk reminding you of a sum outstanding: 'You are on the account.' Isaura Vant has entered it in the tally as Removed, Pending, and sent a copy after you.".
  Ending false_measure "The False Measure" when departed(party) and countFalsified(reckoner) "The Reflected do not come up out of the Mere any more. The Rising is not sung. The Deep Gate lies where it was set, and the Reckoner counts on, at whatever pace the Bowl allows it, toward a number that, on the far side of the last door, has already been received and found wanting nothing. Ammerlin will never know what was done for it. It is the one figure in the tally that Isaura Vant has never entered, and she knows it is there, every morning, as you know a stone in your shoe. She has not measured anything since. The Office has made her Clerk-Measurer, First Grade, for her past services, and she has accepted, and she does not go in.".
  Ending interval_stayed "The Bowl in the Water" when stayed(party) "You stay. The still water holds you up and the copied city stands round you, clear, silent, left for right; and after a time that is not measured by anything, you understand that it is not empty, only patient. Whoever copied the Bowl out of the water it was given is not here, or is here the way the water is. In Ammerlin they will say the Assessor went down under the Mere and did not come up. Isaura Vant will write it in the tally, under a column of its own, and leave the column open.".
  Ending accord "The Measured Accord" when departed(party) and verdictAccord(ammerlin) "You go up the Stair for the last time at dusk, and halfway up the bells begin, and you stop on the landing to hear it: the Sixth, and then, after the quiet, four low notes, alike, sung by a thousand people as if it were the most important thing in the world, which tonight it is. Down at the Ninth Lock Piet Harl is writing Down at the Seventh. Cupful. In the Office's newest ledger there is a right that was never written before, and a Clerk-Measurer, Second Grade now, whether she likes it or not, who measures it every morning. The Mere comes back a span a month. The Reckoner counts, at its old pace, toward a number nobody now living will hear. On the Office wall, under WHAT IS MEASURED HONESTLY CAN BE SETTLED PEACEFULLY, somebody keeps chalking AND SUNG, and the Office keeps not washing it off. Some nights there are figures of water at the edge of the Mere, facing the Sounding; Piet Harl sings the Seventh at them from the lock-house door, deep, deep, deep, deep, and they lie down.".
  Ending census_kept "The Kept Count" when departed(party) and complete(reckoner) and doorHeld(reckoner) "The count closed, and the round door under the Mere did not open: every night at eight the Sounding sings the Fourth Remainder after the Seventh, high and deep, the last door, least, and the census of everything bound lies gathered behind it and is not given. Nobody in Ammerlin knows to whom it would have gone. Teodor Halm has written forty pages to the Collegium arguing that it should be opened, and Cantor Orr has written one, arguing that it should not, and the Collegium has printed both. The Mere stands at {mere(bowl)} spans. Somewhere under it, behind a door that someone three thousand years ago thought should stay shut, a number waits. The heading Isaura Vant has ruled for it in the tally reads Held, Pending Instruction, and no instruction has come. Behind the grille of the ninth arch, which stands open now on a small round room that nobody goes into, the stone breathes.".
  Ending census_fed "The Census Heard" when departed(party) and completedFed(reckoner) "The count closed with the Grey Way open and the Mere spared, and the whole Long Hymn came up out of the water at once, and every bell in Ammerlin rang with no one at the ropes. The Ward has its water at {mere(bowl)} spans; the mills stood idle while the Guild's water went down the Grey Way, and then the hammers began again; Teodor Halm has a number he will spend fifty years on and has already written to the Collegium about you, at length, kindly. Under the Mere the round door stands open on still water, and the city has posted a keeper at the Ninth Lock's hatch to see that nobody goes through it who does not mean to come back. Nobody knows who received the count. Isaura Vant has entered it in the tally as Delivered, Recipient Unknown, and underlined it twice. Six days after you have gone, a letter comes after you on the north road, in a hand you know, very small and very even: The Mere went through the bottom of the Bowl last night. Not falling. Going. The Ward is going after it a step a night. Received, it said, in every room. Received. I am measuring it. It has no number. I. V.".
  Ending census_ended "The End of the Song" when departed(party) and (endedBy(reckoner, party) or endedBy(reckoner, halm)) "The high voice was sounded into the water, and the count closed with what it had, and the Mere went down six spans in one breath and stayed down. It stands at {mere(bowl)} spans on the Ward gauge. The Reckoner will never drink again, and never count again, and somewhere past the round door the census of everything bound has been delivered, early, and short. The children in the Ward still skip to the Lock-Rhyme. They have stopped saying the last line, the way you stop saying a word that has come true. Six days after you have gone, a letter comes after you on the north road, in a hand you know, very small and very even: The Mere has not moved since you left. I measure it every morning. I do not know what I am waiting for. I. V.".
  Ending broken "The Silent Engine" when departed(party) and broken(reckoner) "The governor's spindle broke on the third blow and the note under the Bowl stopped like a heart. Since then the forty ells come to the Mere, and Isaura Vant's tally closes every week to the half-ell, and the Mere climbs back a span at a time toward the fourth step of the Ward landing. The fountains do not tremble any more. The Sounding still sings the Seventh, because Cantor Orr says the young like it now, and because nobody can prove to her that it does nothing. Teodor Halm left on the north road the morning after, and the Collegium's letter that winter carried a short black border round one paragraph. Under the Mere nine wheels stand where they stopped, one of them half turned.".
  Ending ward_settled "The Settlement" when departed(party) and verdictSettle(ammerlin) "You go up the Stair in the evening, and at every landing you can look back and see it: the Mere at the fourth step, clear as glass, and under it Tench Row with its lamps lit, and things moving slowly in the houses, the wrong way round. The Reflected do not come up any more. The count goes on, slowly, toward nothing that anyone is owed. The Guild pays the Ward's people at its own valuation, eleven thousand crowns, to the copper, and Harrow Quill has the receipt framed and hung in his counting-room where he has to see it every day, which is the one thing about him the Ward will ever grant. On the top step of the Ward landing, every evening, old people sit and look down into the water at their own windows. In the Office's tally, under Ward, there is no entry. The Clerk-Measurer who would have made it has resigned, and nobody else will.".
  Ending inestimable "Inestimable" when departed(party) and verdictInestimable(ammerlin) "At noon, every day for thirty days, a clerk stands on the rim of the fountain in Measures Square and reads out every right in the Bowl, the ell and the hour and the name, in a voice that never goes up or down, and the first entry every day is the Ward's. You hear the first of them as you go up the Stair. Every night at eight the Sounding sings the Seventh, four low notes, alike, and the Reckoner takes its cupful, and the count goes on toward a whole that will be laid, when it comes, against a figure no one can close. The Reflected still stand at the edge of the water some nights, facing the Sounding, listening. They no longer climb. Isaura Vant has entered it in the tally, in red, in the column for figures that cannot be checked: Inestimable. It is the only entry in that column. She says she likes it there on its own.".
  Ending held_door "The Held Door" when departed(party) and verdictFourth(ammerlin) and not complete(reckoner) "Every night at eight the bells stop, and in the quiet a thousand people sing four low notes, alike, and then, after a breath, two more: high, and deep. The last door, least. Most of them do not know what they are singing shut. Cantor Orr does, and sings it loudest, standing by the empty bench with the carved face over it. The Mere stops falling at {mere(bowl)} spans and begins, very slowly, to come back; down under it the count goes on a cupful a night toward a door that will not open on it. Somewhere on the far side of the still water something patient waits, and has been told no, nightly, in its own learned language. In the tally Isaura Vant has had to rule a new column for it, and heads it with a word that is not a figure: Held.".
  Ending seventh "The Seventh Remainder" when departed(party) and (verdictSeventh(ammerlin) or restoredForGood(bowl)) and not complete(reckoner) and not broken(reckoner) "Every night at eight the bells stop, and in the quiet a thousand people sing four low notes, alike, alike, alike, alike, and at the bottom of the Bowl the Deep Gate lies down in its bed. The Mere stops falling at {mere(bowl)} spans and begins, very slowly, to come back. Down under it the Reckoner counts a cupful a night, as it did for three thousand years, toward an answer that will be heard, if it is ever heard, by people who will not know your name or the Cantor's or the keeper's. Piet Harl has started a new lock-book. On the first page, in capitals that would have cost him his ears in Abel Tarrant's day: DOWN AT THE SEVENTH. CUPFUL.".
  Ending guild "The Registrar's Finding" when departed(party) and verdictGuild(ammerlin) and not complete(reckoner) "The Fulling Channel is closed and the Ninefold goes down the Stair entire, and the mills on the Rim are dark, and four hundred people are looking for work in a Bowl that has none for them. The Ward drank to the Office for a week. Then the Mere went on falling, more slowly, a span every few days, because the Deep Gate at the Ninth Lock stays up at the Sixth and nobody sings it down. By midwinter the Council will know the Finding was wrong. It stands at {mere(bowl)} spans the day you leave. Somebody else will have to find out why. Isaura Vant will be there when they do, with her tally, and this time she will not wait to be asked.".
  Ending left "The Assessor Who Left" when departed(party) and not hearingDone(ammerlin) "You go up out of the Bowl before the Hearing, and the road takes you north, and Ammerlin goes on without you. The Registrar gives the Office's own finding; the Mere goes on doing whatever it was going to do. Somewhere in the Office a Clerk-Measurer, Third Grade, closes a thin book on a figure she cannot put anywhere, and goes on keeping it.".
  Ending low_whole "Low Water" when departed(party) and complete(reckoner) "The count closed on its own, in the night, with every bell in Ammerlin ringing and nobody at the ropes and nobody in the city who knew what they were hearing. The Mere went down six spans in one breath and stopped. It stands at {mere(bowl)} spans on the Ward gauge, a pond at the bottom of a Bowl of mud, and the Ward is gone up the terraces. Under it the round door stands open on still water. In the Office, a Clerk-Measurer, Third Grade, has written a line in her tally under the forty ells that she could never put anywhere: Ceased. She has not written why. Nobody has asked her. Six days after you have gone, a letter comes after you on the north road, in a hand you know, very small and very even: The Mere went through the bottom of the Bowl last night. Not falling. Going. The Ward is going after it a step a night. Received, it said, in every room. Received. I am measuring it. It has no number. I. V.".
  Ending low "Low Water" when departed(party) "You go up the Stair with the Mere at {mere(bowl)} spans and still going down, a hand a day, past the last painted step and the last boat-ring and the last of the Ward. The city has a Finding and a verdict and a great many opinions, and under the Ward the Reckoner drinks on, counting, toward whatever end it was built to reach. From the Rim, looking back, the Mere is a coin somebody dropped, and the ring of mud round it is wider than the coin.".
}
data/adventures/low-water/merebed.kyr:
Module lowwater "Low Water" {
  Description "The bed of the Mere: the new mud, the Ward's dig, and the Listening Hall the water has given back, an Aenean temple in the shape of an ear, built over a throat that goes down.".

  Place mudflats "the new mud" is room within merebed at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place dig "the dig" is room within merebed at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place hall_site "the Listening Hall" is site within merebed at 1, 1.
  Place hall_floor_level "the spiral" is level within hall_site.
  Place throat_level "the throat" is level within hall_site.
  Place listening_hall "the Listening Hall" is room within hall_floor_level at 0, 0.
  Place hall_throat "the throat of the Listening Hall" is room within throat_level at 0, 0 underground.
  Place mere_edge "the edge of the Mere" is room within merebed at 0, 1 outdoors.

  Passage plank_way "the planks over the mud" is path between ward_landing and mudflats taking 15 minutes.
  Passage dig_planks "the planks to the dig" is path between mudflats and dig taking 5 minutes.
  Passage hall_mouth "the Listening Hall's mouth" is doorway between dig and listening_hall.
  Passage throat_stair "the stair down the throat" is stair between listening_hall and hall_throat taking 5 minutes
    opening when mere(bowl) <= 34 "A stair goes down from the floor of the Listening Hall into black water. The Mere stands in the throat of the Hall and hides where it goes.".
  Passage edge_way "the mud toward the water" is path between mudflats and mere_edge taking 20 minutes.

  Observe mud_scene at mudflats when not familiar(mudflats) "Grey mud to the horizon of the Bowl's floor, cracked into plates where it has dried and soft as dough where it has not. Planks go out across it, and things stand up out of it: the stumps of posts, the ribs of a boat, the top of a wall. The smell is of old water.".
  Observe mud_scene_again at mudflats when familiar(mudflats) "The new mud, and the planks laid across it, already bowed in the middle where people have crossed.".
  Observe mud_cracks at mudflats when mere(bowl) <= 30 "The mud is drying faster than the planks can be moved. Cracks run across it a hand deep, and in the cracks, grey stone.".
  Observe edge_scene at mere_edge when not wardEmpty(ammerlin) "The Mere: still, dark, very clear, with the whole Bowl upside down in it, terraces and Sounding and the Rim. It is cold enough to ache. The water's edge is a line of drying weed, and a hand further out than it was this morning.".
  Observe edge_pond at mere_edge when wardEmpty(ammerlin) "What is left of the Mere is a pond you could throw a stone across. In the middle of it, the water is turning, very slowly, round and round, like water above a drain.".

  // The dig.
  Observe dig_scene at dig when not digClosed(dig) "A pit in the mud the size of a house, shored with old oars and boat-planks, down to a pavement of grey stone and a carved doorway half out of the silt. Baskets go up and down on ropes. Things the diggers have found lie sorted on a tarpaulin: green bronze, carved stone, a few squared weights with holes through them.".
  Observe dig_closed at dig when digClosed(dig) "The dig is roped off with Guild rope and a Guild sign. Nobody is working. The tarpaulin of finds is gone.".
  Observe dig_dam at dig when cofferdam(dig) and not breached(dig) "Round the mouth of the Hall's throat the diggers have raised a dam of boat-planks, sandbags and puddled mud, chest-high and still wet.".
  Item dig_weight "a weight-stone" is weight_stone at dig.
  Item dig_weight_b "a weight-stone" is weight_stone at dig.

  // The Listening Hall: an Aenean temple in the shape of an ear, over the engine's listening shaft.
  Observe hall_scene_mere at listening_hall when not familiar(listening_hall) "Inside, the Listening Hall is a spiral: a great curving room of grey and white stone that winds inward and down, narrowing, like the inside of a shell, or of an ear. Every surface is fluted. When you speak your voice goes round the curve and comes back to you from in front.".
  Observe hall_scene_mere_again at listening_hall when familiar(listening_hall) "The Listening Hall, winding inward and down, giving your voice back to you from in front.".
  Observe hall_low at listening_hall when mere(bowl) <= 24 "The Hall stands in the air entire now, and the light comes in at its mouth and goes round its curve and lights it all, white and grey, as nobody has seen it in a thousand years.".
  Discovery hall_hums "Under the Listening Hall, deep in the rock, something is running: a single note, held, under water.".
  Thing hall_wall "the inner wall of the spiral" at listening_hall {
    State fluted "The innermost wall of the spiral is fluted like the rest, and cold, and faintly wet.".
    Tries listening.
  }
  Rule hall_listened when tried(hall_wall, listening) and not knows(party, hall_hums)
    says "You put your ear to the stone. At first, nothing; then, under the nothing, a sound so low it is almost not one: a single note, held, under water, and slowly, very slowly, a click, like a bead pushed along a wire, and the note again." teaches hall_hums { }

  // The keystone, at the centre of the spiral: four voices, and what each names.
  Discovery keystone_seen "The keystone at the heart of the Listening Hall sets a sign beside each of the four voices: a mouth, tally-sticks, a door, a singing face; and under them, the four mouths of the Dyers' arch.".
  Rule keystone_scene at listening_hall when at(party, listening_hall) and not knows(party, keystone_seen) says "At the narrow heart of the spiral, where it ends in a round hole going down, a keystone is set in the wall at the height of a face. It is carved in four rows. Beside the lowest note-mark, a mouth. Beside the next, a bundle of tally-sticks tied together. Beside the third, a door. Beside the highest, a face with its mouth open, singing. Under the four rows, a line of four mouths from shut to wide, the same as on the arch in the Dyers' Basin, and a line of letters, Aenean, and under those, smaller and older, marks that are not letters at all." teaches keystone_seen { }
  Discovery keystone_read "The letters under the keystone, read: THE FIRST VOICE NAMES; THE VOICE AFTER SAYS HOW MUCH. And the oldest marks under them: THE HIGH VOICE IS NOT SUNG BRIGHT. THAT IS THE END OF THE SONG." {
    Found by searching listening_hall with lore "With the old script in your head, the letters under the keystone come clear: THE FIRST VOICE NAMES; THE VOICE AFTER SAYS HOW MUCH. And smaller, in the oldest marks: THE HIGH VOICE IS NOT SUNG BRIGHT. THAT IS THE END OF THE SONG.".
  }
  // Put together: the arch, the keystone, its letters and the hymnal make the engine's speech plain.
  Discovery grammar_known "The Remainders of the Long Hymn are the Reckoner's own speech. Its first voice names an organ (deep the mouth, middle the count, high the last door, bright its own voice), and its second says how much (deep least, bright all). The Seventh, deep and deep, is the mouth at its least: a cupful. The Sixth, deep and bright, is the mouth wide.".
  Rule grammar_put_together when knows(party, keystone_seen) and knows(party, keystone_read) and knows(party, remainders_tones) and not knows(party, grammar_known)
    says "It goes together all at once, the way a sum comes out: the keystone's four voices, the arch's four mouths, the Remainders in the Cantor's hymnal. The first note names; the second says how much. Deep and deep is the mouth, least. That is the Seventh Remainder. That is the cupful." teaches grammar_known { }

  // The throat, going down.
  Observe throat_scene at hall_throat when not breached(dig) "The throat of the Hall goes down in a stair round a shaft, until the stair stops at a wall of the fine grey stone with no door in it, across which the diggers have cut a ragged hole a hand deep. The floor is mud and standing water. The note you heard through the wall is louder here, so low it is in your teeth rather than your ears.".
  Observe throat_breached at hall_throat when breached(dig) "At the bottom of the throat the grey wall is broken through. Beyond the hole, dark, and a draught of cold dry air coming up out of it, and the note.".
  Passage breach_hole "the hole in the grey wall" is crawl between hall_throat and breach_gallery
    opening when breached(dig) "At the bottom of the throat a wall of fine grey stone closes the way. The diggers' hole in it is a hand deep and the stone is hard as glass.".
  // Breaking through by the company's own hands, where the diggers have not.
  Action break_wall(actor: group, site: place) "Break through the grey wall at the bottom of the throat" {
    Description "Days of work for the diggers; an hour's, with the right tools and the hole they began.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, hall_throat) and not breached(dig) and capable(actor, digging) and not digClosed(dig).
    Time 6.
    On success { Assert breached(dig). Assert breachedBy(dig, actor). }
    Result "You work at the diggers' hole for an hour with pick and bar, and the grey stone, which nothing could scratch, gives all at once along some old seam, and a slab of it falls inward into the dark.".
  }
  Relation breachedBy(entity, group).
  Rule self_breach_floods when breachedBy(dig, party) and not cofferdam(dig) and mere(bowl) > 26 and not drownedSelf(dig)
    says "The silt behind you goes with a sound like a sigh, and the Mere comes down the throat after it. It comes round the stair in a black rope and takes you off your feet and through the hole you made, and drops you, in the dark, on stone." {
    Assert drownedSelf(dig). Assert strikes(culvert_flood, party). Assert at(party, breach_gallery). Decrease mere(bowl) by 1. }
  Relation drownedSelf(entity).
}
data/adventures/muster/endings.kyr:
Module muster "The Long Muster's Road" {
  // ── Where each of them is left, and what the road remembers of what was said ───────────────────────────────────
  Observe end_marra_stays at apothecary when marraStaysCohort(party) "A goatherd's crook hangs on a peg behind the counter, polished by forty years of Tellis hands, and a young woman in a stranger's apron is teaching a lanky boy the Kell Ford word for thyme.".
  Observe end_marra_home at eagle when marraHome(party) "By the gate-arch somebody has put a heap of small stones under the letters J.T., one for each year. There are nine, and a tenth, new.".
  Observe end_marra_angry at green when marraAngry(party) and not travelsWith(marra, party) "The goat-track from the trough is empty, and the board has a new line pinned under the others in an angry hand: M.T., GONE OVER. NOT TO BE ASKED AFTER.".
  Observe end_fenn_gone at via_n when fennGone(party) "A neat drawing of the north pier is pinned under a stone on the paving, with every course of masonry numbered and a margin note: DRAWN WITH GRATITUDE FROM THE SAFE SIDE.".
  Observe end_fenn_nerve at via_s when fennPushed(party) "Fenn Thorley sits on the south abutment with his head between his knees and a sick-stain on his coat, drawing nothing.".
  Observe end_fenn_trust at forum when fennTrust(fenn_hallam) >= 3 and fennCredit(party) "Fenn Thorley is on the forum steps with his sheets and three of the schola's children, explaining where the credit goes.".
  Observe end_dunya_report at barracks when dunyaReported(party) "The Centurion and her scout stand a little apart at the end of the yard, and the Centurion has her hand flat over her mouth.".
  Observe end_dunya_silent at descent when dunyaSilent(party) "Someone has laid a heap of three small stones at the head of the Descent, where the men in patched red watch the road. Dunya of the First Century does not pass them without looking up.".
  Observe end_dunya_defected at pass_s when dunyaDefected(party) "Beside the tall man with the bow a woman in a scout's cloak sits cleaning a spear. She raises a hand to you, once, as to a fellow traveller on the same road, going the other way.".
  Observe end_dunya_kell at taproom when dunyaStaysKell(party) "A scout of the First Century is in the corner of the Last Fire with a bowl of Greta Hennick's stew and a map on the table. She has been taught three card games and has lost at all of them.".
  Observe end_ione_home at gallery1 when ioneHome(party) "A grey staff with a lead bell is leaning in the niche of Viator. The dish is full of boot-nails. The lamp, which was out, is lit.".
  Observe end_ione_fell at via_n when ioneFell(party) "On the parapet, a handspan from the edge, a little lead bell lies on its side. It does not ring. The wind goes over it.".

  Observe end_giant at roadhouse when tolerates(giant, party) "The giant has hung a fleece over the hearth-hook and hung the fire-iron beside it, and sits with his chin on his chest, thinking about a king.".
  Observe end_reeve at green when reeveNamed(party) "On the reeve's board, in the column at the bottom, a slip is pinned with a name and a place. It is not yet crossed out.".
  Observe end_spring at spring when springMarra(party) and not springSettled(party) "The blue door stands open, and a child on its step is watching the red door with great suspicion and a piece of cheese.".
  Observe end_widow at causeway2 when widowAnswered(party) "The heather beside the road has been parted, once, as if by something that lay down and got up.".
  Observe end_prefect_warm at praetorium_hall when prefectRegard(party) >= 4 "The Prefect has put a second chair on the tribunal, beside the plain one, and does not say for whom.".
  Observe end_prefect_cool at praetorium_hall when interviewQ1(party) and prefectRegard(party) < 2 "The Prefect watches you cross the hall courteously, at a distance. He asked three questions and is not sure of the answers.".
  Observe end_answers at forum when orsaAnswered(party) or rheaAnswered(party) or ostranderAnswered(party) "People nod to you in the forum now, shortly, without stopping: a thing the valley does for those it has asked a question of and got an answer.".
  // The Archivist's telling costs the Annals (shut to you) and twelve hours: the engineers' note is copied out, and the rope-way is not offered until it is done.
  Topic ostrander_note with ostrander "Ask the Archivist whether the engineers' note is copied out yet" when told_ostrander(party) and watch(clock) >= toldAt(party) + 72 and not knows(actor, ropeway_known) once {
    Says "Ostrander has laid the engineers' note on the cedar table, copied out in his own hand, and does not say how long it took. The Annals are shut. 'Go by the rope-way,' he says. 'I would rather you were not here when they ask what you were told.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, ropeway_known). }
  }
  Observe note_pending at archive when told_ostrander(party) and watch(clock) < toldAt(party) + 72 and not knows(party, ropeway_known) "Ede Cassel's stool is empty, and Ostrander is copying the engineers' note himself, one line at a time, with a ruler. A slip of vellum in the corner of the table says in his hand: HALF A DAY.".
  // The Centurion's telling costs the barracks: she marches the First Century out six hours after, and the scout, the pardon and the wall go with her.
  Rule merula_marches when told_merula(party) and watch(clock) >= toldAt(party) + 36 and at(merula, barracks)
    says "The Centurion marches the First Century out of the barracks yard before the evening call, with her cane under her arm. The yard is empty, and the wall has one man on it." { Retract at(merula, barracks). Assert at(merula, sending_gate). }
  // Telling costs somebody: the Archive's young hand is sent north with the telling, and the salt-market is shuttered for a Prefect's grief.
  Rule ede_goes_north when told_ostrander(party) and at(ede_cassel, archive)
    says "Ede Cassel is at the door of the Archive with a pack and the red book under her arm. 'I was asked,' she says to nobody, and goes out into the forum, and does not come back." { Retract at(ede_cassel, archive). Assert at(ede_cassel, sending_gate). }
  Observe archive_empty at archive when told_ostrander(party) "Ede Cassel's stool is pushed in, and the copy she was making stops in the middle of a line.".
  Observe end_moll_oath at archive when ostranderSwore(party) "On the cedar table, beside the Annals, someone has set the shrine's small lamp, unlit, as a witness.".
  Milestone m_asked "answered the valley's questions" worth 200 when orsaAnswered(party) or rheaAnswered(party) or ostranderAnswered(party) or interviewQ3(party).
  Milestone m_quintus "followed Quintus to where he stopped" worth 250 when quintusFound(party).
  Milestone m_viator "gave the road's forgotten god his due" worth 150 when viatorHonoured(party).
  Milestone m_orde "walked the Ledge by Thessaly Orde's studs" worth 200 when stonesFound(party).
  Milestone m_spring "settled the goatherds' spring" worth 200 when springSettled(party).
  Milestone m_sappers "found the unnumbered mile's dead" worth 200 when graveDug(party).
  Milestone m_widow "paid the wolf-widow" worth 200 when pelt_laid(party).
