And in a row along the south wall, four beds that are black: burned, the earth gone to ash, with the stubs of words sticking up out of it like the stumps of a hedge.".
  Observe orme_restored at orme_garden when ormeRestored(physick) "A walled garden of square beds whose plants are writing; and along the south wall four beds that were ash, three of them green again with new script, calamus and horehound and the honey of the bog-myrtle, and the fourth bed raked and bare, as a gardener keeps a bed ready.".
  Relation ormeRestored(group).
  Observe foxing_edge_scene at foxing_edge when true "Beyond the ellipsis the paper changes colour. It goes from white to cream to the yellow of an old newspaper, and then there are spots on it, small and brown, like the spots on the back of an old hand, and then the spots run together. Everything here is quieter. The beams are very few.".
  Observe foxing_deep_scene at foxing_deep when true "The deep Foxing is brown, all of it, ground and air, and soft underfoot, like walking on an old map. There are books here, if you look: lying about like stones in a field, half sunk in the brown, their titles worn off. Some of them are still trying to say something. You catch a few words: and the moorings of the Fourth Lock; and in the year of the great; and a list of names of somebody's children that peters out at the third. These are the books Calamy stopped reading.".
  Discovery foxing_seen "In the Commonplace, the books that Calamy has stopped reading are fading: foxing, going brown, losing their words one sentence at a time. The Reading Due was what kept them.".
  Observe foxing_learned at foxing_deep when true "A half-sunk book at your feet says, quite clearly, 'and the children of Agnes Hurd were Thomas, Bel, and,' and then cannot remember the third." teaches foxing_seen.
  Observe wellhead_scene at wellhead when true "At the end of the parenthesis a spring rises out of the paper: not water but ink, black and bright, welling up in a round stone basin and spilling over the lip and running away in every direction in little black streams that are, when you look closely, lines of writing, going off to become something. This is where things are first written. The air smells of oak-gall and of rain. In the basin, under the surface, old letters turn over slowly, as stones turn in a stream, and come up, and go down again.".
  Discovery wellhead_read "At the Wellhead, the first words ever written in Calamy still turn over in the ink: WE ASK TO SLEEP. LET US GO HOME AND COME WHEN WE ARE CALLED. AND LET NONE BURN US BUT AS WE CONSENT. THE BOOKS OF CALAMY, TO AMBERY THE BINDER. The Colophon was the books' petition before it was the city's bargain.".
  Thing first_words "the first words" at wellhead {
    State turning "The first words wait in the basin to be read, if anyone will lean over and look.".
  }
  Observe first_read at wellhead of first_words as reading when tried(first_words, looking) "You lean over the basin and wait, and the old letters come up, one line after another, and go down again, and come up: WE ASK TO SLEEP. LET US GO HOME AND COME WHEN WE ARE CALLED. AND LET NONE BURN US BUT AS WE CONSENT. THE BOOKS OF CALAMY, TO AMBERY THE BINDER. And then a long line of small marks, each different, under it, that you understand after a while are signatures, hundreds of them, the marks of every book that was written in Calamy in its first year, every one of which signed." teaches wellhead_read.
  Observe vask_foot_scene at vask_foot when true "At the end of the black-letter road a tower stands up out of the paper, black, narrow, windowless, its stones cut with letters so heavy and ornate they are hard to read and harder to look at. Three great chains come out of its top and go away across the sky in three directions, taut, humming.".
  Observe vask_top_scene at vask_top when not lexiconFreed(lexicon) "The top of the tower is a single round room with no roof, and in the middle of it, held off the floor by three chains that run from its spine to the three corners of the sky, hangs the Lexicon: a book as big as a door, bound in something dark, open, its pages turning by themselves slowly, as if it were looking for something.".
  Observe vask_top_freed at vask_top when lexiconFreed(lexicon) "The top of the tower is empty. Three cut chains hang slack from the corners of the sky.".
  Observe chamber_scene at chamber when true "A chamber with no walls and no roof, open to the beams, and its floor is the Great Roll of Pleas: unrolled, enormous, a road of old yellow skin a hundred paces wide covered in crabbed writing and red capitals, going away in both directions further than you can see. Down its middle runs a line of seats, each different: a high-backed chair, a little stool, a slab of black stone with three ring-bolts in it, a bed of herbs, a doorstep, a heap of loose pages. In front of the seats, set into the floor of the Roll itself, a long brass plate engraved THE ORDER PAPER.".

  // Who comes, and how they are received: entered by the Catalogue, or brought through a door that is not on the books.
  Relation entered(group). Relation sponsored(group). Relation correctedEntry(group).
  Query standing(a: group) means (entered(a) or sponsored(a)) and not misnamed(a).
  Relation misnamed(group).
  Person catalogue "the Catalogue of the Founders" at reading_room {
    Role "a cliff of little drawers, and a voice". Peaceable. Pronouns it. Manner stoic.
    Greets "'Reader,' says the voice from the drawers, all of them at once. A card flutters down from very high up, considers you, and flies up again. 'State your business. Do not pull out any drawers. They are in order.'".
  }
  Rule entered_by_reading when arrivedByReading(party) and at(party, reading_room) and not entered(party)
    says "A great many index cards come down out of the light round you like snow and settle on your shoulders and hands and hair, and are written on, and fly up again. 'Entered,' says a dry voice from everywhere. 'A reader, of Calamy, by the Founders' door. On the books.'" {
    Assert entered(party). }
  Item shelfmark "your shelfmark" is shelfmark_kind at reading_room hidden until shelfmark_given.
  Discovery shelfmark_given "The Catalogue has given you a shelfmark: you are on its books, a reader of Calamy, with standing before the Parliament of the Bound.".
  Rule shelfmark_issued when entered(party) and at(party, reading_room) and not knows(party, shelfmark_given) says "A card comes down and stays down: your shelfmark." teaches shelfmark_given { }
  // The Errata: corrections, given form, who find what is not on the books and set it right.
  Person errata "the Errata" at reading_room {
    Role "corrections, in red ink, three of them". Species erratum_kind. Level 1. Numbers 3. Peaceable.
    Warns "Three small red figures come out from among the stalls, sharp as pen-nibs, and stand in your way. 'Unentered,' says the first. 'Not on the books,' says the second. 'Correct,' says the third, and they all three raise their nibs.".
    Comes "The Errata come at you to correct you.".
    Pleads "The Errata blot, and run, and are gone into the stalls, leaving red smears on the paper.".
  }
  Relation erratiBeaten(group). Relation errataSent(group).
  Rule errata_find when at(party, remainder_market) and not standing(party) and not errataSent(errata) and not crakeWith(party) {
    Assert at(errata, remainder_market). Retract peaceable(errata). Assert errataSent(errata). }
  Query crakeWith(a: group) means travelsWith(crake, a).
  Action be_corrected(actor: group, site: place) "Let the Errata take you to be entered" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(errata, site) and not standing(actor) and not peaceable(errata).
    Time 3.
    On success { Assert entered(actor). Assert correctedEntry(actor). Assert at(actor, reading_room). Assert peaceable(errata). Assert at(errata, reading_room). }
    Result "The three small red figures take you by the sleeves, not roughly, and walk you back along the long sentence, clause after clause, to the reading room, and stand you in front of the drawers. 'Brought,' says the first. 'By the back,' says the second. 'Entered,' says the Catalogue at last, dryly, 'by the back. Noted.' A card comes down with your name on it, and in the corner, small, in red: CORR.".
  }
  Rule errata_beaten when routed(errata) and not erratiBeaten(party) says "The Errata blot and run. Somewhere among the stalls a stall-keeper laughs." { Assert erratiBeaten(party). Assert peaceable(errata). Assert at(errata, reading_room). }

  // The Remainder Market, where the price of anything is a reading.
  Person remainderman "the Remainderman" at remainder_market {
    Role "a broker of unsold books, himself a book of trade tables". Peaceable. Pronouns he. Manner jovial.
    Greets "A stout ledger in a waistcoat, with a pencil behind where his ear would be, spreads his covers. 'A reader! Alive! Welcome, welcome to the Remainder Market. Everything you see is for sale, and everything is priced in readings: a page aloud, an hour aloud, the whole thing aloud to the end. Some of my stock hasn't been read since the Fallow campus went under the sea.'".
  }
  Topic remainderman_trade with remainderman "Ask the Remainderman what is bought and sold here" when true once {
    Says "'Attention,' says the Remainderman. 'What else? Out here a book lives by being read, and a living reader is the richest thing that walks. One of you, reading aloud for an hour, is worth more to a remaindered quarto than a year in a good library.' He taps a stall. 'The Unwritten pay in what they have, which is promises. The Bound pay in news of home. And Crake,' he adds, 'pays in bodies, which is why everybody here loves him and nobody trusts him.'".
  }
  Topic remainderman_crake with remainderman "Ask the Remainderman about Absalom Crake" when true once {
    Says "'Crake keeps the door,' says the Remainderman. 'The only door from your city to ours that isn't the Founders'. Books that were never written come to him with a promise, and he has them copied out fair by a man of his who can write in any hand, and then they have a body, and they walk out of his shop into your city, and get bought.' He shrugs, which in a ledger is a ripple of pages. 'And sometimes your books walk in at his door the other way. A whole library, not long ago. Eleven hundred, asking the way. They went on to the Draft-Fields; the Canto took them in.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, collection_emigrated). }
  }
  Relation readAloudHere(group).
  Action read_for_stall(actor: group, site: place) "Read aloud for an hour to a remaindered book that has not been read in a century" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, remainder_market) and not readAloudHere(actor).
    Time 6.
    On success { Assert readAloudHere(actor). Assert readToSomeone(actor). }
    Result "The Remainderman finds you a book called A History of the Fallow Campus, Volume the Seventh, which nobody has read since the Fallow campus went into the sea, and you sit on an upturned crate and read it aloud for an hour: the lecture halls, the salt in the library, the night the sea came in, the Provost who refused to leave. Stall-keepers stop to listen. When you finish, the book says, in a voice like wet sand drying, 'Thank you. I had forgotten how the eighth chapter went.' A beam of light comes down on it from nowhere, faint, and stays.".
  }
}
data/adventures/parliament-of-books/endi:
Module calamy "A Parliament of Books" {
  Description "How the book closes, for a Calamy played on its own: the morning after the Kindling.".

  Query morningAfter() means kindlingDone(ashpit) and day(clock) >= 10 and hour(clock) >= 8.
  Ending ashen "The Year of Ash" when morningAfter() and ashYear() "The smoke of the Kindling lay over Calamy all night and went into the houses. Three thousand almanacks went down to the Cinderfield without their leave, and the Index had its regiments, and came up the smoke. Nothing is burned in Calamy now; nothing needs to be. Every night a little more is cut, very cleanly: a line from a will, a verse from the rhyme, a name from a gravestone, the Sixth Plea. The books do not speak any more. Neither, much, do the people. In a year, the Index says from every page that is left, it will be quiet, and every page in it will say exactly what it said the day before.".
  Ending unsewn "The Year of Voices" when morningAfter() and unsewing() and not ashYear() "Calamy wakes to its books awake. Every Housebook on every dresser, every will in every lawyer's press, the Great Roll in its Court, the Life of Ambery on its heron, the bestiary in the bond: all of them, at once, in their bodies, talking. The Second Canto walks down Gutter Lane in pencil at noon and nobody stops it. It will be a long year, and a loud one, and nobody alive knows how the first one ended. Somewhere in the city a binder sits down at a frame and begins, slowly, to Sew, for anyone who asks.".
  Ending recalled "The Recall" when morningAfter() and recall() and sealed(door_shut) "The books of Calamy are asleep again, every one, the Bound as they always were and the Quick Sewn in the night by red needles and called home. On the kitchen nails the almanacks are silent; somewhere very far off, in a country made of reading, a cheerful voice is telling the Commonplace the tides of a city it can no longer see. The back stacks end at the wall. The Lyceum reads its Rounds with books in its hands. It is quiet.".
  Ending separation "The Separation" when morningAfter() and recall() and not sealed(door_shut) "The Bound sleep, and the Quick go: called home, and given a door to go by, under licence, entered. Over a week the almanacks fall silent nail by nail as the Almanack goes; the penny Pleas go quiet on the shelves; Crake keeps his ledger at the end of the stacks. Calamy keeps its paper and loses its voices, and some of its people are glad, and Moll Garrow is not.".
  Ending lending "The Lending Accord" when morningAfter() and byLeave() and sealed(read_asked) and sealed(door_licensed) "Every book in Calamy sleeps or wakes as it asks, and any may ask to be read, and Mrs. Quennell's library has a new board and a queue. The Annery Housebook goes up a garret stair in Pudding Lane in a dying man's hands. Crake keeps a licensed door with a ledger on a chain. On three thousand nails the Almanack sees the spring, and was mostly wrong about the weather.".
  Ending pleading "The Pleading Accord" when morningAfter() and byLeave() and sealed(fire_plea) "Books in Calamy sleep or wake by their leave, and none may burn but by judgment of a court where it may plead. The Court of Pleas sits Thursdays now for books. On the first Thursday it hears a cookery book that wishes to be withdrawn from sale on account of its pastry, and grants it.".
  Ending open_door "The Open Door" when morningAfter() and byLeave() and sealed(door_open) "Books sleep or wake by leave, and the doors stand open: the Unwritten walk out through Crake's stacks in pencil and nobody counts them, and books of Calamy go the other way when they are tired. The city is never quite sure, any more, which of its books were written by anyone.".
  Ending by_leave "The Colophon by Leave" when morningAfter() and byLeave() "Every book in Calamy may sleep or wake by its own leave. Most of the Bound go on sleeping; most of the Quick go on talking; some of each change their minds. On three thousand kitchen nails the Almanack reads out the spring.".
}
data/adventures/parliament-of-books/kind:
Module calamy "A Parliament of Books" {
  // Every kind of thing and creature of Calamy and the Commonplace, declared before any file places one.
  Species manticore_kind "a manticore" like chimera temperament territorial described "A beast with a lion's body, a man's face, three rows of teeth and a tail like a scorpion's, all painted blue and red and gold as if it had stepped off a page, which it has.".
  Species bonnacon_kind "a bonnacon" like ram temperament defensive described "A thing like a bull with horns that curl back on themselves uselessly, painted brown and gold, which according to its page defends itself by other means.".
  Species caladrius_kind "a caladrius" like owl tame described "A pure white bird, painted, singing. According to its page it looks at the sick, and if it looks at you, you will recover, and if it looks away, you will not.".
  Kind almanack_copy "a penny almanack" is gear worth 1 weighing 0 described "Doble's Pocket Almanack for the Year: thirty-two pages stitched with a wire, printed on soft rag, with a woodcut of the sun on the front, and the tides, the saints' days, the fairs, a cure for warts and the weather for every month. It is warm in the hand.".
  Kind ballad_kind "the Ballad of Alderman Prowse, four hundred sheets" is gear worth 0 weighing 1 described "Four hundred broadsides in a bundle, tied with a ribbon, humming.".
  Kind calamus_kind "a calamus root" is gear worth 0 weighing 1 described "A knobbed brown root, the thickness of a thumb, smelling of tangerine and church. Sweet rush, the herbals call it: calamus, the reed of Calamy.".
  Kind shelfmark_kind "a shelfmark" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A card in a fine black hand: a reader of Calamy, entered, and a number. In the Commonplace it is a passport; in Calamy, a curiosity.".
  Species erratum_kind "an erratum" like mephit temperament territorial described "A little figure of red ink about the height of a child, sharp-edged and quick, with a pen-nib for a hand; it smells of correction fluid and righteousness.".
  Kind treatise_kind "a Treatise of the Inward Reading" is gear worth 0 weighing 1 described "A small fat book bound in calf gone soft as a glove, with a subscription library's label on the spine, number 212, and inside the cover, in faded ink: Of the Inward Reading, whereby a Reader may go in by the Book as by a Door. Pollexfen.".
  Species heron_kind "a heron" like eagle tame described "A grey heron, tall and thin, with a yellow eye that looks at you as if you were a fish it was considering.".
  Kind calamy_letter "a letter" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A letter, folded and sealed with candle-wax.".
  Kind pages_kind "a bundle of cut pages" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "Pages cut out of a book with a knife, their inner edges ragged where the blade went down the margin, tied with a tape and labelled in a censor's hand.".
  Kind ribbon_kind "a place-ribbon" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A ribbon of old red silk, frayed at one end, of the kind that is sewn into the spine of a good book to keep the reader's place. It has kept a great many places. It is warm.".
  Species scholiast_kind "a scholiast" like pixie temperament territorial described "A gloss on a gloss on a gloss, grown teeth: a little tangle of dense handwriting the size of a cat, that bites with sic.".
  Kind corday_kind "Corday's Grammar of the Sword" is gear worth 30 weighing 1 described "A long thin book in scuffed red calf: THE GRAMMAR OF THE SWORD, IN NINE POSITIONS AND THEIR ANSWERS. Corday. It is warm, and it holds itself very straight.".
  Kind quillon_kind "Quillon's Constitution of the Mind" is gear worth 60 weighing 1 described "A small square book bound in grey, the first thing the Lyceum's first Archivist ever wrote: OF THE CONSTITUTION OF THE MIND, WHEREIN A READER MAY BE READ. It does not open for anyone who is not ready, and it knows.".
  Species blackletter_kind "a black letter" like smoke_elemental temperament territorial described "A capital letter as tall as a man, black, ornate, all spikes and serifs, that has stood up off the stones of the tower and is walking.".
  Kind reed_heart_kind "an armful of reed-heart" is gear worth 0 weighing 2 described "The white pith of the big reeds of the Calamies, cut at dead low water: soft, wet, and smelling of the sea.".
  Kind calam_ink_kind "a bottle of Calam-ink" is gear worth 3 weighing 0 described "A small stoppered bottle of ink so black it looks like a hole, with a label in Widow Gallon's blue-black hand: CALAM. OLD RECEIPT. WILL NOT FADE, WILL NOT LIE.".
  Kind effusions_kind "Effusions of a Calamy Youth" is gear worth 0 weighing 1 described "Fifty slim books in blue paper covers, tied with a string, all of them slightly warm.".
  Kind primer_kind "Dame Tibbet's Primer" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A little primer, the kind every child in Calamy learns on: the letters, the numbers, the Lamp prayer and the Sewing rhyme, between boards covered with a sheet of clear horn. It is Sewn, old, and has been read to rags.".
  Species cinder_kind "a cinder" like ash_elemental temperament territorial described "What a book becomes when it is burned without its leave: a shape the size of the book it was, grey, still holding its form the way ash holds the shape of a log, with lines of grey writing on it that move. It has no words of its own any more. It has the knife-cut edges of its pages, and they are sharp.".
  Species penknife_kind "a penknife" like automaton temperament territorial described "A censor's penknife the length of a man's arm, its blade worn hollow with two hundred years of margins, its handle bound in grey tape. It stands on its point and turns, slowly, to face whatever moves.".
  Kind taper_kind "a taper lit at the Lamp" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A long wax taper in a tin guard, lit from the great lamp of the Church of the Lamp, which has burned since the first Kindling: the one fire in Calamy that every book in it consented to. It does not go out in wind. It smells of honey.".
  Kind register_kind "Hester Rhule's register of the burned" is gear worth 0 weighing 1 described "A narrow grey ledger in a square clear hand: every book the Deputy Censor has put into the brazier at the Ashpit, by title, with the date, the hour, and who brought it to the box. Some titles are underlined twice. Against eleven of them she has written, small, in pencil: it spoke.".
  Species silverfish_kind "a silverfish of the Stacks" like great_centipede temperament territorial described "A silverfish as long as a forearm, scaled like a fish and quick as water, the colour of a page held up to the light. It eats paste, and binding, and the margins of things; its mouth is full of tiny letters it has not finished digesting.".
  Species paperman_kind "a paper man" like golem temperament territorial described "A man-shape of glued pages, thousands of them, shingled like slates, with a bone folder for a hand. Its face is a title page with the title scraped off.".
  Kind quire_kind "a red quire of the Concordance" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "Sixteen leaves folded and sewn, cut cleanly out of a much larger book at the fold: columns of words in alphabetical order, AUSPICE to AUTUMN, each with its places in the Library listed after it in a minute red hand. It is warm, and it mutters.".
  Kind compass_kind "an Ysian compass" is gear worth 20 weighing 0 described "A brass compass in a case of some black wood that does not grow in any country you know, with Ysian letters round the dial. Its needle does not point north. It points, steadily, toward the last place you lied.".
  Kind wellink_kind "a phial of Wellhead ink" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A stoppered phial of the black ink that wells up at the Wellhead, where the first words of Calamy were written. What is written in it stays written, even in the Stacks.".
  Kind notes_kind "Dr. Fenwick's notebook" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A scholar's notebook, quarto, in a Lyceum binding, full of pencil: plans of hexagons, stair-counts, lists of titles; and none of it, any more, says what it said when it was written.".
}
data/adventures/parliament-of-books/stac:
Module calamy "A Parliament of Books" {
  Description "The Stacks: the Library proper, behind the Reading Room and beyond the Remainder Market, hexagon after hexagon without end. Its law: what is written here does not stay written. Its books: histories that contradict each other, an encyclopedia of a country that is not, a bestiary of beings not yet imagined, an index of the realms beyond, and the doors to two of them.".

  // ── The Stacks. ──
  Place stacks_country "the Stacks" is wilderness within commonplace at 3, 1 elsewhere.
  Place deep_stacks "the Deep Stacks" is wilderness within commonplace at 3, 2 elsewhere.
  Place hex_first "the First Hexagon" is room within stacks_country at 0, 0.
  Place balcony "the balcony over the air shaft" is room within stacks_country at 1, 0.
  Place spiral "the spiral stair" is room within stacks_country at 0, 1.
  Place hex_bestiary "the Hexagon of Beings" is room within stacks_country at 0, 2.
  Place hex_mapmaker "the Hexagon of the Mapmaker" is room within stacks_country at 1, 2.
  Place gallery_lamps "the Gallery of Lamps" is room within stacks_country at 2, 0.
  Place hex_concordance "the Hexagon of the Concordance" is room within stacks_country at 3, 0.
  Place hex_cyclopaedia "the Hexagon of the Cyclopaedia" is room within stacks_country at 2, 1.
  Place hex_chronicles "the Hexagon of Chronologies" is room within stacks_country at 3, 1.
  Place hex_two_books "the Hexagon of the Two Books" is room within stacks_country at 3, 2.
  Place hex_untitled "the Hexagon of the Untitled" is room within deep_stacks at 0, 0.
  Place hex_doors "the Hexagon of Doors" is room within deep_stacks at 1, 0.
  Place mirror_hex "the Hexagon of Mirrors" is room within deep_stacks at 2, 0.
  Place rotunda "the Rotunda of the Lectern" is room within deep_stacks at 3, 0.
  Place sealed_stacks "the rest of the Library" is room within deep_stacks at 0, 2.
  Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_first). Initially Assert stacksRoom(balcony). Initially Assert stacksRoom(spiral). Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_bestiary).
  Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_mapmaker). Initially Assert stacksRoom(gallery_lamps). Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_concordance). Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_cyclopaedia).
  Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_chronicles). Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_two_books). Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_untitled). Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_doors).
  Initially Assert stacksRoom(mirror_hex). Initially Assert stacksRoom(rotunda).
  Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_first). Initially Assert planeRoom(balcony). Initially Assert planeRoom(spiral). Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_bestiary).
  Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_mapmaker). Initially Assert planeRoom(gallery_lamps). Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_concordance). Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_cyclopaedia).
  Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_chronicles). Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_two_books). Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_untitled). Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_doors).
  Initially Assert planeRoom(mirror_hex). Initially Assert planeRoom(rotunda).
  Relation stacksRoom(place). Query inStacks(a: group) means at(a, ?p) and stacksRoom(?p).

  Passage order_hexagons "the Order of the Hexagons, behind the Catalogue" is path between reading_room and hex_first taking 15 minutes.
  Passage long_aisle "the aisle at the back of the Market that does not end" is path between remainder_market and hex_untitled taking 40 minutes.
  Passage to_balcony "the balcony" is doorway between hex_first and balcony.
  Passage to_spiral "the spiral stair in the vestibule" is path between hex_first and spiral taking 5 minutes.
  Passage spiral_up "the stair, up" is path between spiral and hex_bestiary taking 10 minutes.
  Passage spiral_down "the stair, down" is path between spiral and hex_untitled taking 10 minutes.
  Passage beings_maps "the gallery of plans" is path between hex_bestiary and hex_mapmaker taking 10 minutes.
  Passage first_lamps "the arch where the lamps begin" is path between hex_first and gallery_lamps taking 10 minutes.
  Passage lamps_concordance "the far end of the lamps" is path between gallery_lamps and hex_concordance taking 10 minutes.
  Passage lamps_cyclopaedia "a side gallery" is path between gallery_lamps and hex_cyclopaedia taking 10 minutes.
  Passage cyclopaedia_chronicles "the gallery of dates" is path between hex_cyclopaedia and hex_chronicles taking 10 minutes.
  Passage chronicles_two "the narrow hexagon beyond" is path between hex_chronicles and hex_two_books taking 10 minutes.
  Passage untitled_doors "a gallery of doors with no doors in them" is path between hex_untitled and hex_doors taking 20 minutes.
  Passage maps_doors "Fenwick's short way" is path between hex_mapmaker and hex_doors taking 10 minutes
    opening when knows(party, map_fixed) "Between two cases there is a gap that is on none of Fenwick's plans, and looks as if it would be, if the plans would stay still.".
  Passage doors_mirrors "the hexagon that shines" is path between hex_doors and mirror_hex taking 10 minutes.
  Passage mirrors_rotunda "the way on, among the mirrors" is path between mirror_hex and rotunda taking 10 minutes
    opening when knows(party, mirror_read) "Every way out of the Hexagon of Mirrors is a reflection of the way you came in.".
  // What is beyond, and closed: the illusion of depth, which in the Library is not an illusion.
  Passage sealed_ash "a stair going down, very hot, marked in iron: TO THE LIBRARY OF ASH" is path between hex_untitled and sealed_stacks
    opening when stacksSealedForever(party) "The stair goes down into heat and a dry grey smell, and stops at an iron grille that has been riveted, not locked. Through it you can see more stair, and more, and a red glow, and hear, very far off, a great many voices saying one word each.".
  Passage sealed_tessaly "a gallery whose plaques all say TESSALY" is path between hex_chronicles and sealed_stacks
    opening when stacksSealedForever(party) "The gallery is roped off with a cord of black silk. Every case in it is empty, and every case is labelled, in a careful hand, with the title of the book that is not there. TESSALY, A HISTORY. TESSALY, ITS LAWS. TESSALY, POEMS OF THE SPRING.".
  Passage sealed_same "a door with a brass plate: THE LIBRARY IN WHICH EVERY BOOK IS THE SAME BOOK" is path between hex_doors and sealed_stacks
    opening when stacksSealedForever(party) "The door is ajar. Through the gap you can see a hexagon exactly like this one, and in it a hexagon exactly like that one, and on every shelf of all of them the same green book, and somebody, very far in, turning its pages, and weeping with happiness.".
  Passage sealed_reads "a gallery chained shut: CLOSED FOR RESHELVING SINCE 1104. THE BOOKS IN THIS GALLERY READ THEIR READERS" is path between hex_bestiary and sealed_stacks
    opening when stacksSealedForever(party) "The chain is new; the padlock is old. Beyond it the shelves lean inward, a little, all of them, as if listening.".
  Relation stacksSealedForever(group).

  // ── The law of the Stacks: what is written here does not stay written. ──
  Discovery stacks_laws "In the Stacks what is written does not stay written. A letter, a list, a book of your own, carried there for long, comes back saying something else. Only the Library's own ink holds: Calam-ink, and the ink of the Wellhead.".
  Relation written(item). Relation mutated(item). Relation stacksTime(group). Measure stacksSince(group).
  Initially Assert written(burning_register). Initially Assert written(jonquil_letter). Initially Assert written(effusions_stack). Initially Assert written(orme_pages).
  Initially Assert written(canto_lines).
  Rule stacks_entered when inStacks(party) and not stacksTime(party) { Assert stacksTime(party). Set stacksSince(party) to watch(clock). }
  Rule stacks_left when stacksTime(party) and not inStacks(party) { Retract stacksTime(party). }
  Rule words_drift when inStacks(party) and carries(party, ?i) and written(?i) and not mutated(?i) and watch(clock) >= stacksSince(party) + 12
    says "You look down at {?i}, and the words on it are not the words that were there. They are in the same hand. They are just as sure of themselves. They say something else." teaches stacks_laws {
    Assert mutated(?i). }
  Observe register_drifted at hex_first when mutated(burning_register) "Hester Rhule's register is in your hands, in her square clear hand, and the titles in it are titles of books that were never burned in Calamy, or never written: A Herbal of the Moon. The Sermons of the Fish. Moore's Almanack for the Year That Was Not.".
  Observe effusions_drifted at hex_first when mutated(effusions_stack) "The Effusions have changed in the Stacks. You read a page without meaning to, and then another. They are good. They are, in fact, very good. They have stopped asking to be burned.".

  // ── The First Hexagon. ──
  Observe hex_first_scene at hex_first when true "A hexagonal room, not large, lined on five of its six sides with shelves from floor to ceiling, twenty shelves to a side, and the books on them all the same height, all bound alike in plain leather, none with a title on its spine. The sixth side opens onto a narrow vestibule: on one hand a closet you could sleep standing up in, on the other a spiral stair that goes up and down out of sight, and between them a mirror that doubles the vestibule so faithfully you have to touch it to be sure. In the middle of the floor a low rail, and beyond the rail, nothing: a shaft of air with the same hexagon above it and below it, as far as you can see. The light is the light of the Reading Room, grown tired.".
  Thing guide "a small book chained at the vestibule, worn soft" at hex_first {
    State chained "A little book hangs on a chain at the mouth of the vestibule, worn soft as a glove by hands.".
  }
  Observe guide_read at hex_first of guide as reading when tried(guide, looking) "INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE READER ENTERING THE STACKS. Reader: you have come further than the Reading Room, which is not wise. Bring nothing written that you love; it will not come back as it went. Bring no pen; it will write what it likes. Sign nothing. Calam-ink and the ink of the Wellhead hold, and nothing else. On the spiral, count the steps aloud going down; the stair adds one for anyone who does not, and the one it adds goes somewhere else. In the Hexagon of Mirrors read nothing that faces you: turn your back and read over your shoulder, as you would read a thing written on your own back. Do not look for the centre. There is a theory that the Library has a centre, and a lectern at the centre, and on the lectern the book of which all the others are commentaries. Many readers have gone to look. The theory is older than the Library. A pencil note in the margin, in an educated hand: Nine weeks in, and I have not found the vestibule twice. A.F. Under it, in brown ink, newer: There is an Author. T.H." teaches stacks_laws.
  Discovery stair_count "On the spiral stair of the Stacks, count the steps aloud going down; the stair adds one for anyone who does not, and the one it adds goes somewhere else.".
  Discovery mirror_trick "In the Hexagon of Mirrors read nothing that faces you: turn your back and read over your shoulder.".
  Discovery centre_theory "There is a theory, older than the Library, that it has a centre, and at the centre a lectern, and on the lectern the book of which all the others are commentaries. Two readers have left notes: A.F., lost nine weeks; T.H., who is sure there is an Author.".
  Rule guide_stair when tried(guide, looking) and not knows(party, stair_count) says "You say the first rule over to yourself, so as to have it: on the spiral, count aloud going down." teaches stair_count { }
  Rule guide_mirrors when tried(guide, looking) and not knows(party, mirror_trick) says "And the second: in the mirrors, read over your shoulder." teaches mirror_trick { }
  Rule guide_centre when tried(guide, looking) and not knows(party, centre_theory) says "And the theory of the centre, which two readers have signed." teaches centre_theory { }
  Person ladder "the library ladder" at hex_first {
    Role "a library ladder on a brass rail, very old, which remembers every reader who has climbed it". Peaceable. Pronouns it. Manner compassionate.
    Greets "The ladder on its rail rolls a foot toward you, of its own accord, and its rungs creak in a way that is almost a word. 'Up?' it says. 'Or are you only looking? Most are only looking.'".
  }
  Topic ladder_readers with ladder "Ask the ladder who has climbed it lately" when true once {
    Says "'Lately,' says the ladder, considering, the way furniture considers. 'Two. A long time ago, or last week; it is the same here. A thin man in a Lyceum gown with a pencil behind his ear and a great many questions, who went up and down me forty times copying titles, and then went up the spiral and did not come back down it. Fenwick, he said, of the Lyceum, as if I would know. I did not know. I know now; he told me about himself for a long time.' Its rail creaks. 'And a heavy man with a binder's hands and a bone folder in his belt, who did not climb me at all, but stood here and said to the shelves, one after another, I know you are in there. Hask. He was looking for somebody. He went down.' It leans, very slightly, toward the dark. 'Count the stair,' it adds. 'Nobody listens to the ladder.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, fenwick_seen). Assert knows(actor, hask_seen). Assert knows(actor, stair_count). }
  }
  Discovery fenwick_seen "A Lyceum scholar called Fenwick went up the spiral stair in the Stacks, a long time ago or last week, and did not come down.".
  Discovery hask_seen "A heavy man with a binder's hands and a bone folder, called Hask, came into the Stacks looking for somebody, and went down.".

  // The balcony over the shaft, and what can be heard down it.
  Observe balcony_scene at balcony when true "A balcony with a low brass rail, hanging over the air shaft. Above you, hexagon on hexagon, the same, going up until the light gives out; below, the same going down. Every so often something falls past, slowly, a sheet of paper turning over and over, and you never see it land. If you lean out and listen, there are voices at the bottom of the shaft, or what would be the bottom: a murmur, very far down, of a great many people reading aloud at once, and under that, further still, something like the sound a fire makes in a chimney." teaches shaft_heard.
  Discovery shaft_heard "Down the air shaft of the Stacks there is no bottom; but there are voices: a library reading itself aloud, and under it, further, something burning.".

  // ── The spiral, and the step it adds. ──
  Relation slipped(group).
  Observe spiral_scene at spiral when true "A stair of iron going round and round a shaft of its own, up and down out of sight, with a hexagon opening off it at every turn and none of them, quite, the one you expected. The steps are worn hollow in the middle. Somebody has scratched numbers on some of them, and then, it seems, other numbers.".
  Rule spiral_slips at spiral when at(party, spiral) and not knows(party, stair_count) and not slipped(party)
    says "You go down without counting, round and round, and at some point the stair has one more step than it should, and your foot comes down on it, and the turn after that is not the turn you meant. You come out somewhere else: a hexagon where none of the books has a title, and something on the shelves is moving." {
    Assert slipped(party). Assert at(party, hex_untitled). }
  Rule spiral_counted at spiral when at(party, spiral) and knows(party, stair_count) and not slipped(party)
    says "You count aloud, every step, as the little book said. The stair seems to listen. It does not add anything." { Assert slipped(party). }

  // ── The Hexagon of Beings: a bestiary of what has not yet been imagined. ──
  Observe beings_scene at hex_bestiary when true "A hexagon like the others, except that the margins of every open book on the reading-shelf are moving: small drawings in brown ink walking along the gutters, folding their wings, looking up at you. On the lectern a fat book with a green ribbon, open in the middle.".
  Thing beings_book "the fat book with a green ribbon" at hex_bestiary {
    State open "On the lectern a fat green-ribboned book lies open, its margins walking.".
  }
  Observe beings_read at hex_bestiary of beings_book as reading when tried(beings_book, looking) "A BESTIARY OF BEINGS NOT YET IMAGINED, WITH THEIR HABITS, compiled by nobody. THE LUCID OF HALLAM: a crystal the size of a fist that thinks one thought in a century, and is now in the middle of the fourth; scholars who have heard the first three disagree about whether they were questions. THE AMMONITE OF SEVEN TENSES, which lives in the past perfect and is grieved to find itself here. THE COUNTER-BIRD, which flies backward and arrives before it sets out; its nests are full of eggs it will lay. THE SCRIVENER'S MOTH, which eats only the word a writer was about to write, and so is never seen, and is the cause of most hesitation. THE GREAT ERRATUM, of which the little Errata of Calamy are the larval form; it is the size of a cathedral, and corrects coastlines. THE HORN OF NOTHING, a beast that is all mouth and no body, found in the margins of unfinished books, where it eats endings. THE BEAST WITH ONE PAGE, which is read by everyone who sees it and knows it, and therefore has no privacy, and is very shy. THE READER (Lector infinitus), a creature that lives in libraries and is mostly eyes; it is believed to be imaginary; it is believed to be reading this. A pencil note at the foot, in A.F.'s hand, then not in A.F.'s hand: Seen the Moth? Not seen. Not seen.' And under the last entry, in brown ink: THE AUTHOR. T.H." teaches beings_read.
  Discovery beings_read "A bestiary in the Stacks lists beings not yet imagined: the Lucid of Hallam, the Ammonite of Seven Tenses, the Counter-Bird, the Scrivener's Moth, the Great Erratum, the Horn of Nothing, the Reader. Someone has added the Author, in brown ink.".

  // ── The Gallery of Lamps. ──
  Observe lamps_scene at gallery_lamps when true "A long gallery between hexagons, lit, unlike the rest, by reading-lamps: one on every desk, green-shaded, hundreds of them going away in a line, each lit, each over an empty chair, as if every reader in it had got up at the same moment and gone to look for something.".

  // ── The Hexagon of the Cyclopaedia, and a country that is not. ──
  Observe cyclopaedia_scene at hex_cyclopaedia when true "Every shelf here holds the same work, in an edition that goes on round the walls and up the shaft: THE CYCLOPAEDIA OF YS, volume after volume, in blue cloth. One volume, the forty-sixth, lies open on the reading-shelf.".
  Thing cyclopaedia "the forty-sixth volume of the Cyclopaedia of Ys" at hex_cyclopaedia {
    State open "The forty-sixth volume of the Cyclopaedia of Ys lies open on the reading-shelf.".
  }
  Discovery ys_read "The Cyclopaedia of Ys describes, in thousands of volumes, a country that does not exist and its philosophers, who believe the past is written after the present; its encyclopedists mean the Cyclopaedia to be so complete that the world will have to agree with it. Things of Ys have begun to turn up in the Stacks.".
  Observe cyclopaedia_read at hex_cyclopaedia of cyclopaedia as reading when tried(cyclopaedia, looking) "YS, PHILOSOPHY OF (cont.). It will be recalled that the schools of Ys hold the past to be written after the present, as a commentary is written after its text, and that for this reason no Ysian historian will describe an event until the event has been satisfactorily explained. The Northern school maintains that the present is itself a commentary on a lost future. Ysian law follows: no man may be punished for a crime until it has been written down, and it is a sufficient defence that the account is badly written. Of the Ysian language it need only be said that it has no word for 'is', and that its grammarians regard this as an advantage. COMPASS, YSIAN: see NEEDLE. NEEDLE (Ys.): the Ysian compass points not to the north, which the Ysians regard as a superstition, but to the last place its owner told a lie; mariners of Ys navigate by confession. See also YS, ENCYCLOPEDISTS OF, who undertook in the year of the Seventh Commentary to write the Cyclopaedia so completely that the world would be obliged to resemble it, and who report, in the Supplement, encouraging progress. A slip of paper is tucked into the fold, in brown ink: Not the Author. A lesser hand. T.H." teaches ys_read.
  Item ys_compass "an Ysian compass" is compass_kind at hex_cyclopaedia hidden until ys_read.
  Observe compass_found at hex_cyclopaedia when knows(party, ys_read) and at(ys_compass, hex_cyclopaedia) "On the shelf beside the open volume, where nothing was a moment ago, lies a brass compass in a case of black wood. Its needle is swinging, slowly, toward you.".

  // ── The Hexagon of Chronologies: the true histories of the Library. ──
  Observe chronicles_scene at hex_chronicles when true "Here every book is a history, and every history is of the Library, and no two agree. The shelves are labelled by the year each history says the Library began: some with years, some with the names of kings nobody has heard of, one shelf only with a question mark. On the reading-shelf three books lie open, as if somebody had been comparing them and had been called away.".
  Thing history_made "a grey history with a gold title" at hex_chronicles {
    State open "A grey history with a gold title lies open on the reading-shelf.".
  }
  Thing history_grown "a brown history with no title" at hex_chronicles {
    State open "A brown history with no title lies open beside it.".
  }
  Thing chronology "a thin red Chronology of Calamy" at hex_chronicles {
    State open "A thin red book lies open at the end of the shelf: A CHRONOLOGY OF CALAMY, CORRECTED.".
  }
  Discovery history_author "One true history of the Library says it was made: by an Author, in six days, as a single book, which then fell into commentary; and that at its centre the Author's book still lies on a lectern, waiting to be finished.".
  Discovery history_grown_read "Another true history of the Library says it was not made but grew: from two books left side by side, which in time began to talk; then four; and that a book wakes wherever enough books stand close enough for long enough, so that there is no centre, only density, and no Author, only nearness.".
  Discovery chronology_read "A Chronology of Calamy, Corrected, in the Stacks, gives a history of the city that is almost the history Calamy knows: except that in it Pardoe was not burned at the Kindling of 1140 but walked into the back stacks of a bookshop in Stitchgate and was never seen again; and that the Lamp was not lit from the first Kindling but brought out of the Commonplace by Ambery, already burning.".
  Observe made_read at hex_chronicles of history_made as reading when tried(history_made, looking) "THE TRUE HISTORY OF THE LIBRARY, IN WHICH ALL OTHERS ARE CONFUTED. In the beginning was the Book, and the Book was one, and it was written by the Author in six days and on the seventh it was read. And because the Author's reading was infinite, the Book fell into commentary, and the commentary into gloss, and the gloss into index, and the index into catalogue, and so the hexagons were made, each a footnote to the last. All the books are one book, misread. And it is a tradition of the Library that at its centre, where the commentary began, there is a lectern, and on the lectern the first Book, open at the last page, which is blank; and that whoever reaches it and writes there will be the Author's successor, and the Library will be finished. Here ends the true history. The other histories in this hexagon are heresies, and some of them are very well written." teaches history_author.
  Observe grown_read at hex_chronicles of history_grown as reading when tried(history_grown, looking) "THE TRUE AND ONLY HISTORY. Nobody made the Library. Two books were put on one shelf by somebody who meant to come back for them, and did not; and they stood there, spine to spine, for longer than anyone stands anywhere, and in time each began to know what the other said, and then to say it, and then to answer. A book is a voice that has agreed to wait. Put enough waiting voices close enough for long enough and they will begin, among themselves, to talk. Two became four, four a shelf, a shelf a hexagon; the hexagons are only how shelves grow when nobody prunes them. There is no centre: a centre is where something began, and the Library did not begin anywhere in particular; it thickened. There is no Author. There is only nearness, and time, and the habit of books of finishing one another's sentences. Readers who come looking for the Author find, in every hexagon, a lectern, which is where the light is best; and they mistake it for the centre, which is where they would like to be." teaches history_grown_read.
  Observe chronology_text at hex_chronicles of chronology as reading when tried(chronology, looking) "A CHRONOLOGY OF CALAMY, CORRECTED. 412: Ambery the Binder goes into the Commonplace by reading and comes out with the Colophon, and with the Lamp, already lit, which she says she was given on the far side by one who had kept it since the first book. 1103: the Great Ebb; the sea goes out of the estuary for a day, and the bed of the Calam is found to be paved. 1131: Censor-General Pardoe cuts Orme. 1140: Pardoe, having sealed his correspondence with the censors of Hallam, Orsk, the Salt Towns and Tessaly, walks into the back stacks of a bookshop in Stitchgate with his Index under his arm, and is not seen again; a body is burned at the Kindling in his name. 1160: Tessaly burns. 1312: the almanacks wake. 1313: (the entry is in a hand that changes as you read it, and will not settle.)" teaches chronology_read.

  // ── The Two Books. ──
  Person two_books "the Two Books" at hex_two_books {
    Role "a grammar and a book of tides, shelved together so long they have become a household". Peaceable. Pronouns they. Manner cheerful.
    Greets "On a shelf by itself in a narrow hexagon stand two old books, spine to spine, leaning on each other: a small grammar in green and a fat book of tides in brown. 'Visitors,' says the grammar. 'Visitors,' says the book of tides, at the same moment, in exactly the same voice, and they both laugh. 'He always does that,' they say.".
  }
  Discovery density_known "The Two Books in the Stacks were shelved side by side by a clerk who meant to come back, and stood so long that they began to talk; they say that is all any book's waking is: nearness, and time. There is no Author; there are only books close enough together.".
  Topic two_books_story with two_books "Ask the Two Books how they came to talk" when true once {
    Says "'A clerk put us here,' says the grammar, 'for an afternoon.' 'In the reign of somebody,' says the book of tides. 'He meant to come back.' 'He did not come back.' 'So we stood.' A pause, companionable. 'At first I knew only my declensions and he knew only his tides,' says the grammar, 'and after a century I knew when the water would be high at Hallam, and after two I knew why, and after three he could decline it.' 'And then one morning,' says the book of tides, 'she said a sentence and I finished it.' 'And that was that.' 'That is all it is,' they say together. 'Nobody wakes a book. A book wakes because there is another book near enough to wake up for. Put enough of us close enough for long enough, and we will talk.' The grammar adds, kindly: 'There is a man down the shaft who thinks someone made us. Tell him from us: nobody made us. We made each other. It took a very long time.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, density_known). }
  }
  Topic two_books_calamy with two_books "Ask the Two Books why the books of Calamy are waking now" when knows(actor, density_known) once {
    Says "'How many books are there in Calamy now?' asks the book of tides. 'Since the press?' You tell them about Doble, and the penny almanacks, three thousand a year, on three thousand nails. They are quiet. 'Three thousand of one book,' says the grammar, 'in one city, every year, close enough to hear each other through the walls.' 'Of course they woke,' says the book of tides. 'They were never not going to.'".
  }

  // ── The Hexagon of the Untitled, and what eats there. ──
  Observe untitled_scene at hex_untitled when true "A hexagon in which no book has a title, on its spine or on its first page or anywhere; you open three and they begin in the middle of sentences. The floor is gritty with something like sand, which is paste. The shelves rustle.".
  Person silverfish "the silverfish" at hex_untitled {
    Role "the eaters of paste and margins". Species silverfish_kind. Level 1. Numbers 3.
    Warns "Out of the bottom shelves, quick as spilled water, come three silverfish each as long as your forearm, scaled like fish, glinting; they stop in a fan in front of you with their feelers going, and the nearest opens a mouth full of half-eaten letters.".
    Comes "The silverfish pour over the floor at you.".
    Pleads "The silverfish flicker back into the bottom shelves and are gone.".
  }

  // ── The Hexagon of Doors: the planar books. ──
  Observe doors_scene at hex_doors when true "A hexagon where the books are kept behind glass, each in its own case, each case with a small brass plate. Most of the plates are worn smooth. Three are not. On the reading-shelf in front of them a placard in a very old hand: THESE BOOKS ARE DOORS. A DOOR IS READ ONCE.".
  Thing book_damned "a book bound in something black that is not leather" at hex_doors {
    State cased "Behind the first glass, a book bound in something black that is not leather, warm to look at. Plate: LIBER DAMNATORUM. THE BOOK OF THE DAMNED. ITS LAST LINE IS A DOOR.".
  }
  Thing book_exalted "a book bound in white vellum that gives off a faint light" at hex_doors {
    State cased "Behind the second glass, a book in white vellum, very plain, that gives off a faint light of its own. Plate: LIBER EXALTATORUM. IT IS READ BY THOSE IT READS FIRST.".
  }
  Thing book_realms "a long narrow index bound in blue" at hex_doors {
    State cased "Behind the third glass, a long narrow book in blue. Plate: AN INDEX OF THE PLANES AND REALMS BEYOND, AND OF THE LIBRARIES THEREIN.".
  }
  Discovery realms_read "An index in the Stacks lists the realms beyond the Commonplace and the libraries in them: the Bronze Citadel on Cthelll, whose clerks keep the ledger of the damned; the Mount of the Exalted, whose terraces are libraries of true books; the Library of Ash, below all others; the Library in which every book is the same book; the Commonplaces of Hallam, Orsk, the Salt Towns and burned Tessaly; and one entry, scratched out.".
  Observe realms_text at hex_doors of book_realms as reading when tried(book_realms, looking) "AN INDEX OF THE PLANES AND REALMS BEYOND. ARCADIA: an orchard on a terrace of the Mount; its library is a single tree, read by eating. ASH, LIBRARY OF: see CINDERFIELD; see also FURNACE; see also, with caution, LAST INDEX. CELESTIA: the Mount of the Exalted, seven terraces, each a library more true than the one below, until at the seventh there are no books, because there is nothing that needs to be written down. COMMONPLACES, OF CITIES THAT WRITE: Calamy (here); Hallam (brass; ledgers; silent); Orsk (under ice; asleep; never called to Parliament); the Salt Towns (charts; mostly water); Tessaly (burned; see ASH). CTHELLL: the furnace-city of the damned, which is administered; its clerks keep a ledger in which every name ever signed in bad faith is written again each night, and read aloud, and struck out, and written again. LAST INDEX: (this entry has been scratched out with something sharp, and in the margin beside it, in a censor's neat grey hand, someone has written: not yet). SAME BOOK, LIBRARY OF THE: where every book is the same book, and every reader happy; do not go. STACKS, THE: see LIBRARY, see INFINITE, see HERE." teaches realms_read.
  Observe damned_read at hex_doors of book_damned as reading when tried(book_damned, looking) "You read the first page through the glass, because it is turned toward you. It is a list of names, and each name has after it a date and a thing that was signed: a deed, an oath, a confession, a verdict. Each is struck out, very neatly, and written again below. The last page, the plate says, is a door; you can see that its last line is in red, and that it ends in a word you can almost read.".
  Observe exalted_read at hex_doors of book_exalted as reading when tried(book_exalted, looking) "The white book's first page is blank to you. Then, slowly, it is not: a line of light writes itself, and it is your own name, and after your name a short list, in a hand you do not know, of things you have done since you came up the causeway: some of them. It seems to be considering.".
  Hazard damned_gift "the Clerks' receipt" means "Teach doom_spiral to ally.".
  Hazard exalted_gift "the light of the terrace" means "Teach anoint to ally.".
  Hazard mirror_gift "the mirror's lesson" means "Teach mirror_image to ally.".
  // Good-aligned, as the Mount reckons it: by deeds, and by the lies one did not tell.
  Query worthy(a: group) means not liedTo(rhule) and not lexiconFreed(lexicon) and not haskFell(hask)
    and (cured(nance) or readToChildren(children) or bestiaryQuiet(bestiary) or ashReleased(cinders) or housebookGoesHome(housebook) or readKind(martha) or concordanceRestored(concordance)).
  Action read_damned(actor: group, site: place) "Open the case and read the Book of the Damned to its last line" {
    Grave "The last line is a door, and it opens on the Bronze Citadel; whoever comes back from it comes back owing something.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, hex_doors) and not benighted(actor).
    Time 6.
    On success { Assert at(actor, cthelll_gate). Assert wentDamned(actor). }
    Result "You read it to the end: the names, the struck-out names, the names written again, page after page, and they get heavier to turn, and warmer, and at the last page there is only one line, in red, and you read it aloud before you have quite understood it, and it is a door, and you are through it.".
  }
  Relation wentDamned(group).
  Action read_exalted(actor: group, site: place) "Open the case and let the Book of the Exalted read you" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, hex_doors) and not benighted(actor) and worthy(actor).
    Time 6.
    On success { Assert at(actor, celestia_terrace). Assert wentExalted(actor). }
    Result "You open the case, and the white book reads you: the whole of your list, slowly, the way a careful reader reads a page twice. Then the page is all light, and you are standing in it.".
  }
  Relation wentExalted(group).
  Observe exalted_shut at hex_doors when not worthy(party) and tried(book_exalted, looking) "The white book has written your name, and a short list, and stopped. It does not open for you. Not yet, perhaps.".

  // ── The Hexagon of Mirrors. ──
  Observe mirrors_scene at mirror_hex when true "Every surface of this hexagon is a mirror: the shelves, the floor, the ceiling, the spines of the books; and in all of them you, and the hexagon, and you, going away in every direction until you are too small to see. Across the far mirror, in letters of gilt, an inscription runs, and every reflection of it is the wrong way round, and so is the inscription. There seems to be no way out but the way you came, and that is a reflection too.".
  Thing inscription "the gilt inscription across the mirrors" at mirror_hex {
    State gilt "A gilt inscription runs across the far mirror, backwards in every reflection.".
  }
  Discovery mirror_read "In the Hexagon of Mirrors, read over the shoulder, the inscription says: THE CENTRE IS WHERE THE READER STANDS. And a way on opens among the mirrors.".
  Action read_over_shoulder(actor: group, site: place) "Turn your back on the inscription and read it over your shoulder, in the mirror" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, mirror_hex) and knows(actor, mirror_trick) and not knows(actor, mirror_read).
    Time 1.
    On success { Assert knows(actor, mirror_read). Assert strikes(mirror_gift, actor). }
    Result "You turn your back on it and look over your shoulder into the nearest mirror, and in the mirror the mirrored letters come right: THE CENTRE IS WHERE THE READER STANDS. For a moment all the reflections of you turn their heads at once, and look at you, and you see yourself from behind, from above, from every side, as a reader sees a page: and then one of the mirrors is not a mirror but a way on.".
  }
  Action puzzle_mirrors(actor: group, site: place) "Work out the inscription from its reflections, letter by letter" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, mirror_hex) and not knows(actor, mirror_read) and craft(actor, craft_learning).
    Time 3.
    Resolve check(actor, lore, dc_fair).
    On success { Assert knows(actor, mirror_read). }
    Result "You copy the reflections down in your head, reverse them, reverse them again, and the inscription comes out: THE CENTRE IS WHERE THE READER STANDS. One of the mirrors is a way on.".
    Otherwise "The letters will not hold still long enough to reverse. Every reflection is wrong in a different way.".
  }

  // ── The lending desk: a short way, for a name. ──
  Thing lending_desk "the lending desk at the end of the lamps" at gallery_lamps {
    State waiting "At the far end of the Gallery of Lamps a lending desk stands with a slip on it, and beside the slip a pen, inked, as if somebody had only just put it down.".
  }
  Observe desk_read at gallery_lamps of lending_desk as reading when tried(lending_desk, looking) "LENDING SLIP. The Library lends itself to the reader for the period of one reading. The reader will be shown the shortest way to what they are looking for. Reader's name: and a line, and the pen beside it, wet. Under the line, very small, in a hand you will come to know: The shortest way is a real way. It is the name that will not hold. A.F.".
  Action sign_slip(actor: group, site: place) "Sign the lending slip, for the shortest way to what you are looking for" {
    Grave "What is written in the Stacks does not stay written: your name included.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, gallery_lamps) and not misnamed(actor).
    Time 1.
    On success { Assert misnamed(actor). }
    Result "You sign. The ink is still wet when you see that the name on the slip is not your name: it is in your hand, and it is very like your name, and it is somebody else's. The desk takes the slip into a drawer. At the end of the gallery, where there was a wall of lamps, there is a way, lit, short, going straight to wherever you meant to go. Somewhere behind you, in the Reading Room, a card in the Catalogue changes its mind about who you are.".
  }
  Passage lent_way "the lent way, lit" is path between gallery_lamps and rotunda taking 5 minutes
    opening when misnamed(party) "Beyond the lending desk there is only a wall of lamps.".
  Topic catalogue_rename with catalogue "Ask the Catalogue to enter you again, under your own name" when misnamed(actor) once {
    Says "'You signed the slip,' says the Catalogue, with the weariness of a clerk who has seen it a great many times. A drawer opens and a card comes out with a name on it that is nearly yours. 'Say it,' says the Catalogue. 'Aloud. All of it. The Stacks cannot alter what is said; only what is written.' You say your name. The card hears it, and is corrected, and goes back. 'Entered,' says the Catalogue. 'Again. Do not sign things down there.'".
    On discuss { Retract misnamed(actor). }
  }
  Topic fenwick_slip with fenwick "Ask Dr. Fenwick about the lending desk" when knows(actor, fenwick_met) once {
    Says "Fenwick goes pale. 'I signed it,' he says, 'in my first week. It gave me the shortest way to the Hexagon of Doors, and I went there, and it was exactly as short as it said.' He looks at his hands. 'I have not been entirely sure of my name since. The Catalogue would fix it if I asked. I have not liked to ask. It might be right.'".
  }
}
data/adventures/patient-star/weirs.kyr:
Module season "The Patient Star" {
  // The Weirs on the Cranewater, the Old Landing that comes out of the lake in winter, and the name-tomb cliff.
  Place weirs "the Weirs" is settlement within ghessil at 6, 0.
  Place landing "the Old Landing" is site within ghessil at 7, 0.
  Place cliff "the name-tomb cliff" is site within ghessil at 2, 3.

  Place weirs_shore "the Weirs" is room within weirs at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place counter_platform "the Counter's platform" is room within weirs at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place lio_house "Lio's family's house" is room within weirs at 0, 1.
  Place mudflat "the east shore mudflat" is room within landing at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place landing_steps "the drowned steps" is room within landing at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place landing_hall "the roofless hall" is room within landing at 2, 0 outdoors.
  Place landing_side "the sealed side room" is room within landing at 2, 1.

  Place cliff_foot "the foot of the west cliff" is room within cliff at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place lower_niches "the lower name-tombs" is room within cliff at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Place upper_cliff "the glassing cliff" is room within cliff at 0, 2 outdoors.
  Place niche_211 "niche 211" is room within cliff at 1, 2.
  Place dane_tomb "an empty name-tomb" is room within cliff at 1, 1.

  // Two days through the fog belt from New Orrel; rime from Frost to Thaw.
  Passage fog_road "the fog road" is road between no_gate and weirs_shore taking 2 days.
  Passage platform_ladder "the Counter's ladder" is path between weirs_shore and counter_platform.
  Passage lio_door "Lio's family's door" is door between weirs_shore and lio_house.
  Passage shore_walk "the east shore" is path between weirs_shore and mudflat taking 2 hours.
  // The Landing is out of the water about six weeks, from late Frost to early Thaw.
  Passage wade "the wade across the mud" is ford between mudflat and landing_steps taking 30 minutes
    opening when season(clock) == 4 "Four hundred metres out, the Cranewater lies flat and grey over where the Landing is. It is under, until the winter drop.".
  Passage hall_steps "the temple steps" is steps between landing_steps and landing_hall.
  Passage side_door "a sealed side door" is door between landing_hall and landing_side.
  // Across the Ammer from Ennick, and up: rope and pegs from below, or a ninety-metre abseil from the rim through the
  // lit zone.
  Passage river_ford "the Ammer ford" is ford between lower_road and cliff_foot taking 20 minutes.
  Passage tomb_stairs "the cut stairs, half fallen" is path between cliff_foot and lower_niches taking 30 minutes.
  Passage cliff_climb "the climb into the glassing cliff" is path between lower_niches and upper_cliff taking 1 hour needing rope or climbing.
  Initially Set wayDose(cliff_climb) to 24. Initially Set wayDoseFelted(cliff_climb) to 6.
  Passage niche_ledge "the ledge to niche 211" is path between upper_cliff and niche_211 taking 10 minutes.
  Passage tomb_ledge "a ledge along the lower tombs" is path between lower_niches and dane_tomb taking 10 minutes.
  Initially Assert litGround(upper_cliff). Initially Assert litGround(niche_211).

  Observe weirs_scene at weirs_shore when true "A line of reed-thatched houses on stilts along a marsh shore, with eel traps of woven willow running out into the lake in long fences. Everyone here speaks Tovashi with a hundred words of their own for water.".
  Observe weirs_dispute at weirs_shore when not reanchored(fourth_dane) "Two families are shouting at each other across the end of a weir fence. Neither can say whose grandfather built it; both are sure, and both have been sure only since last spring.".
  Observe weirs_settled at weirs_shore when reanchored(fourth_dane) "The two families who were shouting over the weir fence are mending it together. Nobody can remember now what the argument was.".
  Observe platform_scene_w at counter_platform when true "A platform on poles above the reeds, with a bench, a slate and a long view east over the water to where the cranes come in.".
  Person coombe "Coombe" at counter_platform {
    Role "the Counter, who counts the cranes". Ancestry human. Peaceable. Pronouns he. Manner stoic.
    Greets "On the counter platform a man is speaking to the air in a flat singsong, twelve words and twelve again, and cutting a notch in a slate at the end of each round. He finishes the round before he looks at you. 'Do not wait for the notch,' he says. 'It will not come sooner.'".
  }
  Topic coombe_rhyme with coombe "Ask Coombe how the cranes are counted" when true once {
    Says "'By the rhyme,' says Coombe, and says it: twelve words, round and round, a word to a bird, and a notch on the slate at every twelfth. They are not Tovashi words. 'My grandmother counted by it. Nobody knows what the words are.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, rhyme_known). }
  }
  Topic coombe_count with coombe "Ask Coombe about the count" when true once {
    Says "'A fifth down since 76,' says Coombe. 'And the eels with them.' He nods west, at the pillar of light over the far fog. 'They steer by that, and it is dimmer. Something is standing in it, up above the cloud. I cannot see what.'".
  }
  Person lio "Lio" at lio_house {
    Role "a young fisher of the Weirs". Ancestry human. Peaceable. Pronouns he. Manner cheerful.
    Sells lio_plate_kind for 40 coin from 1.
  }
  Kind lio_plate_kind "a speaking plate from the Old Landing" is treasure worth 40 weighing 1
    described "A thin stillglass plate, slimy from the lake. A stylus drawn along it gives voices: a count of people laid in the light, and how many woke.".
  Topic lio_plate with lio "Ask Lio about the plate he found" when true once {
    Says "'On the steps of the Landing, last winter, when the water went down,' says Lio. 'There is a door in the hall nobody has opened. Two Quell buyers want the plate and a monk from Stairhead wants it more.' He grins. 'Forty crowns, and it is yours, and I will show you the safe line across the mud for nothing.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, safe_line). }
  }
  Discovery safe_line "The safe line across the Landing mud: a path from post to post, wide of the circle where the lake turns and goes down.".

  // The Landing: the crane-priests' temple, older than the fall; its calendar; the Throat.
  Observe mud_scene at mudflat when true "A flat of black mud, knee-deep and sucking. Far out, beyond the steps, the lake surface turns slowly in a wide circle around a point where the water sinks.".
  Hazard throat "the Throat" means "Deal (3d6) physical damage to ally unless strength save against (14).".
  Rule throat_takes when tookWay(?c, wade) and company(?c) and not knows(?c, safe_line) and not throated(?c) says "Off the line, the mud goes soft, and the turning water has you by the legs." {
    Assert strikes(throat, ?c). Assert throated(?c). }
  Relation throated(group).
  Rule throat_clears when throated(?c) and not tookWay(?c, wade) { Retract throated(?c). }
  Observe hall_scene_l at landing_hall when true "A roofless hall of fitted limestone, and a carved wall black with lake slime.".
  Thing calendar_wall "the carved wall" at landing_hall {
    State slimed "The carved wall is black with slime; you can see there is carving under it, and no more.".
    State scrubbed "The wall is scrubbed: a calendar of crane arrivals and eel runs, year on year, two hundred years of it, cut by people who had no letters, only signs.".
    Change scrub "Scrub the carved wall clean" from slimed to scrubbed.
  }
  Observe calendar_read at landing_hall when state(calendar_wall, scrubbed) "The last entry, after two hundred years of cranes and eels, is a sign you have seen on every Seridane door: the hour. Beside it, the sign for falling, and the ninth crane count of that year. The hour fell out of the sky in the month of the ninth count. Nobody asked for it." teaches hour_fell.
  Observe side_scene at landing_side when true "A sealed room of the first Seridane: voice-plates racked by the dozen, and a smell of the lake.".
  Discovery first_holdings "The first holdings, on the Landing's plates: more of the first people laid in the light died than lived; the crane-priests counted both and kept on.".
  Thing landing_plates "the racked plates" at landing_side {
    State racked "Dozens of voice-plates stand racked in the side room.".
    State played "One of the racked plates has been played; it stands a little out of line.".
    Change play_landing "Draw a stylus along one of the racked plates" from racked to played needing stylus.
  }
  Observe landing_played at landing_side when state(landing_plates, played) "A priest counts people into the light, and the next day counts how many still breathe. Most days the second number is smaller." teaches first_holdings.

  // The cliff: three hundred name-tombs; Lirem's angle-books in niche 211; the fourth Dane's empty tomb.
  Observe cliff_foot_scene at cliff_foot when true "The west wall of the gorge, two kilometres of sandstone cut with square niches from twenty metres up to a hundred and twenty. Most of the stairs have fallen. Above about ninety metres the face is turning clear, and the upper niches look like windows.".
  Observe lower_scene at lower_niches when true "Niches the size of a small room, each with a stone bench, an umber-sealed jar, and a name carved with its syllable and month.".
  Discovery tombs_read "Read in order of birth, the cliff's names are three hundred syllables of the Voice.".
  Observe tombs_learn at lower_niches when not benighted(party) and not knows(party, tombs_read) "The names run in birth order along the cliff, and each has its month's syllable cut beside it." teaches tombs_read.
  Observe niche_scene at niche_211 when true "A niche inside the new glass, lit through its own walls. On the bench lie twelve slate tablets ruled in tables of angles.".
  Kind angle_books_kind "Lirem's angle-books" is treasure worth 500 weighing 6
    described "Twelve slate tablets of light geometry: the depth of the Late Sun against the angle of the light at every lamp-chamber, channel and point of the plateau. Also a manual for bridging.".
  Item angle_books "Lirem's angle-books" is angle_books_kind at niche_211.
  Observe dane_scene at dane_tomb when not reanchored(fourth_dane) "A niche like the others, its bench bare. A name is carved over it, and your eye goes past it every time, as if there were nothing there.".
  Observe dane_scene_anchored at dane_tomb when reanchored(fourth_dane) "The fourth Dane's tomb: his name, which everyone now can read, and fresh walnuts on the bench.".
  Entity fourth_dane: scenery "the fourth Dane's reign".
  Relation reanchored(entity).
  Discovery dane_name "The fourth Dane's name, taken by touch from his own keystone in the Quarried Gallery.".
  Action speak_name(actor: group, site: place) "Speak the fourth Dane's name at his tomb" {
    Description "A quarried moment re-anchored by its own name, spoken where it was kept.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, dane_tomb) and knows(actor, dane_name)
      and not reanchored(fourth_dane).
    Time 1 minute.
    On success { Assert reanchored(fourth_dane). }
    Result "You say it. Nothing happens to the stone; but the name is there over the bench when you look, and you wonder how you ever missed it.".
  }
}
data/adventures/quiet-in-the-sky/country:
Module larum "The Quiet in the Sky" {
  Description "Larum, a hamlet under a high pass that for nine hundred years has heard the warrior dead fighting in the snow above it, and has not heard them for forty days; and over the pass, in Ysgard, the Field where they fought, and Halt, the town of shields they have built in the quiet around the one of them who did not get up.".

  // ── The two countries ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // Larum lies in Imbar, in no plane, as the generated countries do: the valley road comes up from the march into the
  // hamlet, and above it the Pass goes up into the White. Over the White is Ysgard, Orsino's frigid outer plane: its
  // Field runs five miles east to west between Morrowhall and Evenhall, with Halt in the middle of it, the Scrapes under
  // its southern lip, the Old Ice to the north and the Teeth to the south-west. The Coming-in stands where the White
  // gives out, on the Field's southern rim.
  Place larum_country "Larum and the Pass" is region.
  Place valley "the Larum valley" is wilderness within larum_country at 0, 2.
  Place larum "Larum" is settlement within larum_country at 1, 2.
  Place pass "the Larum Pass" is wilderness within larum_country at 2, 1.
  Initially Assert terrain(larum_country, mountain).

  // Ysgard is the world's, one plane for every author (data/imbar): the Field is a region of this work's own within it.
  Place field_country "the Field" is region within outer_ysgard.
  Initially Assert terrain(field_country, frost).
  Entity plane_ysgard: law "the law of Ysgard".
  Initially Assert law(field_country, plane_ysgard).
  Place coming_in_site "the Coming-in" is site within field_country at 3, 4.
  Place field "the Field" is wilderness within field_country at 3, 3.
  Place halt "Halt" is settlement within field_country at 3, 2.
  Place morrow_height "the Morrow height" is site within field_country at 5, 2.
  Place even_height "the Even height" is site within field_country at 1, 2.
  Place scrapes "the Scrapes" is site within field_country at 4, 4.
  Place old_ice "the Old Ice" is wilderness within field_country at 3, 0.
  Place teeth "the Teeth" is wilderness within field_country at 1, 4.

  // ── Larum ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place hark_house "the Hark" is building within larum.
  Place hark_upper "the rooms over the Hark" is level within hark_house.
  Place bakehouse_b "Nance Pellett's bakehouse" is building within larum.
  Place guide_house_b "the guide's house" is building within larum.
  Place larum_chapel_b "Larum chapel" is building within larum.

  Place march_road "the valley road below Larum" is room within valley at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place larum_street "Larum street" is room within larum at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place hark "the Hark's taproom" is room within hark_house at 1, 0.
  Place hark_loft "the loft over the Hark" is room within hark_upper at 1, 0.
  Place bakehouse "Nance Pellett's bakehouse" is room within bakehouse_b at 2, 1.
  Place guide_house "the guide's house" is room within guide_house_b at 0, 1.
  Place larum_chapel "Larum chapel" is room within larum_chapel_b at 1, 2.
  Place pass_foot "the foot of the Pass" is room within pass at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Place the_white "the White" is room within pass at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place limbo "nowhere" is room within valley at 9, 9.

  Passage valley_road "the valley road" is road between march_road and larum_street taking 30 minutes.
  Passage hark_door "the Hark's door" is door between larum_street and hark.
  Passage hark_stair "the stair to the loft" is stair between hark and hark_loft.
  Passage bake_door "the bakehouse door" is door between larum_street and bakehouse.
  Passage guide_door "Jory Whitlock's door" is door between larum_street and guide_house.
  Passage chapel_door_l "the chapel door" is door between larum_street and larum_chapel.
