  Passage pass_path "the path up to the Pass" is path between larum_street and pass_foot taking 40 minutes.
  Passage white_path "the way up into the White" is path between pass_foot and the_white taking 1 hour.

  // ── Ysgard: the Coming-in ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place cleeve_booth_b "the Teller's booth" is building within coming_in_site.
  Place snow_gate "the Coming-in" is room within coming_in_site at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place cleeve_booth "the Teller's booth" is room within cleeve_booth_b at 1, 0.
  // The way through the White is a line of cairns that is only a way to those who can find it.
  Passage cairn_way "the cairns through the White" is path between the_white and snow_gate taking 1 hour hidden until white_known.
  Passage booth_flap "the booth's flap" is doorway between snow_gate and cleeve_booth.

  // ── Ysgard: the Field ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place field_south "the southern Field" is room within field at 1, 2 outdoors.
  Place lathe_ford "the ford of the Lathe" is room within field at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place the_clear "the Clear" is room within field at 2, 1 outdoors.
  Place east_slope "the foot of the Morrow height" is room within field at 3, 1 outdoors.
  Place west_slope "the foot of the Even height" is room within field at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Place field_north "the northern Field" is room within field at 2, 0 outdoors.
  Passage down_from_gate "the track down from the Coming-in" is track between snow_gate and field_south taking 30 minutes.
  Passage lathe_way "the way to the Lathe" is path between lathe_ford and the_clear taking 20 minutes.
  Passage clear_north "the long slope north" is path between the_clear and field_north taking 40 minutes.
  Passage east_way "the battle-line east" is path between the_clear and east_slope taking 30 minutes.
  Passage west_way "the battle-line west" is path between lathe_ford and west_slope taking 30 minutes.

  // ── Ysgard: Halt ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place oven_b "the Oven" is building within halt.
  Place truce_b "the Truce" is building within halt.
  Place halt_cross "Trophy Row" is room within halt at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place the_ring "the ring of spears" is room within halt at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place banner_lanes "the banner lanes" is room within halt at 2, 1 outdoors.
  Place oven "the Oven" is room within oven_b at 0, 1.
  Place truce "the Truce" is room within truce_b at 1, 2.
  Passage south_lane "the lane in from the south" is path between field_south and halt_cross taking 30 minutes.
  Passage ford_lane "the lane down to the Lathe" is path between halt_cross and lathe_ford taking 20 minutes.
  Passage ring_lane "the way to the ring" is path between halt_cross and the_ring taking 2 minutes.
  Passage banner_way "the banner lanes" is path between halt_cross and banner_lanes taking 3 minutes.
  Passage oven_mouth "the Oven's mouth" is doorway between halt_cross and oven.
  Passage truce_hatch "the Truce's hatch" is crawl between halt_cross and truce.
  Passage halt_east "the road east out of Halt" is path between banner_lanes and east_slope taking 40 minutes.

  // ── Ysgard: the halls ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place morrowhall_b "Morrowhall" is building within morrow_height.
  Place evenhall_b "Evenhall" is building within even_height.
  Place morrow_yard "Morrowhall's yard" is room within morrow_height at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place morrow_hall "Morrowhall" is room within morrowhall_b at 1, 0.
  Place marshal_room "the Marshal's room" is room within morrowhall_b at 2, 0.
  Place even_court "Evenhall's court" is room within even_height at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place even_hall "Evenhall" is room within evenhall_b at 0, 0.
  Place forge "the forge of Evenhall" is room within evenhall_b at 0, 1.
  Passage morrow_climb "the road up the Morrow height" is road between east_slope and morrow_yard taking 30 minutes.
  Passage morrow_doors "Morrowhall's doors" is door between morrow_yard and morrow_hall.
  Passage marshal_door "the door behind the high seat" is door between morrow_hall and marshal_room.
  Passage even_climb "the road up the Even height" is road between west_slope and even_court taking 30 minutes.
  Passage even_doors "Evenhall's doors" is door between even_court and even_hall.
  Passage forge_arch "the arch to the forge" is arch between even_hall and forge.

  // ── Ysgard: the Scrapes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place scrapes_mouth "the mouth of the Scrapes" is room within scrapes at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place warren "the warren" is room within scrapes at 1, 0 underground.
  Place edith_nook "a nook behind the banners" is room within scrapes at 2, 0 underground.
  Passage scrapes_path "the path along the ice-lip" is path between field_south and scrapes_mouth taking 15 minutes.
  Passage warren_crawl "the crawl into the warren" is crawl between scrapes_mouth and warren.
  Passage nook_way "a gap behind the banners" is crawl between warren and edith_nook hidden until nook_known.

  // ── Ysgard: the Old Ice ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place ice_foot "the foot of the Old Ice" is room within old_ice at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Place ice_stair "the ice stair" is room within old_ice at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place sitters_cave "the Sitters' cave" is room within old_ice at 1, 0 underground.
  Passage ice_approach "the way onto the Old Ice" is path between field_north and ice_foot taking 30 minutes.
  Passage ice_steps "the steps cut in the ice" is steps between ice_foot and ice_stair taking 30 minutes.
  Passage cave_mouth "a mouth in the blue ice" is tunnel between ice_stair and sitters_cave hidden until sitters_known.

  // ── Ysgard: the Teeth ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place teeth_path "the path under the Teeth" is room within teeth at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Place wolf_ledge "the wolves' ledge" is room within teeth at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place high_cairn "the cairn on the highest Tooth" is room within teeth at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Passage teeth_track "the track to the Teeth" is track between field_south and teeth_path taking 1 hour.
  Passage ledge_climb "the scramble up to the ledge" is path between teeth_path and wolf_ledge taking 20 minutes.
  Passage tooth_climb "the climb to the highest Tooth" is path between wolf_ledge and high_cairn taking 30 minutes
    opening when not at(wolves, wolf_ledge) or not able(wolves) or tolerates(wolves, party) "Three white wolves stand across the foot of the climb with their heads low.".
}
Module larum "The Quiet in the Sky" {
  // ── What a company grows by here ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // Experience for what is made, carried, learned and decided; not for what is killed. Killing is cheap up here.
  Milestone m_white "found the cairns through the White" worth 100 when knows(party, white_known).
  Milestone m_up "stood on the Field alive" worth 100 when cameUp(party).
  Milestone m_bread "carried the Mother up through the White, and made Grimbold's bread rise" worth 300 when breadRisen(grimbold).
  Milestone m_ford "brought Mab Treloar and Ansel Haverlock to the ford with nothing in their hands" worth 250 when paired(mab).
  Milestone m_wedding "saw the first marriage in Ysgard" worth 250 when wedded(mab).
  Milestone m_song "gave Wystan Hollins a peace to sing" worth 300 when songMade(wystan).
  Milestone m_runners "won the Runners a bench" worth 250 when runnersSeated(cuddy).
  Milestone m_strike "showed the Runners they could say no" worth 200 when runnersStrike(cuddy).
  Milestone m_sitters "found the Sitters under the Old Ice" worth 150 when knows(party, sitters_known) and visitedBefore(sitters_cave).
  Milestone m_tabula "beat Aulus at Tabula" worth 200 when tabulaWon(party).
  Milestone m_sitters_down "brought the Sitters down to Halt" worth 250 when sittersDown(aulus).
  Milestone m_law "learned what a living hand does in Ysgard" worth 300 when knows(party, living_kills).
  Milestone m_wound "read the wound that killed Halvard Eld" worth 150 when knows(party, wound_read).
  Milestone m_edith "found Edith Marl" worth 200 when knows(party, edith_named).
  Milestone m_edith_home "took Edith Marl home down the Pass" worth 250 when edithHome(edith).
  Milestone m_jory "told Jory Whitlock" worth 300 when joryTold(jory).
  Milestone m_jory_met "brought Jory Whitlock up to his son" worth 200 when joryMet(jory).
  Milestone m_ned_home "found Ned Whitlock a place at the Oven" worth 150 when nedHome(ned).
  Milestone m_grave "gave Halvard Eld a grave" worth 400 when toroldMourned(torold).
  Milestone m_cairn "read the name on the highest Tooth" worth 150 when knows(party, halvard_cut).
  Milestone m_truth "told the Field the truth" worth 300 when truthSpoken(field_country).
  Milestone m_hild "gave Hild Varley a reason to be brave" worth 300 when hildResolved(hild).
  Milestone m_bronze "brought up bronze from the bottom of the Clear" worth 150 when knows(party, cassian_known) or holding(party, bronze_find).
  Milestone m_plough "set Gorm Hallett making a plough" worth 150 when ploughMade(gorm).
  Milestone m_halt "saw Halt chosen" worth 600 when outcomeHalt(field_country).
}
data/adventures/quiet-in-the-sky/kinds.k:
Module larum "The Quiet in the Sky" {
  // ── The things of the country: what is carried, sold, bought and given ────────────────────────────────────────────
  Kind sheepskin_kind "a sheepskin coat" like cloak worth 4 weighing 2 described "A heavy coat of fleece turned inward, greasy and smelling of sheep and peat, that comes to your knees. Larum makes them for the guides and the pickers' trade. It keeps the cold of the Field off twice as long.".
  Kind crossbow_find "a crossbow of the last century" is treasure worth 6 weighing 2 described "A heavy crossbow with its string gone and its stock carved with a little running fox, from the wars of a hundred years ago. There is a notch in the stock for every man it killed, and they all got up.".
  Kind mail_find "a shirt of rusted mail" is treasure worth 8 weighing 4 described "A mail shirt torn half off its wearer, the rings rusted together into a stiff sheet, from somewhere in the middle of history.".
  Kind horn_find "a dented war-horn" is treasure worth 10 weighing 1 described "A war-horn of yellowed ox-horn bound with brass, dented, with a mouthpiece worn thin. When you blow it, it still sounds, a long raw note that makes every dead head within earshot turn.".
  Kind banner_find "a frozen banner" is treasure worth 5 weighing 1 described "A banner of a host nobody remembers, stiff as a board with frost: a black bird on a field that was once gold.".
  Kind bronze_find "a bronze blade from the bottom of the Clear" is treasure worth 30 weighing 1 described "A leaf-shaped sword of bronze, green as a beech leaf, its hilt bound in something that was leather a thousand years ago. It has lain at the very bottom of the Clear since before there were halls.".
  Kind challenge_kind "Ansel Haverlock's challenge" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A sheet of something that was once a banner's lining, folded small, in a beautiful old upright hand: TO MISTRESS MAB TRELOAR OF THE MORROW FOOT, ANSEL FENWICK OF EVENHALL SENDS GREETING AND CHALLENGES HER TO MEET HIM AT THE FORD OF THE LATHE AT NOON, WITHOUT ARMS, BEFORE WITNESSES, ON A MATTER THAT HAS WAITED TWO HUNDRED YEARS. The last word has been written over several times.".
  Kind plain_kind "Ansel Haverlock's letter" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A scrap of banner lining in charcoal, smudged, crossed out in three places: MAB. I DO NOT WANT THE WAR. I WANT TO SEE YOU WITHOUT IT. AT THE FORD AT NOON. I WILL COME WITH NOTHING IN MY HANDS. A.".
  Kind halvard_ballad_kind "the Ballad of Halvard Eld" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A penny sheet, grey paper, a woodcut of a man with a sword in each fist and a town burning behind him, and twenty-two verses in a jogging metre: how Halvard Eld, captain of the Free Company of the Hook, put Wendmere of the fullers to the torch, man, wife and child, and laughed; how he died at the siege of Coldharbour with nine men round him; and how he came in out of the snow into Evenhall and was champion in five years, the fastest ever. The last verse says that Halvard will fight on the Field till the stars go out. Somebody has written under it, small: and he'll never be sorry.".
  Kind mother_kind "a little crock of Nance's Mother" is gear worth 0 weighing 1 described "A little brown crock with a cloth tied over the top, heavy and faintly warm, and when you hold it to your ear, very faintly, it ticks and sighs: something in there is alive and working.".
  Kind tobacco_kind "a twist of Larum leaf" is gear worth 1 weighing 0 described "A twist of dark tobacco in a screw of paper, from the shelf behind the Hark's bar. Up on the Field it is worth more than gold.".
  Kind brindle_kind "a slab of roast Brindle" is gear worth 0 weighing 1 described "A slab of dark roast ox the size of a book, wrapped in a cloth, still warm from the spit. In the morning, the hall says, there will be no gap in Brindle where it came from.".
}
data/adventures/quittance/afterwords.kyr:
Module quittance "Quittance" {
  Description "What became of them: in the last minutes before midnight on Reckoning, the small adventures are told over, one chapter to a thread, according to what the company did, so that the ending closes on a city and not on a Hall.".

  Chapter aw_tolliver "At Tolliver's" when watch(clock) >= 1244 and bk_flue_fixed(party) "The oven in Tolliver's bakehouse draws like a church now, to the Ordinance, with a new flue and an inspector's stamp, and the bread is exactly as good as it was. Gwen Tolliver does not understand why she weeps at the first loaf. She says it is the heat.".
  Chapter aw_tolliver_alive "At Tolliver's" when watch(clock) >= 1244 and keeper(brick) "The oven in Tolliver's bakehouse is the warmest thing in the Brickfields tonight, and Gwen has put the old woman's chair in front of the door so that she can see the sparks. A loaf has been set aside for the brigades, both of them, in a basket with two ribbons.".
  Chapter aw_pip "On Pip's Stair" when watch(clock) >= 1244 and pt_saved(party) "On the top landing of the tenement in Salt Lane, the door is open the full width of a hand, and in the tin on the floor a red coal is alive and has a name. Pip is asleep against it with her cheek on the lid. Her grandmother is not asleep, and is looking at you as people look who do not mean to be thanked.".
  Chapter aw_pip_lost "On Pip's Stair" when watch(clock) >= 1244 and pt_lost(party) "On the top landing the door is shut, and there is a tin inside it with ash in it. Nobody in the Wards will say it to you. Pip is keeping her gran's chair warm with her own back, and has started, quietly, in the way of children, to tell people it was never lit.".
  Chapter aw_hob "The Last Round" when watch(clock) >= 1244 and (ll_howPension(hob) or ll_howPlace(hob) or ll_howFinish(hob) or ll_howHearth(hob)) "Hob Tansy is sitting on the Stokers' Steps with his pole across his knees, not lighting anything, listening to the cold-lamps hum on their brackets. 'It's a decent noise,' he says to nobody. 'I'd not say it was a bad noise.' He is waiting for dusk the way a man waits for a train he has already decided not to take.".
  Chapter aw_fusby "Mr Teague's Parrot" when watch(clock) >= 1244 and wk_testified(party) "In a cage on the sideboard of a house on Surety Hill a parrot is repeating a sentence he has been given by the Residuary Office of Quittance in writing: 'Fish, fish, fish-bone, three turns left.' No one in the house knows why it has been entered in the Rolls of the city as the longest-serving witness in its history. The widow who feeds him does so with a certain extra courtesy.".
  Chapter aw_lovers "Surety Hill" when watch(clock) >= 1244 and (sd_end_honest(party) or sd_end_declined(party)) "On the Belvedere, with the city lit below them for the first time in forty years, a surveyor of the Guild and a young man in the Phoenix's blue are sitting with their feet through the balustrade, not touching, discussing a flue. The distance between their hands on the stone is a hand's breadth, and one of them has certainly measured it.".
  Chapter aw_lovers_gone "A Page of the Roll" when watch(clock) >= 1244 and (sd_end_exiled(party) or sd_end_apart(party) or sd_end_forged(party)) "There is a gap in the Surveyors' Guild's long table where a rope used to hang. The clerk, Mr Tinniswood, has pinned a neat card to the empty hook: PROCEEDED ELSEWHERE. UNDECLINED. He has put a pencil beside it, a good one, for when she wants it back.".
  Chapter aw_tench "The Clerk's Chair" when watch(clock) >= 1244 and qu_nerve(party) >= 2 "In the cellars of the Old Exchange, at a desk at the far end of a long vault, a young man in sleeve-guards is calling a roll. He is not calling it fast. Behind him, in a line that has stopped being a line, the dead are going out past him one at a time into a stair of warm air, and he is saying good night to each of them by name, and when he runs out of names he goes on, because it is his chair.".
  Chapter aw_cray "In Annuitants' Row" when watch(clock) >= 1244 and (an_status(party) == 2 or an_status(party) == 5) "At the almshouse the seven have been given the best chairs and a second kettle. A hundred-and-thirty-one-year-old woman, aged nineteen, has taken off her shawls to pour the tea, and nobody, including the man from the Sovereign who is sitting in the corner with his hat on his knee, remarks upon it.".
  Chapter aw_garrity "On the Whitewash" when watch(clock) >= 1244 and arc(garrity) >= 1 and (arc(dree) >= 1 or regard(lamprey) >= 2) "In the fire-house yard the line of whitewash between the Phoenix and the Lamprey has been scrubbed out by someone in the night with a stiff brush, and nobody is willing to say who. Captain Garrity and Captain Dree are standing on the place where it was, at opposite ends of it, not speaking, with a single bucket between them.".
  Chapter aw_kitty "Under the Sluice-tap" when watch(clock) >= 1244 and keeper(reach) "A girl who is officially a barge-load of cold-lamps is helping with the pies at the Sluice-tap, with her sleeves rolled and a smear of flour on her cheek. The lightermen have put a chair by the hearth and a notice over it in chalk: KEPT.".
}

data/adventures/quittance/endings.kyr:
Module quittance "Quittance" {
  Description "How Quittance ends: six ways, and which the company came to.".

  // Endings are tried in the order written; the particular before the general. The Burning and the Slaying are done
  // at the moment they happen. The rest are reached at Reckoning midnight (watch 1248), on what the city has paid.
  Chapter reckoning_midnight "Quittance" when watch(clock) >= 1248 "Midnight on the Cinderwall. The clerk from the Hall of the Five comes out with the Receipt on a board and a hook on a pole, and the crowd, which has not been told to be quiet, is.".


  // ── What resolving it is worth ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Milestone m_candle_warned "warned Candlewick Court" worth 100 when candlewickWarned(party).
  Milestone m_candle_stopped "turned the torchmen from Candlewick Court" worth 200 when candlewickSaved(party).
  Milestone m_gasket_warned "warned Gasket Yard" worth 100 when gasketWarned(party).
  Milestone m_gasket_stopped "turned Skelter's men from Gasket Yard" worth 200 when gasketSaved(party).
  Milestone m_tables "found what the Tables were hiding" worth 100 when knows(party, d_tables_paradox).
  Milestone m_book "got Skelter's rent-book" worth 150 when knows(party, d_prewitt_appoints).
  Milestone m_return "learned the Return" worth 150 when returnLearned(party).
  Milestone m_prewitt "turned Sedley Prewitt" worth 400 when prewittTurned(party).
  Milestone m_fire "spoke with the Fire" worth 300 when fireHeard(party).
  Milestone m_motion "carried the motion before the Five" worth 300 when motionCarried(city).
  Milestone m_lit "lit four of the wards" worth 300 when wardsLit(city) >= 4.

  Ending end_burning "The Burning" when fireWrathful(party) "The Fire does not shout. It stands up out of its hearth, which is the size of a threshing-floor, and keeps standing after the roof of the hall has stopped being a roof. You do not see the rest of it. You hear the glass of the Sunk City begin, all together, to remember being soft, a long ticking like a street of clocks being wound the wrong way; the floor of the Exchange goes from warm to too warm to stand on between one step and the next. By the time you reach the surface Policy Row is a street of lit windows, and then of windows that are only light. The brigades come out and stand in rows, Phoenix and Lamprey, on either side of a line of whitewash, and look at the plates over the doors, and cannot decide whose it is. Quittance burns for three days. Afterward the survivors are counted, in Gate Plaza, by clerks who have saved their ledgers, and the number is nearer the Tables than anyone had hoped, and more than anyone could bear. The Receipt is never found. It turns out there was nothing, after all, to hang it on.".
  Ending end_slaying "The Slaying" when fireSlain(party) "It goes out slowly, as large fires do: first the red, then the white, then the long grey breath of ash in the Hearth Below. There is a moment when the glass walls of the Sunk City tick, all at once, like a hundred clocks stopping. Then there is nothing in the city that is warm that has not been made so by somebody's hand. That winter no hearth in Quittance will light, not the Wards' nor the Phoenix's, nor the little red coal in Hearn House; they will burn coke and go on being cold; the cold-lamps will glow, and be glad of it, and be nothing else. The Receipt is hung at midnight on the Cinderwall as the Founders directed, and it is blank, and the city looks at it and understands, a good deal late, what had been signed. Nobody in Quittance will ever be burned again. It is considered by the Offices to be an acceptable loss.".
  Ending general_average "General Average" when watch(clock) >= 1248 and fireTermAverage(party) and motionCarried(city) "On the afternoon of Reckoning the Cinder Ward is emptied, street by street, by brigades of both Offices, who have been issued, for the occasion, the same bucket and are each trying to be seen not to carry it for the other. Three thousand people sit on the Cinderwall with their bundles and their cats and watch it, in daylight, in good order, with pie. At the stroke of five a man from the Phoenix puts a taper to the well-head. The First Flue breathes in. The Cinder Ward burns, quickly and cleanly, in an hour, and the Fire, which is not in a hurry, takes what it is owed and nothing it is not; and at midnight the Receipt, hung on its hook, is white from edge to edge, and says, in a notary's capitals, QUIT. The Five Offices meet on the Thursday. They are to pay out for three thousand houses, pro rata, in perpetuity; the Chairman of the Residuary, who has the sandwiches, is heard to say that he has never before seen the Tables come out to the farthing. Nobody died. The Providence's Chairman asks, twice, whether the pie can be claimed as a loss.".
  Ending hospitality "The Hospitality Renewed" when watch(clock) >= 1248 and fireTerms(party) and (fireTermKeeper(party) or fireTermNight(party)) "At midnight the Receipt goes up on the Cinderwall as it always did, and it is not blank. It is the colour of a good tea, and it says, in a hand nobody in the city has seen for ninety-four years, RECEIVED, WITH THANKS. The Fire has its terms. A hearth is kept in the Hall of the Five from that winter on, in the place where the plaster was, and a Hearthkeeper sits by it who is not a Hearn. Once a year, on the night of Reckoning, the whole of Quittance lights a fire at once, and nobody is allowed to put it out until morning; and the Offices, who do not believe a word of it, discover that the year's claims on that night are never more than they can pay. The inner wards keep their gas. On Policy Row, on the first of the month, the housemaids set out the saucers of salt as they always did, and now somebody says thank you for them.".
  Ending quittance_best "Quittance" when watch(clock) >= 1248 and wardsLit(city) >= 4 and motionCarried(city) and prewittTurned(party) "The coals come home. All night they come, from every ward, in tins and pans and saucepans and a hearse, up Policy Row to the Exchange, and nobody counts them; the Five themselves carry the last of them down the cellar stair, in a line, in their good coats. At midnight on the Cinderwall the clerk hooks the Receipt, and it goes up white as the sun, and a boy who was never taught his letters reads it aloud to his mother. QUITTANCE. IN FULL. Sedley Prewitt resigns the Chief Underwriting in the morning, and spends the rest of his life, to the horror of the Phoenix, in the Bare Wards, keeping a hearth. His daughter inherits the pencils. The Smokeless Ordinance is amended in the spring by a clause that Cornelia Pettifer is understood to have drafted, which allows every household one fire, and one coal, and the Offices are rather surprised to find that premiums have never been lower. In the Bare Wards, they say, the fires are the same as they were. Only now the brigades come to them.".
  Ending quittance_contested "Quittance, Contested" when watch(clock) >= 1248 and wardsLit(city) >= 4 and motionCarried(city) "The coals come home, though not everyone is glad of it. Sedley Prewitt, who did not turn, sits in the Hall with his hands on the table and watches the Five carry them down; he does not stop them; he does not help. At midnight the Receipt goes up on the Cinderwall, and it is white, and says QUIT, and the crowd cheers, and the Chief Underwriter takes his hat and goes home on foot. There is an inquiry in the spring. The list is found, and produced, and nobody is hanged; a rent-collector is posted to a distant parish; the Phoenix issues a statement of profound regret, printed on the good paper. The Appointed Losses end, because they are no longer needed, and not because anyone is sorry. By summer a number of people are free to say that they always thought so.".
  Ending evacuated_loss "The Ward Without Its People" over end_lapse when burned(cinder_ward) and titheEvacuated(party) "At midnight the Cinder Ward burns with nobody in it, which the Wards have never seen. They watch from the Cinderwall, three thousand of them in rows with their bundles and their lamps, and the black chimney in the middle stands up through the light like the stalk of something. A child asks whether it is a fire or a funeral and is told that it is both, and to hold the cat. In the morning the Offices send a man with a ledger; the Chairman of the Residuary, who has been sitting on the Cinderwall all night with his sandwiches, tells him to write it down as a Total Loss, and then, after a moment, to write it down as a Loss Shared. The Receipt goes up pale pink. Nobody died. In the spring the Tables show the year's deaths by fire as three, all of them in the Brickfields, all of them insured.".
  Ending controlled_loss "The Controlled Loss" over end_lapse when burned(cinder_ward) "At midnight the Cinder Ward burns. It burns from the well-head outwards, and then all at once, and the black chimney in the middle of it stands up through the light like the stalk of something. The brigades are drawn up in the Brickfields, on the whitewash, with their pumps primed, protecting the marked; they watch. A man in a long grey coat is standing at the edge of the Ward with his hat in his hand. He does not move. He has not, you think, expected to be able to bear it, and is finding that he can. At midnight, on the Cinderwall, the Receipt goes up on its hook, and it is the colour of a rose. The city's fires, that year, are lower than at any time in the Tables. In the spring Sedley Prewitt receives the Order of the Sovereign Sun for his services to the public safety. You are paid, as agreed, by a clerk who does not look at you. Three thousand people go to live in the Brickfields with relatives, or in the Reach, or the Wards that are left. The Tables, which cannot show where anyone sleeps, record the year as the quietest on file.".
  Ending end_lapse "The Lapse" when watch(clock) >= 1248 "Midnight comes to the Cinderwall and the clerk hooks the Receipt, and it hangs there. It is blank. Not pale, not faint: blank, the clean white of a card nobody has written on. The crowd waits. A child asks if it is broken. The Offices' Chairmen look at one another, along the line, and the Chairman of the Sovereign, who is the oldest, takes out his watch and winds it. The Fire is not wrathful; it has been courteous for ninety-four years and is courteous now. In the cellars of the Old Exchange the red goes down to a thread, and the thread goes, and the warmth of the city goes after it, out through the stones like a tide. In the morning Quittance finds its hearths cold and its marks unmeaning, and the fires, that winter, are rare: the city does not burn, because there is nothing left in it that will light. The cold-lamps hum. The Offices are paid their premiums. By spring half of Quittance has moved to the country, and the Hen has a new sign, NOTHING GOES WRONG IN HERE, under which nobody asks the landlady whether she means it.".
}
data/adventures/quittance/hearth.kyr:
Module quittance "Quittance" {
  Description "The Hearth Night: what a lit ward looks like from the street, and the city on the nights it is allowed to be warm.".

  Observe lit_brick at brick_lane when coaled(brick) and keeper(brick) "A thread of smoke goes straight up from the bakery chimney, and another from the fire-house, and nobody has called the brigade. Along the terrace one window after another is yellow.".
  Observe lit_brick_lone at brick_lane when coaled(brick) and not keeper(brick) "A thread of smoke goes up from a chimney in the Brickfields, thin and alone, and every curtain on the street is twitching.".
  Observe lit_reach at mere_wharf when coaled(reach) and keeper(reach) "On every barge at the Mere Wharf somebody has a pan on, and the smell of frying drifts along the quay. The lightermen sing, badly, in rounds.".
  Observe lit_glass at foundry_row when coaled(glass) and keeper(glass) "Foundry Row is warm underfoot, and the stokers' wives have opened their windows. A line of lamps down the Row burns low and yellow, and from the shuttered furnaces comes a ticking, like a cooling kettle.".
  Observe lit_hill at hill_street when coaled(hill) and keeper(hill) "Up on Surety Hill a footman has come out on a step with a candle, not mark-insured, and is staring at it as at a cat that has done something clever.".
  Observe lit_mort at annuity_row when coaled(mort) and keeper(mort) "A small light burns in every cottage on Annuitants' Row. The old are sitting up to see it.".
  Observe lit_wards at salt_lane when coaled(wards) and keeper(wards) "Salt Lane is lit from end to end, every window, every grate, and the sound that comes down it is not quite singing. Someone is selling pie at midnight as if it were noon.".
  Observe city_warm at gate_plaza when wardsLit(city) >= 3 and hour(clock) >= 18 "The air in Gate Plaza is warmer than it was in the afternoon, and smells of woodsmoke. The brokers on the Stair have taken their hats off, though nobody seems to have told them to.".
  Observe city_warm_all at gate_plaza when wardsLit(city) >= 5 and hour(clock) >= 18 "All Quittance is warm. The Honest Bell, under the Arch, is humming very slightly, like a cat.".
  Observe arch_hum at arch_hall when wardsLit(city) >= 5 "The Honest Bell is humming. Mr Prest has stopped writing in the Roll and is looking up at it with his pen in the air.".
}
data/adventures/quittance/scenes.kyr:
Module quittance "Quittance" {
  Description "What each place of Quittance looks like, sounds like and costs.".

  // ── The approaches ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe arch_road_scene at arch_road when true "The road comes down off the fields to a city wall the colour of a good tea-cup, and every brick of it wears the same small brass plate: a bird, a fish, an open hand. Ahead the Declaration Arch stands over the road with a bell hung in its crown. A queue of carts waits in front of it with the patience of people who have all been told the same thing about premiums. Bills are pasted on the wall: INSURE YOURSELF BEFORE YOU ENTER. LAPSED POLICIES WILL NOT BE REMINDED.".
  Observe towpath_scene at towpath when true "A mud towpath along the tide-river, below the wall. Lighters nose into a stone water-stair a hundred yards on, where the wall drops its feet into the water and a customs-house pretends not to see.".
  Observe gap_path_scene at gap_path when true "The wall, on this side, is another wall: black, old, not brick but fused glass and slag laid in courses like loaves, and without a single plate on it. This is the Cinderwall. A gap the width of a handcart has been left in it, and through the gap you can smell cooking, and woodsmoke, which the signs on the other wall forbid.".
  Observe mort_road_scene at mort_road when true "A road of white gravel between yews, wide enough for a hearse and a mourner on either side. There is a hearse in the road already, drawn up, with a driver eating an onion.".

  // ── The Gate Quarter ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe arch_hall_scene at arch_hall when true "Under the Arch the road widens into a hall: counters, brass rails, and a clerk to every counter under a hundred-year-old painting of the Burning. The Honest Bell hangs in the vault above on a plain iron hook, a large, plain, dull bell, with a rope that nobody holds. It rings by itself, once, for a lie told under it. A sign: DECLARE YOUR GOODS. DECLARE YOUR PURPOSE. DECLARE YOUR INTENTIONS, IF YOU HAVE ANY.".
  Observe gate_plaza_scene at gate_plaza when true "Gate Plaza is a square of brokers, porters and people who have just been told what they owe. Every doorway has a plate over it, and every plate has a small rival plate beside it that is smaller. A man is selling mark-polish from a tray.".
  Observe hen_scene at hen_taproom when true "A low taproom smelling of beeswax and boiled ham, decorated with framed premiums: the first policy the landlord ever took out on the building, which burned; the second, which also burned; the third, framed in black. 'Nothing's ever gone wrong in here since,' says the sign. Underneath, in another hand: 'Yet.'".
  Observe booths_scene at booths when true "A tin arcade of booths, each with a clerk, a window and a rate card. You can insure a hat, a marriage, a day, a debt, a wager on a debt, or the prospect of an unforeseen event of whatever kind you can describe in less than eleven words. There is a queue at the booth marked FIRST NIGHT IN THE CITY.".
  Observe brokers_stair_scene at brokers_stair when true "Forty steps of worn limestone climb out of the Gate Quarter toward the Exchange. Brokers sit on them in the sun with their hats beside them like cats, shouting rates at nobody.".

  // ── Policy Row and the Exchange ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe row_scene at row_street when true "Policy Row is the widest street in Quittance and the only one that is entirely stone. The Offices face each other across it like families at a wedding: the Phoenix with its gilt bird, the Lamprey's black fish over a door that always seems wet, the Sovereign's sun, the Providence's open hand, and, squeezed between two of them like a cough, a door with an eye over it that says only RESIDUARY. Clerks go by in sleeve-guards, not looking at one another.".
  Observe exchange_scene at exchange_court when true "The court of the Old Exchange is paved in black glass that is not quite level. The Exchange itself is a stump: four arches and a plinth, preserved exactly as the Burning left them, with a rail round it and a notice, DO NOT PRESUME UPON THE FOUNDATIONS. To one side the Hall of the Five stands with its bronze doors open, and on its front, in letters of white fire gone the colour of old teeth, the Receipt: RECEIVED OF THE CITY OF QUITTANCE, THE SUM OF ITS PREMIUM, IN FULL. Not much of it can be read.".
  Observe exchange_bell at exchange_court when hour(clock) == 9 or hour(clock) == 16 "The Exchange bell rings, which is to say a boy in the arcade hits a brass pan with a spoon, and every clerk in the Row looks at his watch.".
  Observe slip_scene at slip_room when true "The Bell & Slip is the coffee-house where the adjusters sit, in boxes, like dogs at kennels. A great slate hangs over the fireplace on which the day's claims are chalked by a boy on a ladder with the particular expression of someone who has been allowed to hold a chisel. The coffee is awful; nobody ever says so. A waiter goes between the boxes crying 'Total loss! Total loss!' with a tray.".
  Observe phoenix_floor_scene at phoenix_floor when true "The Phoenix counting-floor is as high as a church and as quiet. A hundred clerks write in a hundred ledgers under a gilt bird the size of a sheep, with a glass lamp hanging from its beak. On the north wall, behind a rail, runs the longest chart you have ever seen: every house in Quittance, each a pin, each pin a colour, red for the last year's fires.".
  Observe prewitt_scene at prewitt_room when true "A room with a desk, a clock, one chair for visitors and a second, empty, with a woman's shawl folded on it that nobody has moved in six years. The window looks out over the Row and the stump of the Exchange. There are no pictures. There is one lamp, which is unlit.".
  Observe tables_scene at tables_room when true "The Tables Room is a long, warm, low room lit by cold-lamps, lined with the bound Tables of ninety-four years: columns of houses and fires and deaths, ruled by hand in a clerk's three inks. At the far end is a desk, a stool, and a stack of paper on which someone has been drawing the same two curves over and over.".
  Observe hall_scene at hall_five when true "The Hall of the Five is a great plain chamber with five chairs on a dais, one for each Office, and a sixth, empty, stool-sized, beside them that is dusted weekly and sat in by no one. The floor is black glass. Behind the dais, the wall is bare plaster, and where a hearth would be there is a hearth-shaped patch that has been plastered smooth.".
  Observe provid_scene at provid_counter when true "The Providence is the cheerful Office: accident, illness, plate-glass, the loss of a limb, a daughter's elopement. The counter is covered in leaflets with pictures of men falling off ladders in a jaunty and confident manner.".

  // ── The Brickfields ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe brick_lane_scene at brick_lane when true "Brick Lane is the respectable middle of the city: red terraces, black railings, a window-box on every sill and a mark over every door that has been polished within the week. Everybody is somebody's client. A woman sweeps her step with the air of someone who would be dismissed for not doing so.".
  Observe mark_street_scene at mark_street when true "Mark Street is the model street of the Brickfields: twenty-two houses in a row, each with its plate level with its neighbour's, so that the whole terrace looks as though it has been signed. Number Nine's plate is a gilt bird. The two doors either side of it are fish.".
  Observe nine_yard_scene at nine_yard when true "A back yard with a pump, a washing-line and a coal-hole. The wall is high, and there is a ladder lying where it was put down.".
  Observe drill_yard_scene at drill_yard when true "A cobbled yard between the two brigades' fire-houses, one blue, one black. At dawn they drill here, side by side, glaring, on a line of whitewash neither will be seen to cross. The rest of the day it is a place where the young men of both lean on their buckets and exchange remarks about each other's mothers.".
  Observe engine_scene at engine_room when true "A long shed of brass and hose and polished boots. The pump is a steam-engine on wheels, painted blue, with a gilt bird on the funnel. A rack of leather helmets, each with a name chalked inside.".
  Observe tolliver_scene at tolliver_shop when true "Tolliver's is warm and smells so entirely of bread that you stop for a moment, in the doorway, on the step. A counter, a till, loaves in baskets, and a framed certificate: THE PHOENIX FIRE OFFICE, THIS PREMISES INSPECTED AND FOUND SOUND, 1319. The date has been corrected, in ink, in a different hand, to 1320, and then to 1321.".
  Observe bakehouse_scene at bakehouse when true "A hot brick room with a great black oven in its back wall, bigger than a cart, banked and breathing. Over its mouth is cut in the stone, very worn, a line you cannot read from here.".
  Observe dyers_alley_scene at dyers_alley when true "A narrow alley that smells of verdigris and hot tin. Dye-works and die-works stand wall to wall, so that the gutters run in two colours and the house-fronts are dappled with the spill from both.".
  Observe gedge_scene at gedge_back when true "A back-shop stacked with moulds, ingots, stamps and a fire-pot. On the wall hang a hundred cast plates: gilt birds, black fish, open hands, suns, each correct to the last feather and none of them quite round.".
  Observe pargeter_scene at pargeter_front when true "A narrow front room with a good clock, a bad carpet and a family portrait of nine Pargeters, every one of them in the brigade's blue. A black-fish mark has been nailed up on the sideboard, backwards, as a joke by someone who has since been spoken to.".

  // ── The Lightering Reach ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe lighter_stairs_scene at lighter_stairs when true "The Water-Stair: forty slick steps up out of the tide, with a tide-gauge painted on the wall and a lighterman at the top counting what comes off the boats against what his master says should. It is the city's second door, and it is notably more honest than the first.".
  Observe mere_wharf_scene at mere_wharf when true "The Mere Wharf is half a mile of timber and rope along a brown river, loud with gulls and winches. Lighters and barges lie three deep. A black fish is painted on every bollard. One barge is lying wrong: down by the head, with its decks awash, and a crowd looking at it in the way crowds look at something that will be someone's fault.".
  Observe salvor_scene at salvor_yard when true "The salvors' yard is where wrecks are put back together: spars, anchors, bits of cabin, a ship's bell, a stuffed gull. There is a smell of tar and wet rope, and a board with a tariff: SHARE OF A TOTAL LOSS, ONE THIRD; OF A SALVAGE, ONE HALF; OF A CASE YOU DO NOT ASK ABOUT, AS AGREED.".
  Observe skell_scene at skell_yard when true "A rival yard, shut off by a broken fence, with a sign that says SKELL & SONS in letters a size larger than any honest sign. A crew of eight is playing cards on a hatch. Something under a tarpaulin is dripping.".
  Observe cradle_scene at cradle when true "At the end of the quay the diving-bell hangs in a gantry: a bronze bell as big as a cart, with a seat inside and a bench, and a crank that three men turn. Nobody is using it. A sign says, in a fine-hand brigade capital, FOR THE USE OF THE LAMPREY & RIVER OFFICE ONLY, PROVIDED YOU BRING A WITNESS.".
  Observe sluice_scene at sluice_room when true "A dark, wet taproom, built round an iron sluice-wheel which turns slowly in the floor with the tide. The beer is brown and the pie is brown. Lightermen sit with their backs to the wall and talk without moving their lips.".
  Observe lamprey_floor_scene at lamprey_floor when true "The Lamprey & River counting-floor is hung with charts of the tide and models of ships in glass. Clerks in oilskin cuffs work under a black fish with a gold eye. It smells of wet paper. A notice: SHIPS LOST ARE NOT FORGOTTEN, MERELY PAID FOR.".
  Observe dree_scene at dree_room when true "A small cabin-like room with a porthole that looks out on a wall. Captain Dree's chair has been screwed to the floor against the possibility of a sudden swell.".
  Observe hold_scene at margaret_hold when true "Green water and brown light, boards groaning, crates floating up and bumping the beams. Cold-lamps lie in their straw by the hundred, each in a sealed glass jar, and a few of them are still alight.".

  // ── The Glass Quarter ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe foundry_scene at foundry_row when true "Foundry Row has been fireproofed, smokeproofed, noise-proofed and cheerfully sold. The furnaces are shuttered behind new brick, their chimneys capped and their heat piped away in iron to the Gasworks; the street is hot underfoot and dull. A stoker's wife stands at a window with her arms folded, looking at a cold hearth.".
  Observe gas_gate_scene at gas_gate when true "A tall iron gate with a rising sun on it and the words OUR COMFORT IS GUARANTEED in brass. Behind it a gasometer breathes like the lung of something asleep.".
  Observe gas_yard_scene at gas_yard when true "Coke in black hills. Rails. A shift of stokers black to the elbow, sitting on upturned buckets, not talking, while the foreman reads a notice to them in the voice of a man who has been told what it says.".
  Observe retort_scene at retort_house when true "The retort-house is a black cathedral of ovens, with a cat asleep on the warmest. The heat comes off the iron in waves, and for a moment you understand why a man might go on shovelling for thirty years.".
  Observe board_scene at board_room when true "A boardroom as large as a ballroom, wainscoted in the same dark wood as the Phoenix's and lit by one great gas chandelier which hisses. A map of the city on the table has a number on each ward: the premises now connected to the mains.".
  Observe lamp_front_scene at lamp_front when true "The Philosophical Lamp-house is part workshop and part shop. Cold-lamps stand in rows on shelves, in globes of green and white glass: lamps that give light and no heat, and no flame, and no smoke, and a faint hum, and which are by far the most expensive things in the room. A card: THE END OF FIRE.".
  Observe wynne_scene at wynne_lab when true "A laboratory crowded with glass retorts, jars, springs and notebooks. One wall is shelved with sealed glass jars, each with a tiny glow in it and a paper label in a woman's quick hand: NIGHT 41, NIGHT 42, NIGHT 43. The glows are not all the same colour.".
  Observe demo_scene at demo_hall when true "The demonstration hall is a plain room with a platform, rows of benches, and a floor of black stone so clean you could eat off it. A hundred cold-lamps hang from the ceiling on wires, dark.".
  Observe lamplighters_scene at lamplighters_hall when true "The Lamplighters' Hall is a long room hung with ladders and poles. Rows of brass tinder-boxes, each polished, each labelled with a name. A board lists the Rounds: Foundry One, Foundry Two, Tinkers, Stokers; the last name on each is Tansy.".
  Observe tinkers_scene at round_tinkers when true "Tinkers' Court is a dead end of shut workshops, each with its tin sign still hanging: a kettle, a spoon, a pair of bellows. In the dust on one shutter there is a child's handprint, at the height of a child who has been told not to. At the end, a lamp on a bracket, and below it a ladder rung worn bright by forty years of the same boot.".
  Observe steps_scene at round_steps when true "The Stokers' Steps are a flight of fifty brick stairs going down toward the Furnace Wharf, damp, and worn into a trough that is deeper on the left, where a century of men carried the bucket in the right hand. The last step is a hand's breadth shallower than the rest. Every stoker knows it; nobody has mended it. A lamp stands at the top and one at the bottom.".
  Observe glaziers_scene at round_glaziers when true "A narrow passage lined with glaziers' sheds, full of slabs of window-glass stacked on edge like cards. The lamp on the corner is out. A glow of some sort shows inside one of the sheds.".
  Observe furnace_wharf_scene at round_furnace when true "The Furnace Wharf: a river-edge of old iron, with the furnace-mouths bricked up and the bricks warm to the hand. Gulls sit along the top of the wall, exactly in a row, and they are all facing the same way.".

  // ── Lantern Hill ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe hill_scene at hill_street when true "Surety Hill: wide, quiet, shaded, as if the noise of the city had been bought out. The big houses have the plates of two or three Offices apiece, one above the other, like medals, and a footman at each door. From the top, the whole of Quittance lies spread below you with its flat roofs and chimneys, a very tidy ruin of brick.".
  Observe belvedere_scene at belvedere when true "A round terrace at the top of the hill, with a parapet worn smooth at elbow height by people who came up to look at the city and stayed to look at each other. The whole city is down there: the Row, the Reach, the grey rim of the Bare Wards and, where the Exchange stands, a faint wobble of heat in the air even in winter.".
  Observe hearn_parlour_scene at hearn_parlour when true "A parlour full of the things of a family that has been important for a long time and has stopped noticing: portraits, clocks, a harp, a mantelpiece of unopened letters. All the chairs face the fireplace, and the fireplace is bricked up.".
  Observe hearn_hearth_scene at hearn_hearth when true "A small back room with an old black hearth in it and nothing else. The hearth is lit. The fire in it is no bigger than a hand, a low red coal in a bed of ash, and the room is the warmest room you have been in in the city, in the way a room is warm that someone has loved for a long time.".
  Observe guild_scene at guild_hall when true "The Surveyors' Guild: a hall with a model of Quittance under a glass case, every house a tiny red cube, and a long table on which a hundred plans are pinned flat with plumb-bobs. A board lists the Surveyors, the houses they have passed and the houses they have Declined.".
  Observe teague_scene at teague_front when true "A sitting-room in the first days of mourning: black crape on the clock, black crape on the mirror, black crape on the cat. A birdcage on a stand has a cloth over it, and under the cloth something is cracking seeds with deliberation.".
  Observe corbett_scene at corbett_study when true "A cheerful, cold study full of surveying instruments: theodolites, plumb-lines, a stack of roof-plans with pencilled notes in the margin. Ianthe Corbett's coat hangs on a hook with a rope looped over it.".

  // ── The Bare Wards ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe wards_gate_scene at wards_gate when true "Inside the gap in the Cinderwall, the Bare Wards begin without ceremony: timber houses leaning over alleys, lines of laundry, the sound of a hundred conversations in a hundred upper rooms. There are no plates on any door. There are, on a surprising number of them, plates; they are the wrong colour.".
  Observe salt_lane_scene at salt_lane when true "Salt Lane runs down the middle of the Wards like a cut: crooked, crowded, loud, smelling of smoke and frying and people. Hearths glow in every window. In the rest of the city the sign says fire is forbidden; here there is a fire in every room.".
  Observe penny_hall_scene at penny_hall when true "A room with a long table, a locked box with three locks, a chalked ledger, and a board listing the dead of the year: forty-one names, and beside each the sum the club paid for the burying. Nine more names are chalked on a second board, headed NEXT.".
  Observe market_scene at night_market when hour(clock) >= 17 or hour(clock) < 5 "The Night Market has lit up under a hundred cooking-fires and a few cold-lamps nicked from the Hill: eel-pie, gin, salvage, second-hand marks, old lamps, stolen hats. Everyone here has the air of someone who has been told the rules and finds them amusing.".
  Observe market_day_scene at night_market when hour(clock) >= 5 and hour(clock) < 17 "By day the Night Market is a trodden square of empty stalls. A dog sleeps in the middle of it and an old woman sells matches from a basket.".
  Observe pip_scene at pip_stair when true "A tenement stair, five flights of rotten timber, with a landing at each floor and a smell of cabbage. On the top landing is a door open an inch, and in the gap you can see, on the floor, a tin with a red light in it.".
  Observe candlewick_scene at candlewick when true "A tight court of seven timber houses, black with old smoke, round a common pump. The washing hangs between the roofs. Someone has chalked on the pump, in a clerk's hand, a number and a date.".
  Observe skelter_scene at skelter_room when true "A rent-office with a counter and a hatch and a grating, and behind the grating a man doing sums. A rent-book as thick as a Bible lies open, and the door is locked from the inside.".
  Observe cinder_scene at cinder_ward when true "The Cinder Ward: three thousand people in eleven streets round a flat black ground that was the centre of the old city. The houses are tall, packed, wooden, hung with washing; and in the middle of the ground stands a chimney that is a hundred years older than they are, built of black glass, from which, at all hours, a thin white smoke goes straight up.".
  Observe gasket_scene at gasket_yard when not burned(gasket_yard) "Gasket Yard is a square of tenements round a dry well, where the washing is pegged between windows and a boy is chalking a hopscotch grid with the end of a spoon. A notice is pasted to the well-head in a clerk's hand. Nobody has read it aloud.".
  Observe flue_scene at first_flue when true "The First Flue is a chimney of fused glass sixty feet high and wide enough for a cart. There is no door in it. Warm air comes up out of it, and the faint sound of someone tending something.".

  // ── Mortmain ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe mort_lodge_scene at mort_lodge when true "The lodge-gate of Mortmain is wrought iron, open, with a porter in a hat. Beyond it the garden-cemetery runs in terraces and lawns to the river, every grave with a small brass plate: the Sovereign's sun, the year, and a number.".
  Observe annuity_row_scene at annuity_row when true "Annuitants' Row is a terrace of white cottages with green shutters, each with a rose and a notice: THE SOVEREIGN MUTUAL PAYS. They are the best-kept dwellings in the city; the people in them have all agreed to live a very long time.".
  Observe alms_scene at alms_room when true "The almshouse day-room: seven chairs, seven shawls, a stove, a kettle, and a hum of conversation conducted in a variety of deaf voices. The wall is papered with old Sovereign Mutual leaflets, which nobody has been able to bring themselves to remove.".
  Observe oakes_scene at oakes_room when true "A neat parlour with its shutters half-drawn and a great chair by the window. In the chair, under a heap of shawls, a very small old lady with an ear-trumpet sits with her eyes shut. A tea-tray has been set at her elbow. It has two cups.".
  Observe sov_scene at sov_floor when true "The Sovereign's counting-floor is hung with sunbursts and memento mori in equal numbers. The clerks speak softly, as clerks do who have to ask people whether they are dead.".
  Observe catacomb_head_scene at catacomb_head when true "A mossy path ends at a low grated door in the cemetery wall, with a Sovereign's sun above it so worn that it might be anything. A stair goes down behind the grating, into a cold that smells of old stone.".

  // ── The Sunk City ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe cellar_foot_scene at cellar_foot when true "At the foot of the Exchange stair the cellars begin, vaulted in black glass, dry, warm, silent. Somewhere there is a draught that moves your lamp-flame toward the dark, steadily, like a hand drawing you by the sleeve.".
  Observe arcade_scene at cellar_arcade when true "An arcade of fused pillars goes away in both directions, and under the arches there are the shapes of desks, counters and ledgers, melted into the floor in the attitude of men and women at work.".
  Observe queue_scene at queue_hall when not (qu_nerve(party) >= 2) "The Queue: a long vaulted hall with a line of the dead standing in it, patient, in nightclothes and Sunday best and sleeve-guards, a good many with children by the hand. They are the colour of candle smoke. Each holds a scrap of something. They are, to a man, looking toward a desk at the far end where a clerk's chair is empty, and every one of them is waiting to be called.".
  Observe bell_foot_scene at bell_foot when true "Black water in a round chamber, a lamp-lit ladder rising in a shaft, and the iron stub of a diving-bell's air-hose coming down out of the dark.".
  Observe catacomb_foot_scene at catacomb_foot when true "The bottom of the catacomb stair is a vault of bones stacked like firewood and labelled by year, and every year's label is the same: UNCLAIMED. A slot in the wall, at about the height of a man's chest, is stuffed with old receipts.".
  Observe glass_street_scene at glass_street when true "The Glass City: a street of fused houses, a street of glass, slag and brick, all melted at once and cooled at once, so that the façades run into each other like wax. In a window a glass table is laid for four. A glass cat sits in the road.".
  Observe slag_a_scene at slag_a when true "The first slag gallery is a long tube of black glass, slick, warm underfoot, with strings of pale light running along the roof like veins. The air shivers. Your lamp-flame leans toward the far end.".
  Observe slag_b_scene at slag_b when true "The second gallery is hotter. The walls have run and cooled in great shining curtains, and in the curtains, at intervals, there are figures set in the glass like flies, in the attitude of people who had just been told to hurry.".
  Observe furnace_row_scene at furnace_row when true "Furnace Row: forty furnaces, cold, in a row, each with a brass plate bolted to the brick, each plate the same, THIS PREMISES INSURED. Glass men stand between them in rows, like statues of clerks, their cuffs smoking.".
  Observe vault_door_scene at vault_door when true "A round door of black glass in the end of the gallery, ten feet across, with a notary's seal in the centre the size of a plate and a slot beneath it. The air coming through the seams is warm and smells of paper.".
  Observe vault_scene at vault when true "The Strongroom of the Old Exchange: a round chamber lined with shelves of black glass, in which stand rows and rows of sealed instruments, rolled, tied with ribbon gone to ash. In the middle there is a table, and on the table lies a single roll, and by the roll an ink-well in which the ink has not dried in ninety-four years.".
  Observe flue_foot_scene at flue_foot when true "The foot of the First Flue: a round well of glass looking straight up into a pinpoint of white sky. Heat blows down it like breath.".
  Observe hearth_scene at hearth_below when true "A chamber of glass, round, wide as a cathedral crossing, with a great hearth in the floor: not a fire, but the memory of a fire, a bed of white ash as large as a threshing-floor, and in the ash, very small and very bright, a red coal the size of a human heart. Your footsteps come back from the walls a moment late, and politely.".
}
data/adventures/sallowfield/places.kyr:
Module sallowfield "Three Nights at Sallowfield" {
  Description "Sallowfield: sixty people at a ford on the Brimble, a stranded coach, and an unpaid company three days up the valley.".

  // The Brimble runs north to south. The town is on its west bank; the coach road comes in from the east and crosses by
  // the ford or by the old packhorse bridge. Wyre's company comes down the east bank.
  Place vale "the Brimble vale" is region within imbar.
  Place eastbank "the east bank" is wilderness within vale at 2, 1.
  Place sallowfield "Sallowfield" is settlement within vale at 1, 1.
  Place upvale "the upper vale" is wilderness within vale at 1, 0.
  Place lowvale "the lower vale" is wilderness within vale at 1, 2.
  Place inn "the Ploughshare" is building within sallowfield.
  Place chapel "the chapel of Saint Eadred" is building within sallowfield.
  Place millhouse_b "Quarmby's mill" is building within sallowfield.
  Place smithy_b "Kersey's forge" is building within sallowfield.
  Place granary_b "the tithe granary" is building within sallowfield.

  Place east_road "the east road, at the ford" is room within eastbank at 2, 1 outdoors.
  Place green "Sallowfield green" is room within sallowfield at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place taproom "the Ploughshare taproom" is room within inn at 0, 1.
  Place forge "Kersey's forge" is room within smithy_b at 0, 2.
  Place granary "the tithe granary" is room within granary_b at 0, 0.
  Place nave "the nave of Saint Eadred's" is room within chapel at 2, 0.
  Place bell_loft "the bell loft" is room within chapel at 2, 1.
  Place tower_roof "the tower roof" is room within chapel at 2, 2.
  Place mill_yard "Quarmby's mill yard" is room within sallowfield at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place mill_loft "the mill loft" is room within millhouse_b at 0, 1.
  Place race "the mill race" is room within sallowfield at 0, 2 outdoors.
  Place ford_stones "the ford stones" is room within sallowfield at 2, 1 outdoors.
  Place ford_meadow "the ford meadow" is room within sallowfield at 2, 2 outdoors.
  Place bridge "the packhorse bridge" is room within sallowfield at 2, 0 outdoors.
  Place well "the green well" is room within sallowfield at 1, 0 outdoors.

  Place fold "the high fold" is room within upvale at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place high_track "the high track" is room within upvale at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place lookout "the Scar lookout" is room within upvale at 2, 0 outdoors.
  Place lower_farm "Greenhalgh's farm" is room within lowvale at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place reed_marsh "the reed marsh" is room within lowvale at 2, 1 outdoors.
  Place south_road "the south road" is room within lowvale at 1, 2 outdoors.
  Place parley_stone "the parley stone" is room within eastbank at 2, 2 outdoors.

  Passage ford_east "the ford, east side" is ford between east_road and ford_stones taking 10 minutes.
  Passage bridge_east "the packhorse bridge, east end" is bridge between east_road and bridge taking 10 minutes.
  Passage bridge_green "the bridge head" is path between bridge and green taking 5 minutes.
  Passage ford_meadow_way "the ford meadow" is path between ford_stones and ford_meadow taking 5 minutes.
  Passage meadow_green "the lane from the meadow" is road between ford_meadow and green taking 10 minutes.
  Passage inn_door "the Ploughshare door" is door between green and taproom.
  Passage forge_door "the forge door" is door between green and forge.
  Passage granary_door "the granary door" is door between green and granary.
  Passage nave_door "the chapel door" is doorway between green and nave.
  Passage bell_ladder "the bell ladder" is ladder between nave and bell_loft.
  Passage roof_hatch "the roof hatch" is ladder between bell_loft and tower_roof.
  Passage well_path "the way to the well" is path between green and well taking 3 minutes.
  Passage mill_lane "the mill lane" is path between green and mill_yard taking 10 minutes.
  Passage mill_door "the mill door" is door between mill_yard and mill_loft.
  Passage race_path "the race path" is path between mill_yard and race taking 5 minutes.
  Passage race_meadow "the race path to the meadow" is path between race and ford_meadow taking 10 minutes.
  Passage high_lane "the lane to the high track" is road between green and high_track taking 20 minutes.
  Passage fold_path "the track to the fold" is path between high_track and fold taking 30 minutes.
  Passage scar_path "the path to the Scar" is path between high_track and lookout taking 40 minutes.
  Passage low_lane "the lower lane" is road between green and lower_farm taking 20 minutes.
  Passage marsh_path "the reed track" is path between lower_farm and reed_marsh taking 20 minutes needing wayfinding or woodcraft.
  Passage marsh_meadow "the marsh edge" is path between reed_marsh and ford_meadow taking 25 minutes.
  Passage south_lane "the south road" is road between lower_farm and south_road taking 30 minutes.
  Passage parley_way "the road to the parley stone" is road between east_road and parley_stone taking 20 minutes.
  Passage lookout_east "the Scar path down to the east road" is path between lookout and parley_stone taking 40 minutes.
  Passage ford_race "the ford stones to the race" is path between ford_stones and race taking 10 minutes.
}
data/adventures/sallowfield/scenes.kyr:
Module sallowfield "Three Nights at Sallowfield" {
  Observe east_road_scene at east_road when true "The coach stands tilted at the water's edge with its off-hind wheel in the river, and the coachman is on his knees in the gravel looking at the axle as at a dead dog. Across the ford, a village: a chapel tower, a mill, fifteen roofs. The water is brown and not deep.".
  Observe ford_stones_scene at ford_stones when true "Flat stones set a stride apart across the Brimble, awash to the ankle. The west bank rises in a slope of cropped grass, and a miller's boy is fishing from it with a bent pin. On the east bank, in the mud, there are fresh hoof-prints going down to the water and back.".
  Observe bridge_scene at bridge when true "A packhorse bridge of two arches, single-file wide, with a cobbled hump and no parapet to speak of. Someone has chalked a name on the keystone and someone else has rubbed it out.".
  Observe green_scene at green when true "A green with a well at one end, a chapel at the other, and between them a flock of geese that has decided the visitors are theirs. An inn, a forge and a granary face the green. Smoke goes straight up from every chimney.".
  Observe taproom_scene at taproom when true "The taproom of the Ploughshare smells of wet dog and boiled mutton. Nan Ashworth's slate hangs behind the bar with the day's debts on it, two columns, in two kinds of chalk.".
  Observe forge_scene at forge when true "The forge is cold except for the one corner where the coach's iron tyre-strap lies in the coals. Peg Kersey's hammers hang by size. A pile of horseshoe nails stands in the corner like a heap of grey seed.".
  Observe granary_scene at granary when true "A long stone barn with the tithe-sacks stacked to the rafters: the whole winter of sixty people, and then some. The air is dry and sweet and full of dust. Mice have been told about it.".
  Observe nave_scene at nave when true "A small chapel, white-washed, with a rood screen of black oak and a plate-chest bolted to the floor. A bell-rope hangs down through a hole in the roof. The pews have been cut for shorter people than you.".
  Observe bell_loft_scene at bell_loft when true "The bell hangs in a frame of oak beams the thickness of a man, and the ladder to the roof goes up past its lip. The walls are a yard thick. There are slit windows on three sides, each wide enough for an arm and an arrow.".
  Observe tower_roof_scene at tower_roof when true "From the tower roof the whole vale lies open: the river in its loops, the east road coming down from the hills, the mill and the green, the marsh like a dark thumbprint to the south. A parapet waist-high runs round, with a gutter for pouring things.".
  Observe mill_yard_scene at mill_yard when true "Quarmby's mill grinds with a noise you feel in your teeth. A heap of sacks, a cart with a broken shaft, a dog asleep in the one patch of sun. The race runs under the yard in a stone channel, loud and cold.".
  Observe mill_loft_scene at mill_loft when true "The mill loft is dim and white with flour. Stones turn below the boards; the whole floor shivers. A hoist-door in the end wall opens on the yard, thirty feet up.".
  Observe race_scene at race when true "The race is a brown tongue of water cut from the Brimble above the bridge and led down to the wheel. At its head a sluice-gate on a rack and pinion stands open. Beyond it the meadow lies lower than the river, and ruts of cartwheels run into the grass.".
  Observe ford_meadow_scene at ford_meadow when true "A wet meadow between the ford and the village, grazed short. The ground gives a little underfoot. A hedge of hawthorn marks the town's end of it, and a gap in the hedge has been mended with a hurdle.".
  Observe well_scene at well when true "The green well is a ring of stone with a windlass. The bucket comes up cold and tasting faintly of iron. Someone has tied a ribbon to the rope and no one will say who.".
  Observe fold_scene at fold when true "A dry-stone fold on the hillside, high enough to see over the shoulder of the Scar, with a hut at the end for lambing. A hundred sheep stand in the lee of the wall and look at you as one animal. The turf is cropped to velvet.".
  Observe high_track_scene at high_track when true "A sheep track along the side of the hill, a stone's throw above the last field. The east road is a pale thread across the river, a mile off. Anything on it would be seen long before it was heard.".
  Observe lookout_scene at lookout when true "The Scar is a ledge of limestone with a cairn on it. The east road runs under it for a mile and a half, with every bend in plain sight, and the hills beyond are green and brown and empty to the horizon.".
  Observe lower_farm_scene at lower_farm when true "Greenhalgh's farm: a long house, a barn, a yard of trodden muck, a dozen cows. The farm sits where the valley floor is lowest and the first to be reached by anything coming down the river bank. The dog barks at you from the middle of the yard and does not leave it.".
  Observe reed_marsh_scene at reed_marsh when true "A mile of reed and standing water, black between the stems. A causeway of hurdles runs half-way into it and stops. Cranes call. The mud sucks at your boots and lets go with a noise like a kiss.".
  Observe south_road_scene at south_road when true "The south road leaves the valley between two low hills and goes on, flat and empty, towards places you have heard of. Nobody is on it. It would be easy to be one of the nobodies.".
  Observe parley_stone_scene at parley_stone when true "A standing stone as high as a man, on a rise on the east bank where the road dips. The grass round it has been trodden by feet that stand there to talk. You are a long way from the village and a good way in sight of it.".
}
data/adventures/sallowfield/wake.kyr:
Module sallowfield "Three Nights at Sallowfield" {
  // ── What the morning finds ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Relation walkedOn(group).
  Rule plan_open when planned(party) and parleyOpen(party) and not planMod5(party) {
    Assert planMod5(party). Decrease thrust(ford_stones) by 2 or to nothing. Decrease thrust(bridge) by 2 or to nothing. Decrease thrust(mill_yard) by 2 or to nothing. }
  Rule plan_refused when planned(party) and parleyRefused(party) and not planMod6(party) {
    Assert planMod6(party). Increase thrust(ford_stones) by 1. Increase thrust(bridge) by 1. Increase thrust(mill_yard) by 1. Increase thrust(nave) by 1. Increase drillBonus(party) by 2. }
  // To hear what he is owed is to give him a hearing: his line leans less, and the village's levy hears a captain with a case.
  Rule plan_owed when planned(party) and owedHeard(party) and not planMod7(party) {
    Assert planMod7(party). Decrease thrust(ford_stones) by 2 or to nothing. Decrease thrust(bridge) by 2 or to nothing. Decrease thrust(mill_yard) by 2 or to nothing.
    Decrease drillBonus(party) by 1 or to nothing. }
  Relation planMod5(group). Relation planMod6(group). Relation planMod7(group).

  Action walk_on(actor: group, site: place) "Walk on south, and do not look back" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, south_road).
    Time 0.
    On success { Assert walkedOn(party). }
    Result "You go. It is a road, and it goes on, and you go on it.".
  }

  Chapter ch_axle "The Axle" when true "A coach with a cracked axle at a ford, and the smith says three days.".
  Chapter ch_probe "The Probe" when watch(clock) >= 78 "Dusk on the first day. Two horsemen have looked at the ford.".
  Chapter ch_parley "The Stone" when parleyHeld(party) "A white rag on a lance, a standing stone, and a man who would sooner not.".
  Chapter ch_night "The Night" when p1done(party) "Four hours, in four movements. The bell is the village's oldest thing, and the bridge its newest.".
  Chapter ch_wave1 "The First Rush" when w2planned(party) "The first wave is in, and the reports are coming. There is an hour before the second.".
  Chapter ch_wave2 "The Second Wave" when w2done(ford_stones) and w2done(bridge) and w2done(mill_yard) and w2done(nave) "The second wave has gone where the first opened a road.".
  Chapter ch_morning "The Morning" when dawned(party) "It is light. You count.".

  Objective ob_news when watch(clock) < 120 and not knowsNumbers(party) "A company of unpaid soldiers has been seen on the east road. Crowther the shepherd, Nan Ashworth and the reeve each know a different part.".
  Objective ob_watch when watch(clock) < 78 and not watchedFord() "His riders will come to the ford at dusk. What they find there will be told.".
  Objective ob_works when not planned(party) and not barricadeUp(party) and not bridgeCut(party) "There are two days. A wall, a cut, a flood and a drill each take hours the others need.".
  Objective ob_parley when parleyHeld(party) and not wyreMet(party) "A white rag on a lance, by the standing stone.".
  Objective ob_night when battleOn() and not dawned(party) "It is dark. They are coming.".

  Milestone m_scout "caught the boy in the reeds" worth 150 when heldScout(lowes).
  Milestone m_stone "went to the standing stone and heard the captain out" worth 200 when wyreMet(party).
  Milestone m_farm "got Ned Greenhalgh and his cows out" worth 150 when greenhalghSaved(party).
  Milestone m_turned "bought Lieutenant Fothergill" worth 250 when fothergillTurned(party).
  Milestone m_spoiled "ruined the winter's grain to save the village" worth 200 when grainSpoiled(party).
  Milestone m_picks "turned the picked men away" worth 300 when picksWithdrawn(party) or picksBeaten(party).
  Milestone m_dawn "saw the third dawn" worth 400 when dawned(party).

  // Fates, by name, at dawn.
  Observe fate_quarmby_dead near party when dawned(party) and felled(quarmby) "Gil Quarmby is lying across the mill door with the key in his hand. They have not touched the mill. It looks to have been the one thing he asked.".
  Observe fate_quarmby_live near party when dawned(party) and not felled(quarmby) "Gil Quarmby is already on the wheel with a rag, wiping the soot off the buckets. 'Forty years,' he says, to nobody. The wheel turns.".
  Observe fate_pinn_dead near party when dawned(party) and felled(pinn) "They found Davy Pinn at the foot of the bridge with the sling still round his hand. His father is at the mill, grinding, because it is the only thing he knows how to do.".
  Observe fate_pinn_live near party when dawned(party) and not felled(pinn) and pinnBrave(party) "Davy Pinn is sitting on the tower roof with his legs over the parapet, eating a heel of bread. He is twelve years old, and he is wearing somebody's helmet.".
  Observe fate_cragg_dead near party when dawned(party) and felled(cragg) "They say Ellen Cragg is in the nave with her back against the plate-chest and an arrow in her hand, nock to string. The pile beside her is counted: thirty-one gone, ten left.".
  Observe fate_cragg_live near party when dawned(party) and not felled(cragg) "Ellen Cragg is counting what is left. 'Ten,' she says. She does not say it sadly. She says it as though it were a debt, and she was glad to know the figure.".
  Observe fate_mowbray_dead near party when dawned(party) and felled(mowbray) "They say Father Mowbray is in his own church with the doors wide. They have not taken the plate. The last thing he said was, the witnesses agree, a blasphemy of astonishing length.".
  Observe fate_mowbray_live near party when dawned(party) and not felled(mowbray) and mowbrayRaised(party) "Father Mowbray has said a rite over a man and the man has stood up. He is sitting in the porch, sweating through his surplice and swearing under his breath and continuously, like a pot.".
  Observe fate_cragg_kin near party when dawned(party) and not felled(cragg) and craggKin(party) "At the bottom of her tally, under the ten, Ellen Cragg has written a name in her own hand. It is a short name.".
  Observe fate_cragg_killed near party when dawned(party) and not felled(cragg) and craggKilled(party) "Ellen Cragg has not spoken to you since the ford. She has left a bow on your bed, strung, which is either courtesy or the other thing.".
  Observe fate_mowbray_arms near party when dawned(party) and not felled(mowbray) and mowbrayArms(party) "Father Mowbray has the stain of it on his sleeve, and says the morning office in it.".
  Observe fate_pinn_sent near party when dawned(party) and not felled(pinn) and pinnSent(party) and not pinnBrave(party) "Davy Pinn was on the green all night, as promised, and counted every man who went by, and is willing to say the number at length.".
  Observe fate_kersey_dead near party when dawned(party) and felled(kersey) "They say the forge is cold and Peg Kersey is in the doorway, on her side. There are black points on the floor all round her, and none of the men who fell on them are alive.".
  Observe fate_greenhalgh near party when dawned(party) and greenhalghDead(party) "Ned Greenhalgh is in his yard, with a cow. He had not been willing to leave. The cow is alive.".
  Observe fate_wadsworth near party when dawned(party) and wadsworthRan(party) "Hob Wadsworth is in the cellar of the Ploughshare, in the dark, under a barrel. He has been there since the second hour. It is a good barrel, and he has found the tap.".
  Observe fate_elland near party when dawned(party) and ellandFights(party) and not felled(elland) "Tib Elland is holding a granary door with a tally-stick. The door has held since midnight, and so has he.".
  Observe fate_hay near party when dawned(party) and hayLost(party) "Greenhalgh's meadow is a brown lake with the hurdles standing out of it, and his hay is under it. The cows will be on straw by Christmas, and he is sitting on the gate with the dog, looking at it.".
  Observe fate_winter near party when dawned(party) and winterShort(party) "The granary is stained or empty. There is going to be a winter in Sallowfield, and some of it will be hungry. People in the queue for the well are doing the sum aloud.".
  Observe fate_picks_argued near party when dawned(party) and picksArgued(party) "The three went off down the east road at first light, and one of them stopped at the bridge to tell the sentry he had been right about the coin.".
