  // ── How the places look ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe cross_scene at cross_road when not visitedBefore(cross_road) "The road comes up out of the march between snow-fields and stops being a road and starts being a fell road at a cross of grey stone, man-high, with a ledge round its foot worn hollow by knees. Someone has carved on its shaft, very neatly: FOR THE FAULTS OF ANOTHER. A low stone house stands beside it with smoke coming out of it, and on the step of the Cross a barefoot old man is mending a sandal.".
  Observe cross_again at cross_road when visitedBefore(cross_road) "The Penitent's Cross, with its worn ledge, and its vigil-house, and the road going north up the fell.".
  Observe reeve_hut_scene at reeve_hut when true "The vigil-house: one room, a good fire, a pair of snowshoes on the wall, a long pole shod with iron, a lantern with a horn shutter, and a book open on the table with a column of farm-names down one side and against each, for each night, a small neat C. Against CARTH, twenty-two of them.".
  Observe stone_scene at proxy_stone when not visitedBefore(proxy_stone) "Halfway up the fell the road passes a standing stone, and at the foot of the stone a man is kneeling in the snow with his head bowed and a board hung round his neck on a cord. He has been kneeling there since last winter. The frost has kept him. The board says, in good letters, FOR THE ADULTERY OF ONE OF THE COMMON COUNCIL OF GAUNT, FORTY NIGHTS, and under it, smaller, in a different hand, TOBIAS KELL, PROXY.".
  Observe stone_again at proxy_stone when visitedBefore(proxy_stone) and not keptBoard(party) "The Proxy's Stone, and Tobias Kell kneeling at the foot of it with his board round his neck, in the snow.".
  Observe stone_after at proxy_stone when visitedBefore(proxy_stone) and keptBoard(party) "The Proxy's Stone, and Tobias Kell kneeling at the foot of it with no board round his neck now, and his own name cut in the stone above him with the point of a knife.".
  Observe fork_scene at drove_fork when true "The Drove Fork, where the drovers' road goes off west round the shoulder of the fell, green under the snow where the beasts have trodden it, toward country that has never heard of Gaunt; and the fell road goes on up, white, to the top of Carth Fell.".
  Observe drovers_scene at drovers_way when true "The drovers' road, going west round the fell in a long trodden curve, wide enough for a herd, empty, and going on.".
  Observe fell_scene at fell_top when not snowing() and state(fell_snow, waiting) "The top of Carth Fell: a cairn, a wind that has come a long way, and the whole of the country to the north laid out below you, white and flat to the end of the world, and in the middle of it, very small and very clear, a walled city on a rise with a great church in the middle of it with one tower and the stump of another.".
  Observe fell_scene_after at fell_top when state(fell_snow, lying) "The top of Carth Fell, deep in new snow. To the north the Levels, white to the end of the world, and Gaunt in the middle of them, small and clear, with its one tower and the stump of another.".
  Observe yard_scene at carth_yard when snowing() "The yard at Carth: a long low house with the byre under the same roof, its one window black; a peat-stack drifted half over; a dog at the door, which barks once and then whines. No smoke goes up from the chimney. On a farm, in snow, with the light going, that is the strangest thing you have ever seen.".
  Observe yard_day_smoke at carth_yard when not snowing() and not vigilEnded(carth_vigil) and state(hearth, ablaze) "The yard at Carth, deep in snow: the long low house and its byre under one roof, the drifted peat-stack, and smoke going up from the chimney that the whole fell can see.".
  Observe yard_day at carth_yard when not snowing() and not vigilEnded(carth_vigil) and not state(hearth, ablaze) "The yard at Carth, deep in snow: the long low house and its byre under one roof, the drifted peat-stack, and a chimney with no smoke.".
  Observe yard_ended at carth_yard when not snowing() and vigilEnded(carth_vigil) "The yard at Carth, with smoke going up from the chimney straight into the cold air, and the snow round the door trodden brown.".
  Observe house_scene at house_place when not vigilEnded(carth_vigil) and state(hearth, cold) and not nightfall() and not carthNight() "The house-place at Carth by day, in what light comes through one small window: a long low room with smoke-black beams that have had no smoke on them for a month; a dresser with three plates; a box-bed in the wall with its doors open and too many blankets in it; a settle; a rocking-chair; and the dead hearth. Everyone's breath shows.".
  Observe house_lit at house_place when state(hearth, ablaze) "The house-place at Carth, with a fire on the hearth: a long low room, smoke-black beams, a dresser with three plates, a box-bed in the wall with its doors open and too many people in it, a table, a settle, and on the floor by the hearth a place laid on a cloth, a bowl and a spoon, for nobody.".
  Observe house_out at house_place when vigilEnded(carth_vigil) and not state(hearth, ablaze) "The house-place at Carth, with the hearth swept and a peat fire laid, and the door open for the cold to go out.".
  Observe byre_scene at carth_byre when true "The byre at Carth, through the house-place wall: warmer than the house, for the breath of a cow and a calf; straw underfoot; and along the far wall something long on a hurdle under a sheet, that the dog will not go near.".
  Observe levels_scene at levels_road when not visitedBefore(levels_road) "The road across the Levels: flat, white, straight, and at the end of it Gaunt, which gets bigger very slowly. It is walled twice, a new wall round an old one, and a third wall round the middle where the Minster stands, so that from out here it looks like a target. Off to the east a dark line of wood. Off to the west, in the city's wall, a gate with no road going out of it; and out beyond it on the snow, a long way off, a ruined sheepfold, with one thread of smoke going up from it.".
  Observe levels_again at levels_road when visitedBefore(levels_road) "The road across the Levels, with Gaunt at the end of it in its three walls, and out to the west the sheepfold's thread of smoke.".
  Observe levels_lantern at levels_road when nightfall() and (hour(clock) >= 21 or hour(clock) < 4) "Over the walls of Gaunt, high up where the north tower's scaffold must be, a single lantern is moving, slowly, from one corner to another, and back.".
  // The put-outs' fold: where the Gate of Ash leads.
  Place fold "the put-outs' fold" is room within levels at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Passage fold_track "the track across the snow to the fold" is path between levels_road and fold taking 40 minutes.
  Observe fold_scene at fold when not nightfall() "A sheepfold of dry stone on the bare Levels, half its walls down and the other half roofed over with turves and old sailcloth, and a fire in the middle of it under a hole. Seven people live here, or eight: you are not sure whether the bundle by the fire is a person. They are the ones the Gate of Ash was opened for, over the years, who did not walk away. From here Gaunt is a grey shape on the skyline with its tower and a half, and every one of them, when they are not working, sits facing it.".
  Observe fold_night at fold when nightfall() "The fold at night: the fire under its smoke-hole, seven faces round it, and far off across the snow the lamps of Gaunt, and the one lantern moving on the tower.".
  Observe wood_edge_scene at wood_edge when true "The edge of the Bishop's Wood: oak and holly, thick, dark, and a board on a post: THE BISHOP'S WOOD. THE DEAD-WOOD RIGHT IS SUSPENDED THIS WINTER BY ORDER OF THE WOOD-REEVE. TRESPASSERS WILL BE ASSESSED. Under it, cut in the post itself, older and deeper and nearly grown over: TO THE POOR OF GAUNT, THE FALLEN WOOD, FOR EVER. There has been no bishop to keep the wood in two hundred and eleven years; the Wood-reeve keeps it for him.".
  Observe deadfall_scene at deadfall when true "A clearing where an oak came down in some old gale and took three others with it: dead wood, grey and dry and stacked by nature, enough to keep the Row through a month. Wolf-tracks cross the snow in a line, all in the same prints, the way wolves go when there are a lot of them.".
  // The Row
  Observe fell_gate_scene at fell_gate when not visitedBefore(fell_gate) "The Fell Gate of Gaunt: a gate in the new wall, a gatehouse, and at a table under the arch, out of the wind, a man in a black gown with a box of tally-sticks and a knife, who is assessing everyone who comes in for the faults they did on the road. There is a queue. Everybody in it is thinking.".
  Observe fell_gate_again at fell_gate when visitedBefore(fell_gate) "The Fell Gate, with the Assessor at his table under the arch and his box of tallies.".
  Observe row_scene at row_lane when not nightfall() and not visitedBefore(row_lane) "The Row: two storeys of cold lodgings leaning on the old wall, a street of trodden snow, and in every other doorway someone sitting with their feet in a bowl of warm water, because their feet are their living. A board at the corner says BAREFOOT HALL and a hand points. Through the old wall, by Bow Gate, you can see the Middle Town, and smell its bread.".
  Observe row_again at row_lane when not nightfall() and visitedBefore(row_lane) "The Row: lodgings on the old wall, feet in bowls in the doorways, Bow Gate, the Barefoot Hall.".
  Observe row_ladle at row_lane when not nightfall() and not eveDay() and not ashDay() "By the Hall door the Barefoot copper sits cold on its brazier, and on a nail above it hangs a long iron ladle, polished bright as a spoon at a christening. Nobody in the Row touches it. 'The Duchess's,' says a woman in a doorway, when she sees you looking, and will not say who the Duchess is.".
  Observe row_night at row_lane when nightfall() "The Row at night: one lamp, at the Barefoot Hall's door, and a copper on a brazier beside it with steam going up, and a queue.".
  Observe hall_scene at barefoot_hall when true "The Barefoot Hall: a long room with benches, a board on the wall of the day's rates, a stove that is not lit, and along one wall a row of pegs, each with a name chalked over it and nothing on it. The pegs of those who died last winter. There are forty-one. Over the thirtieth, ELLEN WRAY, FROM THE FELL, and beside it, smaller, in a different hand, a little mark like a cut log, which somebody has tried to rub out and not quite managed.".
  Observe heb_scene at heb_cellar when true "Heb's cellar: a table, a lamp, a hundred tally-sticks in a hundred notchings in bundles on the wall, and knives, and a little brazier for darkening a new cut so it looks old.".
  Observe ditch_scene at row_ditch when not nightfall() "The Row ditch, frozen from wall to wall into a long grey slide, and on it every child in the Row, sliding, in a line, singing. By the culvert grating at the end the ice is black and thin.".
  Observe ditch_night at row_ditch when nightfall() "The Row ditch at night, frozen, the slide worn black down the middle by a day of children, and at the far end one boot, forgotten, standing upright.".
  Observe ash_scene at gate_of_ash when not gateOfAshOpen() "The Gate of Ash: an arch in the new wall with a gate in it, and no road outside it, only the Levels. Over the arch, cut deep: WHAT IS NOT IN THE REGISTER IS NOT IN GAUNT. The gate is chained, and the chain is sealed.".
  Observe ash_open at gate_of_ash when gateOfAshOpen() "The Gate of Ash stands open on the Levels and the dusk, with the chain hanging and the seal broken, and the cold coming in.".
  // The Middle Town
  Observe shambles_scene at shambles when not nightfall() and not visitedBefore(shambles) "The Shambles: the Middle Town's long market street, butchers' and bakers' and chandlers' under one long penthouse, and everybody buying, because the Fast is coming and in the Fast you may not buy any of it. Up at the end the Bearer's Steps go up to the Close Gate. Down the other end, Bow Gate and the Row. A man is selling hot chestnuts and indulgences from the same brazier.".
  Observe shambles_again at shambles when not nightfall() and visitedBefore(shambles) and not licence() "The Shambles: the penthouse, the butchers, the chestnut man, the Steps up to the Close and Bow Gate down to the Row.".
  Observe shambles_night at shambles when nightfall() and not licence() "The Shambles at night, shuttered, with the lamp of the Fat Lamb at one end and the lamp of the Close Gate at the other.".
  Observe shambles_eve at shambles when licence() "The Shambles on Fastens' Eve: lit end to end with torches, crowded, masked. A wooden giant with a pig's head and a belly made of a barrel goes by on a door, carried by eight apprentices: the Fat King. Everyone is eating everything.".
  Observe stand_scene at the_stand when daytime() "The Stand: the old sheep-market, its hurdle pens full of men and women, each pen with a chalked board. FASTS 3D A DAY. VIGIL (INDOORS) 6D. VIGIL (OUT) 1S. BAREFOOT 1S A MILE. STRIPES BY ARRANGEMENT. Burgesses' men go along the pens with lists, looking at feet. Nobody here is sorry for anything, and all of them are working.".
  Observe stand_empty at the_stand when not daytime() "The Stand at night: the pens empty, the boards rubbed out, and a chalk-end left on the clerk's stool for the morning.".
  Observe exchange_scene at wood_exchange when true "The Wood Exchange: a hall with a counter and a great pair of scales, a board of prices, and over the door a carved wooden billet, the city's sign for wood. The board says: OAK, THE CORD, 30S. ASH 28S. THORN 24S. FAGGOTS, THE HUNDRED, 9S. These are the prices of a city that owns its forest. A clerk is writing the prices up by a shilling, carefully, with the chalk held between two fingers so as not to get it on his cuff.".
  Initially Assert teachesAt(billet_known, wood_exchange).
  Observe billet_matched at wood_exchange when knows(party, billet_coin) and not seenOnce(billet_known) "You know that shape. You have had it under your thumb, in the dark, on a cold shilling: the little cut log over this door is the mark on the Scaifes' coin." teaches billet_known.
  Discovery billet_known "The little cut log struck on the Scaifes' shillings is the billet over the Wood Exchange: the forty nights at Carth were bought with the Wood Exchange's own coin.".
  Observe lamb_scene at fat_lamb when not licence() "The Fat Lamb: a big warm inn, the warmest room you have stood in since the march, full of people eating as if somebody were going to take the plates away, which on Wednesday somebody is. A fire with half a sheep turning over it, and a boy turning the sheep.".
  Observe lamb_eve at fat_lamb when licence() "The Fat Lamb on Fastens' Eve: masks, music, a fiddle and a drum, the fire, the ox, couples at every table who would not be at one together on any other night, and the landlord going round with a jug saying 'Midnight, mind. Midnight.'".
  Observe tanners_scene at tanners_row when true "Tanners' Row: once the tanneries, now the houses of the tanners' widows and grandchildren, who do not tan; tall houses with steps. A drapery, a bakehouse, and a door with a brass knocker in the shape of a hand.".
  Observe pickersgill_scene at pickersgill_parlour when true "Mistress Pickersgill's parlour: Turkey carpet, a good fire, a cage of finches, three books of devotion with uncut pages, and one, much handled, without a title.".
  Observe brewhouse_scene at dinsdale_brewhouse when true "Dinsdale's brewhouse: coppers, steam, the smell of malt, and at a high desk in the corner, in a velvet bonnet, Mistress Grizel Dinsdale, brewster, doing sums.".
  Observe drapery_scene at sowerby_shop when true "Sowerby's drapery: bolts of broadcloth to the ceiling, a long counter, and on the wall behind it, framed, a drawing of the Ladder of Merit with SOWERBY on the second rung, and a space above it, waiting.".
  Observe bakehouse_scene at bakehouse when state(oven, cold) "Mother Sugden's bakehouse: a cold oven the size of a cottage, trays of dough under cloths, rising, and nowhere to put them.".
  Observe bakehouse_hot at bakehouse when not state(oven, cold) "Mother Sugden's bakehouse, roaring: the oven alight, trays going in and out on a peel, and the smell of shrove-cakes coming out of the door and down Tanners' Row like a crowd.".
  Observe steps_scene at close_gate_street when true "The Bearer's Steps: thirty broad stone steps up to the Close Gate, every one worn into a dip in the middle by knees, and the Close Gate at the top with a porter behind a grille. On the left, in the Close wall, the masons' yard door. On the right, Gaol Lane.".
  Observe gaol_lane_scene at gaol_lane when true "Gaol Lane: a narrow way between houses and the Close wall, and in the wall, at the height of a tall man's head, one barred window. Further on, the wall goes up past the north tower's scaffold, poles and ropes and ladders lashed against the sky.".
  // The Close
  Observe close_scene at close_green when not visitedBefore(close_green) "The Close: warm. You notice it before anything else: the wind does not come in here, and the snow on the lawn has been swept into heaps. Canons' houses with smoking chimneys; the Penitentiary, a long grey building with forty windows; the Schools; and the Minster, enormous, with one tower finished and the other a stump in a cage of scaffold. Everyone here has been forgiven.".
  Observe close_again at close_green when visitedBefore(close_green) "The Close: swept snow, smoking chimneys, the Penitentiary, the Schools, the Minster and its one and a half towers.".
  Observe porch_walked at minster_porch when sowerbyWalked(sowerby) or dinsdaleWalked(dinsdale) "The Minster porch, and in it the Ladder of Merit: a board of black oak twice the height of a man, on which the most penitent men and women of Gaunt are listed in gold, in order of how much they have paid other people to suffer. At the top: HUGH THACKRAY, WOOD-REEVE. Under it, where the second name should go this morning, a gilder is up a ladder with his brush in the air, waiting to be told whose.".
  Observe porch_scene at minster_porch when not sowerbyWalked(sowerby) and not dinsdaleWalked(dinsdale) "The Minster porch, and in it the Ladder of Merit: a board of black oak twice the height of a man, on which the most penitent men and women of Gaunt are listed in gold, in order of how much they have paid other people to suffer. At the top: HUGH THACKRAY, WOOD-REEVE. Second, by a hair's breadth and a fresh coat of gold that was not there yesterday: GRIZEL DINSDALE and P. SOWERBY, alternately.".
  Observe nave_scene at minster_nave when not ashDay() "The nave of the Minster: very high, very cold despite the Close, and at the crossing Saint Oswy's shrine, a stone man carrying another man on his back, both of them worn smooth by hands. Cut on the plinth: OSWY BORE HIM UP THE HILL THAT HE MIGHT BE FORGIVEN. Under it, a hand's breadth of the stone has been dressed back flat and smooth, as if something more had been cut there once, and taken off. A man in a blue gown is selling candles to burn for other people.".
  Observe nave_ash at minster_nave when ashDay() "The nave of the Minster on Ash Day, full: the whole city, it seems, with a grey thumb-mark on every forehead, standing, waiting, looking at the Chapter House door.".
  Observe chapter_scene at chapter_house when not sitting() "The Chapter House: a round stone room with a stone bench all round it and a stone chair at the head, and in the middle, on the floor, a little square of different stone, where the accused stands. Round the wall above the bench, cut one under another, the names of every Lord and Lady Penitentiary of Gaunt, thirty-one of them, the oldest worn almost away; the newest, cut sharp and still pale, HAWISE STRAKE, OF THE ROW.".
  Observe penitentiary_scene at penitentiary when true "The Penitentiary: a long room of clerks, and behind them forty great books on forty lecterns, the Register of Gaunt, every fault and every penance and who did it, back two hundred and eleven years, to the first line of the first book, in brown ink gone the colour of tea: In the year the Bishop went away, and the Penitentiary took up his keys; and at the end of the room, at a desk with a fire beside it, a woman in grey with a pen behind her ear.".
  Observe schools_scene at schools when true "The Schools: a hall with two pulpits facing each other across it like a quarrel built in oak, and benches, and students on the benches, and on the wall a list of Determinations for sale, with prices.".
  Observe tower_scene at tower_foot when not nightfall() "The foot of the north tower: the stump of it, eighty feet of fine stone and then nothing, in a cage of poles and lashings and ladders and platforms that has been there so long the poles have gone silver. On the top platform a course of new white stone has been laid today. A board: THE NORTH TOWER. BEGUN IN THE YEAR OF THE COMMERCE. GIVE TO THE FABRIC.".
  Observe tower_night_known at tower_foot when nightfall() and seenOnce(unbuilding) "The foot of the north tower at night, the scaffold a black net against the sky.".
  Observe lodge_scene at masons_lodge when true "The masons' lodge: a long shed against the Close wall, banker-benches, chips of white stone on everything, the tracing-floor with the north tower drawn on it full size in scratched lines, finished, as it was meant to be, two hundred years ago.".
  Observe gaol_scene at gaol_cell when true "The Consistory gaol: a warm room with a bed, a table, a fire, a barred window high up on Gaol Lane, and a door with a grille. The Consistory is merciful. It only means to put him out in the snow.".
}
data/adventures/winter-in-carth/growth.k:
Module gaunt "A Winter in Carth" {
  // ── What the company grows by ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // Experience for things done, not things killed: a promise kept or not, a night got through, a mind moved.
  Milestone m_custody "took Ninian Hern into custody on the fell road" worth 50 when custody(party).
  Milestone m_answered "answered Hern's three questions on the road" worth 100 when answeredSorry(party) and answeredDead(party) and (saidBinds(party) or saidChosen(party)).
  Milestone m_kell "gave Tobias Kell his own name" worth 100 when keptBoard(party).
  Milestone m_night "got through the night at Carth" worth 150 when nightOver(party).
  Milestone m_dowsie "kept Dowsie Scaife warm without a fire" worth 250 when dowsieSafe(dowsie) and not hernCoat(hern) and not state(hearth, ablaze) and not byreFire(carth_vigil) and nightOver(party).
  Milestone m_dowsie_fire "lit a fire at Carth for a child" worth 150 when litWithoutLeave(party) and dowsieSafe(dowsie).
  Milestone m_letter "kept the letter of the vigil and the child warm" worth 250 when byreFire(carth_vigil) and vigilOn() and nightOver(party) or quenched(carth_vigil) and vigilOn() and nightOver(party).
  Milestone m_granny "brought Old Mother Scaife in out of the byre" worth 100 when grannyIn(carth_vigil) and grannyGone(carth_vigil) and nightOver(party).
  Milestone m_ralph "laid Ralph Scaife out with the words for the dead" worth 100 when ralphLaid(carth_vigil).
  Milestone m_shriven "made your shrift clean in Gaunt" worth 100 when shriven() and assessed(party).
  Milestone m_own "did your own penance in Gaunt" worth 100 when keptStepVigil(party) or walkedBarefoot(party).
  Milestone m_patron "found out whose forty nights they were" worth 150 when knows(party, thackray_vigil).
  Milestone m_annis "brought Annis Scaife face to face with the man who bought her vigil" worth 150 when annisSaid(thackray).
  Milestone m_thackray "moved Hugh Thackray to act" worth 300 when thackrayChanged().
  Milestone m_released "saw the Carth vigil released" worth 200 when vigilReleased(carth_vigil).
  Milestone m_widow "brought Joan Pickersgill and Abel Lumb to one table" worth 200 when betrothed(joan).
  Milestone m_ladder "set the Ladder's rivals at each other until the Stand was bought out" worth 150 when standCornered(dinsdale).
  Milestone m_sowerby "saw a burgess of Gaunt do his own penance" worth 150 when sowerbyChanged(sowerby).
  Milestone m_tower "saw the north tower's new course stand" worth 200 when courseSet(joby).
  Milestone m_pellow "showed the Lady Penitentiary what the Fabric does by night" worth 150 when pellowExposed(pellow).
  Milestone m_skates "fished Tib Ackroyd's skate-bones out of the ditch" worth 50 when tibHelped(party).
  Milestone m_baker "lit Mother Sugden's oven" worth 50 when bakerHelped(party).
  Milestone m_wood "brought the Row a sledge of dead wood, by right" worth 150 when broughtWood(party).
  Milestone m_strike "brought the Barefoot out on Ash Day" worth 300 when struck(barefoot).
  Milestone m_bess "carried Bess Ackroyd's word to Hern" worth 100 when hernHeardBess(hern).
  Milestone m_masked "spoke with the masked woman at the Barefoot copper" worth 100 when metMasked(party).
  Milestone m_hawise "moved the Lady Penitentiary" worth 300 when hawiseMoved().
  Milestone m_prudence "kept Prudence Garth from selling the night" worth 100 when prudenceTurned(prudence).
  Milestone m_window "got the bars out of the gaol window" worth 150 when barsOut(hern).
  Milestone m_quist "set two Doctors of the Faculty at each other" worth 100 when crossed(consistory).
  Milestone m_witness "stood witness for Carth before the Consistory" worth 200 when testifiedCarth(party).
  Milestone m_recant "gave Ninian Hern the words to live by" worth 400 when verdictRecant(consistory).
  Milestone m_bearer "saw a sentence borne by another in the Chapter House" worth 400 when verdictBearer(consistory).
  Milestone m_fast "saw the Consistory adjourned for want of proxies" worth 400 when verdictFast(consistory).
  Milestone m_gate "went out of the Gate of Ash with him" worth 200 when wentWithHern(party).

  // ── The Barefoot soles ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // Whoever has walked the fell with Hern, done a barefoot mile in Gaunt, and kept a night on the Bearer's Steps has
  // learned what the Row knows: to stand in snow. Once, for one member, as a Manual is read.
  Relation solesLearned(group).
  Action learn_soles(actor: group, reader: member, site: place) "Have {reader} learn from the Row how to stand in snow" {
    Description "Hern's way: you don't stand on your feet, you stand on your mind. Once learned, never lost.".
    Requires memberOf(reader, actor) and awake(reader) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, barefoot_hall) and askedSorry(actor) and walkedBarefoot(actor) and keptStepVigil(actor)
      and not solesLearned(actor).
    Time 6. Resolve endow(reader, constitution, by_one).
    On success { Assert solesLearned(actor). }
    Result "Bess Ackroyd sits you down on the Hall bench with your feet in a bowl and tells you, for an hour, what Hern taught her at nine: where the cold goes if you let it, and where it goes if you don't; how to put a foot down whole on frozen setts; how to kneel on your mind. Some of it is nonsense. Most of it is not. At the end she dries your feet herself, which in the Row is a thing done for few.".
  }
}
data/adventures/wrayford/city.kyr:
Module wrayford "The Third Night" {
  Description "Wrayford, a bridge-city where the drove roads cross the Wray, in the three days after the lord's riders hanged three carters from the gatehouse rail: a city of carters, aldermen, ferrymen and printers, a toll nobody wants and everybody is making money from, and a widow who will bury her husband before the third night is out.".

  // ── The vale ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // The drove roads come down off the fells to the one bridge in forty miles. The city proper is on the north bank;
  // across nineteen arches, the Liberty of Overbridge, which has been Saint Wade's since before there was a bridge.
  Place wray "the vale of the Wray" is region within imbar.
  Initially Assert terrain(wray, hills).
  Place fells_edge "the fell road" is wilderness within wray at 1, 0.
  Place wrayford "Wrayford" is settlement within wray at 1, 1.
  Place bridge "Wrayford Bridge" is site within wray at 1, 2.
  Place overbridge "Overbridge" is settlement within wray at 1, 3.
  Place south_country "the south road" is wilderness within wray at 1, 4.

  // ── Buildings ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place pardoe_house "the Pardoe house" is building within wrayford.
  Place nine_wheels "the Nine Wheels" is building within wrayford.
  Place wash_house "Win Fenner's wash-house" is building within wrayford.
  Place guildhall "the Guildhall" is building within wrayford.
  Place counting_house "the Bridge Company's counting-house" is building within wrayford.
  Place quoin_house "Quoin's print shop" is building within wrayford.
  Place pawn_house "the pawnshop in Cutler's Lane" is building within wrayford.
  Place tull_house "Tull's cutlery" is building within wrayford.
  Place hulme_house "the reeve's house" is building within wrayford.
  Place gidley_house "Alderman Gidley's house" is building within wrayford.
  Place ice_store "Gidley's ice-house" is building within wrayford.
  Place gatehouse "the gatehouse" is building within bridge.
  Place hobday_house "the toll-keeper's house" is building within bridge.
  Place bridge_chapel "Saint Wade's chapel on the bridge" is building within bridge.
  Place saint_wades "Saint Wade's" is building within overbridge.
  Place abbess_house "the Abbess's lodging" is building within overbridge.
  Place ferry_inn "the Ferry Inn" is building within overbridge.

  // ── Rooms ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place drove_road "the drove road, above Wrayford" is room within fells_edge at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place carters_yards "the carters' yards" is room within wrayford at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place northgate "Northgate" is room within wrayford at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place wain_row "Wain Row" is room within wrayford at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Place pardoe_kitchen "the Pardoe kitchen" is room within pardoe_house at 0, 2 indoors.
  Place pardoe_yard "the Pardoe yard" is room within pardoe_house at 0, 3 outdoors.
  Place wheels_taproom "the Nine Wheels' taproom" is room within nine_wheels at 2, 0 indoors.
  Place fenner_copper "Win Fenner's wash-house" is room within wash_house at 2, 1 indoors.
  Place market_cross "the Market Cross" is room within wrayford at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place guild_hall "the Guildhall's long hall" is room within guildhall at 1, 2 indoors.
  Place guild_below "below the Guildhall" is level within guildhall.
  Place guild_cellar "the Guildhall cellar" is room within guild_below at 1, 3 underground.
  Place reeve_yard "the Guildhall yard" is room within wrayford at 2, 2 outdoors.
  Place counting_room "the counting-house" is room within counting_house at 3, 1 indoors.
  Place pinch_room "the collector's room" is room within counting_house at 3, 2 indoors.
  Place shambles "the Shambles" is room within wrayford at 0, 4 outdoors.
  Place cutlers_lane "Cutler's Lane" is room within wrayford at 2, 4 outdoors.
  Place quoin_shop "Quoin's print shop" is room within quoin_house at 3, 4 indoors.
  Place pawnshop "the pawnshop" is room within pawn_house at 2, 5 indoors.
  Place tull_shop "Tull's cutlery" is room within tull_house at 3, 5 indoors.
  Place mercer_hill "Mercer Hill" is room within wrayford at 3, 0 outdoors.
  Place hulme_study "the reeve's study" is room within hulme_house at 4, 0 indoors.
  Place gidley_parlour "Alderman Gidley's parlour" is room within gidley_house at 4, 1 indoors.
  Place ice_house "the ice-house" is room within ice_store at 5, 0 underground.
  Place wharf "the Wharf" is room within wrayford at 0, 5 outdoors.
  Place ferry_stage "the ferry-stage" is room within wrayford at 0, 6 outdoors.
  Place under_arches "the bank under the first arches" is room within wrayford at 1, 6 outdoors.
  Place gate_road "the Bridge End, under the gatehouse" is room within bridge at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place toll_ruin "the burned toll-house" is room within bridge at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Place gate_top "the top of the gatehouse" is level within gatehouse.
  Place gate_leads "the gatehouse leads" is room within gate_top at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place bridge_street "Bridge Street, on the arches" is room within bridge at 2, 0 outdoors.
  Place hobday_room "Jennet Hobday's front room" is room within hobday_house at 2, 1 indoors.
  Place chapel "the bridge chapel" is room within bridge_chapel at 3, 0 indoors.
  Place chapel_below "the starling steps" is level within bridge_chapel.
  Place starling "the starling ledge under the middle arch" is room within chapel_below at 3, 1 outdoors.
  Place overbridge_street "Overbridge Street" is room within overbridge at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place south_stair "the south ferry-stair" is room within overbridge at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place nave "Saint Wade's" is room within saint_wades at 2, 0 indoors.
  Place wades_acre "Wade's Acre" is room within overbridge at 3, 0 outdoors.
  Place abbess_court "the Abbess's court-room" is room within abbess_house at 1, 1 indoors.
  Place ferry_taproom "the Ferry Inn" is room within ferry_inn at 2, 1 indoors.
  Place tanyards "the tan-yards" is room within overbridge at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Place bear_garden "the bear-garden" is room within overbridge at 0, 2 outdoors.
  Place south_road "the south road, out of Overbridge" is room within south_country at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place wades_step "Wade's Step, in the middle of the old ford" is room within bridge at 1, 3 outdoors.

  // ── Ways ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Passage drove_way "the drove road" is road between drove_road and northgate taking 30 minutes.
  Passage yards_lane "the yard lane" is path between northgate and carters_yards taking 5 minutes.
  Passage row_lane "Wain Row" is path between northgate and wain_row taking 5 minutes.
  Passage pardoe_door "the Pardoes' door" is door between wain_row and pardoe_kitchen.
  Passage pardoe_back "the back door" is door between pardoe_kitchen and pardoe_yard.
  Passage wheels_door "the Nine Wheels' door" is door between northgate and wheels_taproom.
  Passage wash_door "the wash-house door" is door between northgate and fenner_copper.
  Passage cartway "the Cartway" is road between northgate and market_cross taking 10 minutes.
  Passage guild_door "the Guildhall door" is door between market_cross and guild_hall.
  Passage cellar_stair "the cellar stair" is stair between guild_hall and guild_cellar.
  Passage yard_gate "the Guildhall yard gate" is gate between market_cross and reeve_yard.
  Passage counting_door "the counting-house door" is door between market_cross and counting_room.
  Passage pinch_door "the door behind the counter" is door between counting_room and pinch_room.
  Passage shambles_lane "Shambles Lane" is path between market_cross and shambles taking 5 minutes.
  Passage fish_stair "the fish-stair" is steps between shambles and wharf.
  Passage cutlers_way "Cutler's Lane" is path between market_cross and cutlers_lane taking 5 minutes.
  Passage quoin_door "Quoin's door" is door between cutlers_lane and quoin_shop.
  Passage pawn_door "the pawnshop door" is door between cutlers_lane and pawnshop.
  Passage tull_door "Tull's door" is door between cutlers_lane and tull_shop.
  Passage mercer_steps "the Mercer Steps" is steps between market_cross and mercer_hill.
  Passage hulme_door "the reeve's door" is door between mercer_hill and hulme_study.
  Passage gidley_door "Alderman Gidley's door" is door between mercer_hill and gidley_parlour.
  Passage ice_door "the ice-house door" is door between mercer_hill and ice_house.
  Passage bridge_end "Bridge End" is path between market_cross and gate_road taking 5 minutes.
  Passage stage_walk "the wharf-side" is path between wharf and ferry_stage taking 5 minutes.
  Passage bank_path "the bank path under the bridge" is path between wharf and under_arches taking 5 minutes.
  Passage ruin_way "the toll-house doorway" is doorway between gate_road and toll_ruin.
  Passage gate_stair "the gate-ward's stair" is stair between gate_road and gate_leads.
  Passage gate_arch "the gatehouse arch" is arch between gate_road and bridge_street.
  Passage hobday_door "the Hobdays' door" is door between bridge_street and hobday_room.
  Passage chapel_door "the chapel door" is door between bridge_street and chapel.
  Passage starling_ladder "the ladder down through the undercroft" is ladder between chapel and starling.
  Passage drawbridge_span "the drawbridge" is bridge between bridge_street and overbridge_street taking 10 minutes.
  Passage south_steps "the ferry-stair steps" is steps between overbridge_street and south_stair.
  Passage nave_door "Saint Wade's door" is door between overbridge_street and nave.
  Passage acre_door "the door to the Acre" is door between nave and wades_acre.
  Passage abbess_gate "the Abbess's gate" is gate between overbridge_street and abbess_court.
  Passage ferry_inn_door "the Ferry Inn's door" is door between overbridge_street and ferry_taproom.
  Passage tan_lane "Tanners' Lane" is path between overbridge_street and tanyards taking 5 minutes.
  Passage bear_lane "the bear-garden lane" is path between tanyards and bear_garden taking 5 minutes.
  Passage south_way "the south road" is road between overbridge_street and south_road taking 30 minutes.

  // The pier face, from the bank under the first arch up to the gatehouse rail: a climb for a climber, or a rope's
  // work for anyone who can get one fixed. Boys have done it for a dare since the bridge was built.
  Passage pier_face "the pier face" is ladder between under_arches and gate_leads taking 10 minutes needing climbing or rope.
  // Dorcas Mudd's ferry, from her stage on the Wharf to the south stair: while she runs it, and at night only for those
  // she will run it for.
  Passage ferry "Dorcas Mudd's ferry" is ferry between ferry_stage and south_stair taking 20 minutes
    opening when ferryRunning() or carries(party, ferry_token) "The ferry-boat is drawn up on the stage with its oars shipped. Nobody crosses by Dorcas Mudd's ferry unless Dorcas Mudd is rowing it.".
  // The old ford, below the bridge, where the city got its name: under water by day, when Alderman Dunch's mills at
  // Wrayholme are grinding, and shallow in the small hours, when they pen the river to fill their ponds for the morning.
  // Halfway over is Wade's Step, the deep place where the saint stumbled, and what lives in it.
  Passage ford "the old ford" is ford between under_arches and wades_step taking 15 minutes
    opening when lowWater() "The Wray runs deep and brown over where the old ford was. Nobody wades it while the mills are grinding.".
  Passage ford_far "the far ford-stones" is ford between wades_step and tanyards taking 15 minutes
    opening when lowWater() and (tolerates(bargeman, party) or not able(bargeman)) "The far stones are on the other side of the Step, and of what lies in it across the way.".
}

data/adventures/wrongboat/hunt.kyr:
Module wrongboat "The Wrong Boat" {
  // ── The hunt ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // A pursuit that seeks a fixed place is an itinerary. These seek the company: one for each place it can stand,
  // taken up while the hunt is on, hiding or not (a hidden company is searched for, not forgotten), so that Bess (and, once the company has passed the race-head, the lads) go to
  // where the company is, by the ways that are open, and stop when they are there.
  Query huntBess() means not bessAlly(party) and not bessMet(party) and since(14) and (trailLostAt(party) == 0 or watch(clock) >= trailLostAt(party) + 30) and not bessTook(party) and not boxReturned(party).
  Query huntLads() means not ladsDealt() and not escort() and (ladsMet(party) or been(party, ferry_stage)).
  Pursuit hunt_bess_road for bess "coming for you" priority 8 when huntBess() and at(party, road) seeks at(bess, road).
  Pursuit hunt_bess_quay for bess "coming for you" priority 8 when huntBess() and at(party, quay) seeks at(bess, quay).
  Pursuit hunt_bess_taproom for bess "coming for you" priority 8 when huntBess() and at(party, taproom) seeks at(bess, taproom).

Module wrongboat "The Wrong Boat" {
  Description "The Aldwater, from the Staithe quay down through the fen, the fair at Pelham, the mill-race and the ferry at Highfoot, on the wrong barge, with the wrong parcel, with someone coming.".

  // The river country, upstream to down. A road runs by the river (the chaser's way); the barge goes by water.
  Place aldwater "The Aldwater country" is region within imbar.
  Place staithe_ward "Staithe" is settlement within aldwater at 0, 0.
  Place fen "the Wend Fen" is wilderness within aldwater at 1, 1.
  Place pelham_ward "Pelham" is settlement within aldwater at 2, 2.
  Place mill_reach "the mill reach" is wilderness within aldwater at 3, 3.
  Place highfoot_ward "Highfoot" is settlement within aldwater at 4, 4.
  Place hill_road "the hill road" is wilderness within aldwater at 5, 5.
  Place heron "the Heron and Pipe" is building within staithe_ward.
  Place tollhouse "the toll-house" is building within staithe_ward.
  Place barge "the barge Patient Mary" is site within aldwater at 0, 1.
  Place mill "Auster's mill" is building within mill_reach.
  Place last_inn "the Last Pint" is building within hill_road.

  // Staithe.
  Place road "the Staithe road" is room within staithe_ward at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place quay "the Staithe quay" is room within staithe_ward at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place taproom "the Heron and Pipe" is room within heron at 2, 0.
  Place toll_counter "the toll-house counter" is room within tollhouse at 1, 1.
  // The barge, whose four rooms are carried from landing to landing.
  Place deck "the deck of the Mary" is room within barge at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place cabin "the Mary's cabin" is room within barge at 1, 0.
  Place hold "the Mary's hold" is room within barge at 0, 1.
  Place galley "the Mary's galley" is room within barge at 1, 1.
  // The fen.
  Place fen_landing "the fen landing" is room within fen at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place causeway "the long causeway" is room within fen at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place bell_cot "the bell-cot" is room within fen at 2, 0 outdoors.
  Place eel_stage "the eel-stage" is room within fen at 1, 1 outdoors.
  // Pelham fair.
  Place fair_quay "Pelham quay" is room within pelham_ward at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place fairground "Pelham fairground" is room within pelham_ward at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place puppet_booth "the puppet booth" is room within pelham_ward at 2, 0.
  Place draper "Coyle's slop-shop" is room within pelham_ward at 1, 1.
  Place horse_lines "the horse lines" is room within pelham_ward at 2, 1 outdoors.
  Place lockup "the Pelham lock-up" is room within pelham_ward at 0, 2.
  Place pelham_inn "the Magpie" is room within pelham_ward at 0, 1.
  // The mill reach.
  Place race_head "the head of the mill-race" is room within mill_reach at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place millyard "the mill yard" is room within mill_reach at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place weir "the weir" is room within mill_reach at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place millhouse "Auster's kitchen" is room within mill at 2, 0.
  Place sluice_hut "the sluice hut" is room within mill_reach at 0, 1 outdoors.
  // Highfoot and the hill road.
  Place ferry_stage "the Highfoot stage" is room within highfoot_ward at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place far_bank "the far bank" is room within highfoot_ward at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place ferry_hut "the ferrywoman's hut" is room within highfoot_ward at 0, 1.
  Place hill_foot "the foot of the hill road" is room within hill_road at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place inn_room "the Last Pint" is room within last_inn at 1, 0.
  Place pass_gap "the gap in the hills" is room within hill_road at 2, 0 outdoors.

  Passage road_quay "the Staithe road" is road between road and quay taking 10 minutes.
  Passage heron_door "the Heron's door" is door between quay and taproom.
  Passage toll_door "the toll-house door" is door between quay and toll_counter.
  // Barge to landing: the gangplank is down where the Mary lies.
  Passage plank_staithe "the Mary's gangplank" is ferry between quay and deck taking 1 minute opening when bargeAt(1).
  Passage plank_fen "the gangplank to the fen" is ferry between fen_landing and deck taking 1 minute opening when bargeAt(2).
  Passage plank_fair "the gangplank to Pelham" is ferry between fair_quay and deck taking 1 minute opening when bargeAt(3).
  Passage plank_mill "the gangplank to the race-head" is ferry between race_head and deck taking 1 minute opening when bargeAt(4).
  Passage plank_foot "the gangplank to the Highfoot stage" is ferry between ferry_stage and deck taking 1 minute opening when bargeAt(5).
  Passage deck_cabin "the cabin hatch" is door between deck and cabin.
  Passage deck_hold "the hold hatch" is ladder between deck and hold.
  Passage deck_galley "the galley door" is door between deck and galley.

  // Fen.
  Passage fen_ways "the fen path" is path between fen_landing and causeway taking 20 minutes.
  Passage causeway_cot "the causeway to the bell" is path between causeway and bell_cot taking 20 minutes.
  Passage causeway_eels "the plank walk to the eel-stage" is path between causeway and eel_stage taking 10 minutes.
  Passage fen_to_fair "the long causeway into Pelham" is road between bell_cot and fairground taking 1 hour.
  // Pelham.
  Passage quay_fair "Quay Street" is road between fair_quay and fairground taking 10 minutes.
  Passage fair_booth "the puppet booth's flap" is doorway between fairground and puppet_booth.
  Passage fair_slops "Coyle's door" is door between fairground and draper.
  Passage fair_lines "the horse lines" is path between fairground and horse_lines taking 10 minutes.
  Passage fair_inn "the Magpie's door" is door between fair_quay and pelham_inn.
  Passage inn_lockup "the lock-up door behind the Magpie" is door between pelham_inn and lockup.
  Passage fair_to_mill "the river road to the mill" is road between horse_lines and millyard taking 2 hours.
  // Mill.
  Passage head_yard "the head-race path" is path between race_head and millyard taking 10 minutes.
  Passage yard_weir "the weir path" is path between millyard and weir taking 10 minutes.
  Passage yard_kitchen "the mill door" is door between millyard and millhouse.
  Passage yard_sluice "the sluice path" is path between millyard and sluice_hut taking 10 minutes.
  Passage weir_sluice "the top of the weir" is path between weir and sluice_hut taking 5 minutes.
  Passage mill_to_stage "the towpath to Highfoot" is road between weir and ferry_stage taking 2 hours opening when not ladsBlock() or since(250) "The towpath goes on downstream past two men in grey coats who are standing in the middle of it, not in any hurry.".
  // Highfoot.
  Passage stage_hut "the ferrywoman's door" is door between ferry_stage and ferry_hut.
  Passage ferry_across "the Highfoot ferry" is ferry between ferry_stage and far_bank taking 20 minutes opening when ferryCrossing() "The ferry lies on the far bank, and the ferrywoman is in no hurry.".
  Passage far_hill "the hill road" is road between far_bank and hill_foot taking 30 minutes.
  Passage foot_inn "the inn door" is door between hill_foot and inn_room.
  Passage foot_gap "the road to the gap" is road between hill_foot and pass_gap taking 1 hour.
}
data/adventures/wrongboat/scenes.kyr:
Module wrongboat "The Wrong Boat" {
  // ── Staithe ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe road_scene at road when true "The Staithe road comes down through a cutting to a river the colour of tea. Mist stands on the water, and under the mist two barges are lying side by side with their ropes crossed. Nobody has hung out a name.".
  Observe quay_scene at quay when true "The quay is a plank frontage a hundred paces long, and every plank of it is occupied. Sacks, a crate of geese, a bargeman asleep on a barrow, a child selling hot eels out of a bucket. Two barges lie against it, the Patient Maud and the Patient Mary, as alike as two boots, and half the shouting on the quay is about which is which.".
  Observe taproom_scene at taproom when true "The Heron and Pipe is a low room that smells of eels and pipe-ash and wet rope. Every bench has a bargeman on it. Behind the bar a stout woman in a man's coat is doing six things and shouting about a seventh.".
  Observe toll_counter_scene at toll_counter when true "A counting-room with one window onto the quay. A scale for coin, a ledger on a chain, a stove with a kettle gone cold. On the wall a list of barges and their dues, in a clerk's black hand, with three lines ruled out in red.".

  // ── The barge ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe deck_scene at deck when true "A forty-foot barge, low in the water, loaded with onions and bricks. A tiller aft, a stove-pipe amidships, washing on a line. Tarred ropes everywhere. Somebody is singing in the galley, loudly, a song with a great many verses about a miller, and the verses are getting worse.".
  Observe cabin_scene at cabin when true "A cabin like a wardrobe, with six hammocks in it. A parrot's cage, empty. A shelf with a Bible, a cribbage board and a dried eel, the eel the better thumbed.".
  Observe hold_scene at hold when true "The hold is full of onion sacks to the beams, and the air is sweet and wet and makes your eyes run. Between the sacks and the hull there is a gap, a body wide.".
  Observe galley_scene at galley when true "A stove, a copper, a table bolted to the floor. A woman the width of the doorway is stirring something with a spoon the length of an oar, and crying a little, steadily, as a woman does who has done so all her life and finds it makes the food better.".

  // ── The fen ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe fen_landing_scene at fen_landing when true "The river leaves its banks and the land leaves its edges. Reeds to the height of a house, black water between, and a plank landing with a bollard on it and a notice nailed to the bollard.".
  Observe causeway_scene at causeway when true "A raised causeway of packed brushwood and clay runs out across the fen, a cart wide, with water on both sides at the same level as the road. Eels turn in it. Every hundred paces there is a post, and on every post, in a different hand, a mark.".
  Observe bell_cot_scene at bell_cot when true "A hut on stilts at the causeway's turn, with a bell hung under the eaves, big as a coal-scuttle. A rope runs from its clapper into the hut. Someone inside pulls it once, slow, and the sound goes out over the fen and nothing in the fen answers.".
  Observe eel_stage_scene at eel_stage when true "A stage of rotten planks over the water, eel-traps stacked at one end, a skiff tied at the other. The smell is mud and smoke. Nobody has been here since morning, and a pot of something is still warm.".

  // ── Pelham ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe fair_quay_scene at fair_quay when true "Pelham quay on fair-day. Eleven barges abreast, tied bow to stern, so that a person could walk across the river without wetting a boot. The air is frying onions and horse and brass band, and nobody can hear anybody.".
  Observe fairground_scene at fairground when true "A field of tents and a thousand people moving in it in every direction at once. Gingerbread, a bear on a chain, a man selling the true cross in short lengths. Everyone is carrying something. A hamper would be nothing here.".
  Observe puppet_booth_scene at puppet_booth when true "The inside of a puppet booth: a painted cloth stage, a plank to stand on, a rack of heads. A man in his shirt is arguing in three voices with himself, in a language he has made up, and has not stopped for you.".
  Observe draper_scene at draper when true "A slop-shop, hung with coats of every trade and cut. Bargemen's smocks, a clergyman's bands, a bridegroom's waistcoat in lavender. The woman behind the counter is measuring a customer's neck with her eyes.".
  Observe horse_lines_scene at horse_lines when true "Eighty horses at a rope. A horse-dealer is being lied to by another horse-dealer, with respect. Beyond the lines the river road goes away between willows towards the mill, and there is no one on it.".
  Observe pelham_inn_scene at pelham_inn when true "The Magpie is full of men eating standing up. A fiddler is asleep in the chimney-corner with his bow in his hand. Through a hatch in the wall you can see a kitchen where nobody is cooking and everyone is shouting.".

  // ── The mill reach ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe race_head_scene at race_head when true "Where the barges leave the river for the mill-cut. A lock with a lever and a bell. The water inside is higher than the water outside, and shivers in its walls.".
  Observe millyard_scene at millyard when true "A cobbled yard with a wheel the height of a house turning behind a wall. Flour on every surface, the cart horse white to the knee. A miller's wife is beating a sack with a broom and singing under her breath, to keep time.".
  Observe weir_scene at weir when true "A long apron of wet stone with the whole of the Aldwater going over it in one sheet, white, loud, and cold in the face. A wooden walk along the top, a hand-wide, with a rail on one side. The towpath goes away along the bank on the far side of the noise.".
  Observe millhouse_scene at millhouse when true "A flagged kitchen warm as bread. A table, a dresser, a child's slate with a sum on it still unsolved. A pot of tea is stewed black and a plate of cold pie sits with a cloth over it, for somebody expected.".
  Observe sluice_hut_scene at sluice_hut when true "A hut on the lip of the weir with one iron wheel inside, tall as a man, red with rust and greased at the spindle. A painted board: FIRST TURN OPENS THE RELIEF. DO NOT THEN STAND BELOW.".

  // ── Highfoot ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe ferry_stage_scene at ferry_stage when true "The towpath ends at a stage and a chain. A flat ferry lies on the far bank. On this side a hut, a bell on a post, and a hand-lettered board that says RING ONCE.".
  Observe ferry_hut_scene at ferry_hut when true "A one-room hut with a stove and a bunk and a kettle. On the wall a row of pegs, each with a name and a coat hanging from it, and one empty peg with no name.".
  Observe far_bank_scene at far_bank when true "The far bank, high and dry, with the hills standing up behind it. A road goes up between hedges. Behind you the river is wide, and the near bank is suddenly small.".
  Observe hill_foot_scene at hill_foot when true "The road forks at a milestone. Left, an inn with a smoking chimney and a sign that has lost its picture. Right, the road to the gap, climbing between stone walls into cloud.".
  Observe inn_room_scene at inn_room when true "The Last Pint: one long room, a fire at each end, an innkeeper with a cough. A shelf of clocks, all stopped at different times, and a dog on every step of the stairs.".
  Observe pass_gap_ally at pass_gap when bessAlly(party) "The road crests in a notch between two shoulders of hill. On the other side, the sea, far off, or a kind of light that is not sky. Bess is a pace behind you, with her coin-scale hanging in her hand, looking at it.".
  Observe pass_gap_scene at pass_gap when not bessAlly(party) "The road crests in a notch between two shoulders of hill. On the other side, the sea, far off, or a kind of light that is not sky. Nobody is behind you on the road. Nobody is in front of you either, which is new.".
}
data/adventures/wrongboat/wake.kyr:
Module wrongboat "The Wrong Boat" {
  // ── Chapters, aims, and the ways it can end ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Chapter ch_quay "The Wrong Boat" when true "Two barges that look alike, a quay full of shouting, a mist that is lifting. Somebody is about to hand you something.".
  Chapter ch_afloat "Afloat" when since(9) and been(party, deck) "The Mary goes down the Aldwater at a walking pace, with onions, with a song, with the quay getting smaller and a thing in your pack that you cannot put down.".
  Chapter ch_fen "The Fen" when been(party, fen_landing) "Reeds, mist, one road, and every sound is a long way off or right beside you.".
  Chapter ch_fair "Pelham on Fair-day" when been(party, fairground) "A great many people, no one of whom is looking for you, and one of whom is.".
  Chapter ch_mill "The Mill Reach" when been(party, millyard) "A weir, a lock, a lever, and two men in grey coats standing on the path as if they had been planted.".
  Chapter ch_foot "Highfoot" when been(party, ferry_stage) "The last of the river. After this there is only the hill, and whatever you have chosen to carry up it.".

  Objective get_away when t0() > 0 and not boxReturned(party) and not caught(party) and not bessTook(party) "Get down the Aldwater and over the hills before a toll-clerk, or the Trust's two lads, catch you with something that is not yours.".
  Objective what_is_it when holding(party, music_box) and not drawerOpen(party) "There is a music box in the hamper. It plays a tune everyone on the river knows. It has a back-plate nobody has looked behind.".
  Objective hob_wait when hobMet(party) and not boxReturned(party) "Hob Garrod is in the Pelham lock-up, and has asked that Bess Lowther be told.".

  Milestone m_afloat "got away from Staithe on the wrong boat" worth 100 when been(party, deck).
  Milestone m_accused "was shouted at on a quay for a hamper" worth 60 when accused(party).
  Milestone m_fen "crossed the Wend Fen" worth 120 when been(party, bell_cot) or been(party, eel_stage).
  Milestone m_fair "went through Pelham on fair-day and was not caught" worth 150 when been(party, fairground) and been(party, millyard).
  Milestone m_lie "lied to a woman's face about a box" worth 120 when liedToBess(party).
  Milestone m_tune "heard the song the box was made for" worth 100 when knows(party, tune_known).
  Milestone m_plate "read what was scratched in the back-plate" worth 150 when knows(party, maker_known).
  Milestone m_hob "heard Hob Garrod out" worth 100 when hobMet(party).
  Milestone m_gap "got to the gap in the hills" worth 300 when been(party, pass_gap).
    Milestone m_chain "crossed the Highfoot ferry chain hand over hand" worth 200 when chained(party) and not chainFell(party).

  // What the chances of the river leave behind.
  Observe galley_duty near teague when galleyDuty(party) and at(party, galley) "You have been peeling since Staithe. There is an onion in your hair, and Mrs Brabant has given up apologising for it.".
  Observe bess_pitied_note near bess when bessPitied(party) and bessMet(party) "Bess has stopped hurrying. She is still coming, but she is walking now.".
  Observe bess_hob_note near bess when hobKnown(party) and bessAlly(party) "Bess has asked three times how far to Pelham, and the third time she did not wait for the answer.".
  Observe shim_loyal_note near shim when shimLoyal(party) and travelsWith(shim, party) and at(party, weir) "Shim looks at the water and then, carefully, at nothing.".

  // Fiasco at the fair: the one thing nobody can see coming is a horse.
  Relation tradedDally(group).
  Action trade_to_dally(actor: group, site: place) "Trade the music box to Mr Dally for his horse, Parnassus" {
    Speaker dally.
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, horse_lines) and travelsWith(dally, actor) and holding(actor, music_box) and dallyBolted(actor) and not tradedDally(actor) and not bessAlly(actor).
    Time 0.
    On success { Spend music_box from actor. Assert tradedDally(actor). }
    Result "'For Hester,' says Mr Dally, taking it like a diploma. 'For when she asks why I was late, and why I came, and where I got a music box.' He gives you the reins of a long-faced bay with a look of grave surprise. 'He is a fine horse,' he says. 'He does not like going forwards.'".
  }

  // ── Endings ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Ending beaten "Left on the Towpath" when beatenUp(party) "The larger lad did not mean it. That is said afterwards, a good deal, in the Trust's room over the toll-house, and nobody is persuaded. Whatever there was goes back down the bank in a sack with the smaller one holding it, not counting what is left. The river keeps on going, loud and unconcerned, and you lie there and listen to it.".
  Ending chain_fell "The Aldwater Keeps It" when chainFell(party) "You are over, with your hands skinned and your pack light. On the stage behind you the ones who were after you have come to the edge and stopped. They look at the water. Then they turn and go back up the planks without a word, because there is nothing in the river worth the wetting.".
  Ending caught "Taken on the Towpath" when caught(party) "The larger lad has what he came for under his arm, and the smaller has not looked at you once. You walk on with your pack light and your hands empty.".
  Ending bess_took "Her Hands on the Box" when bessTook(party) "She has what she came for, and she has not hurt anyone, and it is the worst of all the things that could have happened. She carries it away from you in both hands, up the bank, and you do not follow, because there is nothing to follow for. Behind, it begins to play, and she walks faster.".
  Ending gave_hob "The Rightful Owner, Technically" when gaveHob(party) "By the next morning the box is at Fosse's, and the forty coin is in the Magpie's till, and Hob Garrod is out of his cell and standing at the bar on a very good voice. The toll-clerk walks into Pelham on the afternoon boat with a dust-coat over her black sleeves, and is told by a pot-boy, who thinks it is a joke, which way he went. You are on the hill by then, and you do not see her face, which is a mercy, and one that you chose.".
  Ending returned "The Lowther Kitchen" when boxReturned(party) and ladsDealt() "Bess Lowther carries it home in both hands, as if it might spill, and sets it on the table in the room over the toll-house. She does not wind it. She sits and looks at it until the light goes. You were not asked to stay, and you do not, but you hear it from the street, at the third winding, when she finally does. It plays the tune right through, and then there is a small sound, like a latch.".
  Ending returned_taken "The Lowther Kitchen, Briefly" when boxReturned(party) "Bess Lowther carries it home in both hands and sets it on the table in the room over the toll-house, and sits and looks at it until the light goes. In the morning there are two men in grey coats at the door, who are polite, and who have a paper. She does not wind it. She puts the key in her pocket, and when they have gone with the box she goes on sitting in front of the place on the table where it was.".
  Ending bargain "A Glorious Bad Bargain" when tradedDally(party) "You ride out of the horse lines on the long-faced bay, who goes sideways, and Mr Dally leaves on foot with a music box under his arm and every church bell in the county against him. At the third milestone the horse stops and looks at you with great intelligence. At the fourth it lies down. Three hours later a stout man with a gun and a pale girl with a dog pass in a wagon the other way, and Mr Dally is in the back of it holding the music box and saying, with enormous dignity, that he has never been so happy. The horse has got up.".
  Ending delivered "Forty Coin and a Back-plate" when soldQuill(party) and not boxKnown(party) "Barnaby Fosse winds it once as you leave, to see it work. It plays to the end. 'B.L., from T.L.,' he says to the shelf of stopped clocks. You are halfway to the gap with forty coin before you turn, and look back at the inn with the sign that has lost its picture, and wish you had read the plate first.".
  Ending delivered_known "Forty Coin, Knowing" over delivered when soldQuill(party) and boxKnown(party) "Barnaby Fosse winds it once, to see it work, and it plays to the end. You read the plate yourself before you let go. You sold it anyway. The forty coin is real and heavy, and the clock-mender does not say a word to you about it, which is a courtesy.".
  Ending hand_over_hand "Hand over Hand" when chained(party) and not chainFell(party) and at(party, far_bank) "You lie on the far stones with your hands burning and the box where it was. Across the river the stage is a small plank rectangle with two people on it, not shouting, and the ferry swinging empty on its chain. Una stands in her door with her arms folded. She keeps her arms folded. She lifts one hand a little, as at a boy who has done a thing in the water that she once did herself.".
  Ending shim_pelham "Tobacco for Hob" over lost_friend when at(party, pass_gap) and shimGone(party) and shimSeesHob(party) and not shimBetrayed(party) "At the crest you turn, and Pelham is a smear of smoke with a fair in it, and somewhere in the smear a lad in a cap is walking up Quay Street with a screw of tobacco in his fist, to sit on a step outside a lock-up and not say anything. You wave anyway.".
  Ending lost_friend "Without Shim" over the_weir when at(party, pass_gap) and shimGone(party) "The gap is windy and bare. You have the road, and you do not have the boy who shouted the news of every barge on the river at nobody. At the crest you turn, once, and below at the Highfoot stage, small as a pin, there is a figure with its hand up. You wave. You cannot tell if he sees.".
  Ending to_his_face "Said to His Face" over with_bess when at(party, pass_gap) and bessReunited(party) "You come over the gap without her. She stayed in Pelham with a man on a bench, which is a place nobody would have chosen for a reunion, and what was said in it you only heard the beginning of. On the crest you look back once. A thin smoke is going up from the Magpie's chimney, and it is a long way off, and you cannot tell if there is one person under it or two.".
  Ending with_bess "Bess at the Gap" over lost_friend when at(party, pass_gap) and bessAlly(party) and not bessReunited(party) and holding(party, music_box) "Bess Lowther stops at the crest with her coin-scale hanging forgotten in her hand and looks out at the hills as if they had been put there as a courtesy. 'I've never been this far,' she says. 'I'd supposed the river was all there was.' She holds out her hand, and you give her the box, and she does not wind it. 'Not till I've said it to him,' she says. She turns back down the hill alone, towards Pelham and a man in a lock-up. You stand on the crest with your hands empty and your faces cold.".
  Ending shim_loyal "Blood Is Blood" over with_shim when at(party, pass_gap) and shimGoesOn(party) and shimLoyal(party) and travelsWith(shim, party) "Shim comes up the hill behind you, not ahead, with his bundle and his eyes on his boots. At the crest he turns and looks down at a river you cannot see from here and a man in a lock-up you told him not to mind. 'I said I would,' he says. 'I will.' He does not shout the news of the sea. It would be unfair to ask him to.".
  Ending with_shim "Shim at the Gap" over clean when at(party, pass_gap) and shimGoesOn(party) and travelsWith(shim, party) "Shim comes up the last of the hill ahead of you, three yards at a time, and stands in the notch with his bundle and shouts the news of the sea at it. 'IT'S A VERY LARGE ONE!' he says. 'IT'S GOT NOTHING ON IT!' He has never been further than Pelham.".
  Ending peal_love "A Peal Behind You" over clean when at(party, pass_gap) and dallyWed(party) and dallyLoves(party) "Down the valley, small, a flat cracked bell is going, and going, and has got into the rhythm of a thing that is being rung by someone who will not stop for a gun. You do not hear a shot. You stand on the crest and listen for one anyway, and Mr Dally, you decide, is the only man you have met this week who got exactly what he went for.".
  Ending peal_cold "The Wrong Church, and Then the Right One" over clean when at(party, pass_gap) and dallyWed(party) "Somewhere below, a bell is ringing at the wrong hour for a wedding, and then, after a pause the length of a sensible man changing his mind, at the right one. Nobody told Mr Dally he was in love. He went anyway, with his flower, and you will never find out if it was courage or the gun.".
  Ending cashed "Fifty Coin and No Questions" when at(party, pass_gap) and soldHonest(party) "You come over the gap with fifty coin, which is as much as most people get from a river. Behind, a horse-dealer winds a music box for his wife, and in a toll-house at Staithe a woman sits on her stool with three red lines in the ledger and a face like a closed door.".
  Ending empty "Empty Hands" when at(party, pass_gap) and dropped(party) "You cross the gap with nothing in your hands at all. It is a clear morning, and the hills go on. Somewhere under the Aldwater a box of dark wood is lying in the mud with its spring let go, and every so often, when the current moves it, it plays one note, and stops.".
  Ending una_end "Tom, Behind You, Always" over clean when at(party, pass_gap) and unaSung(party) and boxWound(party) and holding(party, music_box) "On the crest you turn once to look at the river and find that you can see the whole of the Highfoot stage, with a small upright figure at the end of it, still, leaning on a boathook. She is not looking at you. She is looking at the pack. It is some time before you understand that she is listening for it.".
  Ending brabant_end "What Mrs Brabant Said" over clean when at(party, pass_gap) and teagueSaw(party) and holding(party, music_box) and not boxReturned(party) and not hobTold(party) and not bessAlly(party) "You have come over the gap with the box, and a cook in a steam-filled galley told you whose it was and where to take it, and you did not. You wind it once at the crest, to find out whether it feels different. It does not, quite. It plays the same six notes, and the tune turns in the middle, and you think of a spoon that stopped.".
  Ending hob_unsaid "A Message Not Passed" over cashed when at(party, pass_gap) and hobAsked(party) and not hobTold(party) and not bessAlly(party) and not boxReturned(party) "A man on a bench in Pelham with his hat over his face said he was in the lock-up, and had no money, and that it was the one place on the river she would know where to find him. You were to tell her. Over the gap you can still see the smoke of Pelham, if you look back, which you try not to.".
  Ending quill_end "A Bargeman's Initials" over clean when at(party, pass_gap) and quillRead(party) and holding(party, music_box) "Fosse gave it back and would not buy it, which is the best offer you had on the river and the only one you did not take. You carry it up the gap with the back-plate to the light. B.L. FROM T.L. You are not sure, still, what a decent person does with it. You are sure that you now know what it is.".
  Ending pitied "Walking, Not Running" over clean when at(party, pass_gap) and bessPitied(party) and not bessAlly(party) and not boxReturned(party) "A long way down the hill road behind you, small and black-sleeved, a woman is walking. Not running. She said it was not hers to ask for and then she believed you, or she stopped minding; you cannot tell which from here. You do not wait.".
  Ending peeled "Paid in Onions" over clean when at(party, pass_gap) and galleyDuty(party) "You smell of onions. You will smell of onions for a week, and a cook in a galley on the Mary will tell the story of three passengers who peeled, for nothing, from Staithe to Pelham, and did not fall in the copper.".
  Ending tea_end "Tea, and No One to See" over clean when at(party, pass_gap) and teaTaken(party) "You drank it standing in a miller's yard with flour on every surface and a woman who beat a sack and did not look at you. It was good tea. You are over the gap now, and you still cannot tell the miller's wife whether you were running from a man or toward one, and you have a notion that she knew.".
  Ending dally_flight "Still Flying" over clean when at(party, pass_gap) and dallyBolted(party) and travelsWith(dally, party) "Mr Dally comes up the last of the hill behind you with the dead flower in his buttonhole, looking back down the valley at every third step, and not once at the sea. At the crest he sits on a stone. 'I think,' he says, 'that I have been rather a coward.' Then, 'Is there anywhere further?'".
  Ending the_weir "Down the Weir" over clean when at(party, pass_gap) and holding(party, music_box) and ladsSwept(party) "You come over the gap with the box. The sergeant will say he sent them for a lost dog, and one of them will say nothing at all for a week. Wilfred Auster fished out the second with a boathook, and has not mentioned your name to the Trust, because nobody has asked, and because he is a miller and not a fool.".
  Ending hamper "Over the Gap with a Hamper" when at(party, pass_gap) and holding(party, hamper_kind) "You have carried it all the way up the hill, unopened, as you were told. At the crest you put it down and look at the label, DO NOT OPEN, in a hand that falls off its Ds like a roof. Nobody is behind you. You are still not sure whose it is. You sit on it, and eat a cake you do not have, and look at the sea.".
  Ending clean "Clean Water" when at(party, pass_gap) and holding(party, music_box) and not boxKnown(party) "The gap is a notch in the hills with the sea beyond, or a light that is not sky. You have the box and the road, and as far as you can see nobody behind you. You wind it, there on the crest, to see what all the fuss was, and it plays the whole tune, a man's tune, written in a hurry for a wife, and the wind takes it away down the other side.".
  Ending known_keeping "B.L. from T.L." over clean when at(party, pass_gap) and holding(party, music_box) and boxKnown(party) "You know what it is, and you have it, and the gap is a notch in the hills with the sea beyond. You wind it on the crest. It plays the tune the river sings, as the man wrote it, before the verses. There is nobody to give it to. You put it back in the pack, and carry it down.".
  Ending gap_any "Over the Gap" when at(party, pass_gap) "You come over the gap with nothing to show for the river but the river. It will do to be going on with.".
}

{
  "about": "What a town's shrine holds about a deep site's seal, and the ways a company may argue it out, each tried once (src/world/deep/deep-argument.ts binds it into each deep site that has a seal and a town with a priest). In what is said, {priest} is the priest, said by their name; {name} is the deep site's name; {noun} is what the seal is asked about (the walled stair), {opened} what it opens, {cut} what is cut on it, {carry} what the shrine would have the company take below. In a move, needs is what it asks besides the priest's having spoken, check the roll it is (a skill and how hard), won whether it wins the priest over, learn a fact it teaches ({grief}: the priest's grief), caught whether a failed try shuts the shrine to the company, always whether even a won try does; {bane} is the fact of the keeper's bane.",
  "grief": "{priest}'s brother went down into {name} and did not come back up. What {priest} says of {opened} is grief as much as doctrine.",
  "ask": "Ask {priest} about {noun} in {name}",
  "stand": "'The makers shut {opened} themselves,' says {priest}, 'and they knew what they were doing. What they shut in, they shut in for all of us. Open it, and I will not pray for you, nor heal you, nor sit up with your dead.'",
  "again": "Ask {priest} again about {noun}",
  "careful": "'Go carefully,' says {priest}.",
  "carry": " 'And take {carry} with you, if you find it.'",
  "told": "Then {priest} tells you what the shrine has always kept of it: {bane_said}",
  "moves": [
    { "id": "evidence", "label": "Tell {priest} what {cut} say", "needs": "knows(actor, {bane})", "check": "persuasion, dc_easy", "won": true,
      "yes": "{priest} hears the words out, and is quiet for a while. 'If the makers wrote that, they meant it to be read,' {priest} says at last. 'And meant someone to go down with the light.'",
      "no": "{priest} hears the words out, and is not moved. 'Words cut in stone,' says {priest}. 'Anyone can cut words.'" },
    { "id": "argue", "label": "Argue with {priest} that what is below should be met, not walled in", "check": "persuasion, dc_hard", "won": true,
      "yes": "{priest} argues it with you point by point, and gives way on the last one. 'Then go,' says {priest}, 'but go as if it mattered.'",
      "no": "{priest} argues it with you point by point, and gives way on none of them." },
    { "id": "read", "label": "Watch {priest} for what goes unsaid", "check": "insight, dc_fair", "learn": "{grief}",
      "yes": "It is in how {priest} says 'down there': not as doctrine, but as a place someone went.",
      "no": "Whatever goes unsaid, you do not see it." },
    { "id": "grief", "label": "Speak to {priest} of the brother who went down", "needs": "knows(actor, {grief})", "check": "persuasion, dc_easy", "won": true,
      "yes": "{priest} looks at you a long time. 'He went down into {name} and no one went after him,' says {priest}. 'If you are going, go after him too.'",
      "no": "{priest} turns away. 'You know nothing about it,' says {priest}, and that is the end of it." },
    { "id": "lie", "label": "Tell {priest} the keepers of names sent you to see to {opened}", "check": "deception, dc_hard", "won": true, "caught": true,
      "yes": "{priest} looks at you for a long moment, and nods. 'Then see to it,' says {priest}.",
      "no": "{priest} looks at you for a long moment. 'The keepers send their own,' says {priest}. 'Get out of my shrine.'" },
    { "id": "threat", "label": "Tell {priest} {opened} will be opened whatever is said", "check": "intimidation, dc_fair", "won": true, "caught": true, "always": true,
      "yes": "{priest} goes white, and tells you what you came to hear, to be rid of you. There will be nothing more for you from this shrine.",
      "no": "{priest} is not afraid of you. 'Then open it without me,' says {priest}, 'and bury your own dead.'" }
  ],
  "promise": { "label": "Promise {priest} to shut {opened} again when you come back up",
    "yes": "{priest} takes your hand in both hands. 'Then I will hold you to it,' says {priest}. {told}" },
  "broken": "{priest} looks past you at the door. 'You promised to shut it again,' says {priest}, and nothing more to you, then or after.",
  "shut": "{priest} will not look at you. The shrine is shut to whoever opened {opened} against its word."
}
