        "things": [{"id": "boat", "name": "the dug-out boat", "seen": "A dug-out boat lies upside down under the alders.", "closer": "The boat is a single oak trunk, hollowed by fire and adze, black with age and still sound. Its paddle lies underneath, and its bow is carved into a beast's head, worn nearly smooth.", "known": "A beast's head on the bow was the fen-folk's way before the drainers came. A boat like this is a hundred years old if it is a day, and somebody has kept it sound."}] },
      { "id": "mere", "name": "the mere", "scene": "Open water: a mere ringed with reed, so still it holds the sky. Old stakes stand in a line out into it and stop, as if a path had once gone further.", "ambience": "A grebe dives and comes up a long way off.",
        "things": [{"id": "stakes", "name": "the line of stakes", "seen": "Old stakes stand in a line out into the mere.", "closer": "The stakes are black oak, sharpened at the top. Where the line stops you can see, under the surface, a sunken causeway going on toward the middle.", "known": "A causeway out to the middle of a mere goes to something: a hold on an island long since sunk, or a place where things were given to the water. The old fen-folk did both."}] },
      { "id": "sluice", "name": "the broken sluice", "scene": "A sluice of squared timbers stands half in the water, its gate gone, a channel running straight as a rule away from it into the reed. Somebody drained this fen once, or meant to.", "ambience": "Water talks in the broken gate.",
        "things": [{"id": "post", "name": "the sluice-post", "seen": "The sluice-post is cut all over with marks.", "closer": "At every height the water has reached, somebody has cut a line in the post with a year beside it. The highest mark is above your head.", "known": "The years go back two hundred winters, and the highest marks are the oldest of all. The fen is drier than it was, though nobody finished draining it."}] },
      { "id": "staithe", "name": "the reed landing", "scene": "A landing of piled faggots where the reed-cutters bring their bundles out. Cut reed is stacked here in ricks, waiting for a boat.", "ambience": "Reed-buntings sit on the ricks.",
        "things": [{"id": "ricks", "name": "the reed ricks", "seen": "Ricks of cut reed stand on the staithe.", "closer": "The reed is tied in bundles a fathom round, the way thatchers buy it. Chalked on the end of the nearest rick is a tally, and a mark like a bird's foot."}] }
    ],
    "water": [
      { "id": "ford", "name": "the ford of the {river}", "scene": "The {river} spreads out slow and brown through the fen, and a line of stones lets you cross it, if you are careful where you put your feet.", "ambience": "Eels move under the stones.",
        "things": [{"id": "stones", "name": "the crossing-stones", "seen": "A line of stones crosses the {river}.", "closer": "One stone in the middle rocks under a foot. Somebody has set a white pebble on the stone after it, as a warning to the next to cross."}] },
      { "id": "punt", "name": "the punt-crossing of the {river}", "scene": "A flat-bottomed punt is tied to a post on this bank of the {river}, with a rope running across to the far side to pull it by.", "ambience": "The rope creaks as the current leans on the punt.",
        "things": [{"id": "box", "name": "the fare-box", "seen": "A wooden box is nailed to the punt's post.", "closer": "The box has a slot in its lid and a few coppers in the bottom: the fare, left on trust for whoever keeps the punt."}] }
    ],
    "view": { "change": "Climb the willow and look out over {zone}", "seen": "From the willow you can see over the reed: the channels, the open water, the line of firm ground, and which way it all goes.", "unseen": "The willow's lowest fork is shoulder-high." }
  },
  "heath": {
    "trails": ["an old drove-way", "a sheep-trod through the heather", "a peat-road", "a line of marker posts"],
    "into": "the track up onto {zone}",
    "hint": "A sheep-trod goes off through the heather here, but no sheep made it: there are boot-nails in the peat, and the heather is cut back at the turns.",
    "entry": { "name": "the foot of {zone} by {from}", "scene": "The fields give way to heather and gorse, and the land rises to the moor. {from} is behind you and below." },
    "lost": { "name": "somewhere on {zone}", "scene": "Somewhere on {zone}. Heather in every direction, the same low hummocks, and a sky with no sun in it to steer by.", "astray": "The trod you were following thins to nothing in the heather. Every rise looks like the last, and the mist has the far ones.", "guided": "{?m} kneels to see which way the heather lies, then stands and points. 'That way.' It is." },
    "landmarks": [
      { "id": "cairn", "name": "the cairn", "view": true, "scene": "A cairn of grey stones stands on the highest ground, taller than a man, every traveller's stone added to it. You can see a long way from here.", "ambience": "A curlew calls, a long way off.",
        "things": [{"id": "stones", "name": "the stones of the cairn", "seen": "The cairn is built of every kind of stone the moor has.", "closer": "Every kind the moor has, and some it hasn't: a lump of white quartz, a piece of red brick, a sea-pebble a long way from any sea.", "known": "The custom is old: every traveller adds a stone for luck on the way, and so the cairn grows. The sea-pebble came farther than anyone walks now.", "do": {"name": "Add a stone of your own to the cairn", "done": "Your stone is on the cairn now, with everyone else's."}}] },
      { "id": "stone", "name": "the leaning stone", "scene": "A single standing stone, taller than a rider, leans out of the heather as if it were listening. The ground at its foot is bare, as though something walks round it.", "ambience": "Wind hums on the edge of the stone.",
        "things": [{"id": "ring", "name": "the bare ring round the stone", "seen": "The heather is worn away in a ring round the stone's foot.", "closer": "The ring is a path, beaten by feet going round and round, sunwise. Sheep do not walk sunwise. At the foot of the stone is a hole, worn smooth, with something in it.", "by": "rites", "known": "People walk three times sunwise round a stone like this to ask it something, and leave the asking in the hole at its foot. What is in it now is a lock of hair, tied with thread.", "do": {"name": "Walk three times round the stone, sunwise", "done": "You have walked three times round the stone, sunwise. Nothing that you can see has changed."}}] },
      { "id": "bothy", "name": "the shepherds' bothy", "scene": "A bothy of piled stone and turf, roofed with heather, with a fold for sheep against its back wall. The ashes in its hearth are not very old.", "ambience": "A wheatear flits from the wall to the fold and back.",
        "things": [{"id": "hearth", "name": "the bothy hearth", "seen": "Ashes not long cold lie in the bothy's hearth.", "closer": "Kindling is stacked dry under the hearth-stone, as shepherds leave it for the next one caught out on the moor.", "find": {"kind": "herbs", "name": "a twist of dried herbs", "seen": "In a niche in the wall is a twist of dried herbs, left the same way."}}] },
      { "id": "peat", "name": "the peat cuttings", "scene": "The moor has been cut away in long black steps, and the peats stand drying in little stacks of three, row after row. Water lies in the bottom of the cuttings.", "ambience": "Bog-cotton nods along the edge of the cuttings.",
        "things": [{"id": "face", "name": "the cut face of the peat", "seen": "The cut face of the peat stands black and wet.", "closer": "In the cut face, a spade's depth down, runs a line of grey: wood, a birch branch as fresh as the day it fell, though there is no tree within a mile.", "known": "Peat keeps whatever falls into it. This moor was a birchwood once, before the peat grew over it, and that branch has lain in the dark ever since."}] },
      { "id": "dewpond", "name": "the dewpond", "scene": "A round pond lined with clay lies in a hollow of the moor, with no stream to fill it. The sheep come to it from miles, and the mud round it is printed all over.", "ambience": "Skylarks go up and up over the pond.",
        "things": [{"id": "lining", "name": "the pond's clay lining", "seen": "Where the sheep have trodden the pond's edge, its lining shows.", "closer": "Under the trodden edge: puddled clay over a bed of straw over chalk, laid as fine as a floor. No stream fills this pond; it was made to hold the dew and the rain.", "known": "Dewpond-makers kept their craft in families and walked the moors making ponds for whoever would pay. One of them made this one, and it has held longer than the bothy has stood."}] }
    ],
    "water": [
      { "id": "ford", "name": "the ford of the {river}", "scene": "The {river} runs brown off the peat between banks of heather, shallow over flat stones.", "ambience": "A dipper bobs on a stone in the stream.",
        "things": [{"id": "flats", "name": "the flat stones of the ford", "seen": "Flat stones pave the bed of the {river} at the ford.", "closer": "The stones are laid, not lying: a pavement under the water, wide enough for a cart, the edges worn round by a long time of wheels.", "by": "wayfinding", "known": "A paved ford on the open moor means a road once ran here that is a sheep-trod now: the drove road that went over the tops before the valley road was made."}] }
    ],
    "view": { "change": "Climb the cairn and look out over {zone}", "seen": "From the top of the cairn the moor lies open all round: the trods, the streams, the far edge where the fields begin.", "unseen": "The stones of the cairn make a rough stair." }
  },
  "fell": {
    "trails": ["a sheep-trod along the fellside", "a cairned path", "a scree path", "a wall-side track"],
    "into": "the path up onto {zone}",
    "hint": "A small cairn stands a little off the path, too small for a waymark and too neat to have fallen so: someone marked a way off from here.",
    "entry": { "name": "the foot of {zone} by {from}", "scene": "The ground steepens. Walls run up the fellside and give out where the bracken begins. {from} is behind you, in the valley." },
    "lost": { "name": "somewhere on {zone}", "scene": "Somewhere on {zone}. Rock and scree and cloud, and the ground falling away on more sides than one.", "astray": "The cloud comes down, and with it the end of the path. Every way you turn the ground falls away into grey.", "guided": "{?m} watches the cloud a while, picks out a wall running down the fellside, and follows it. It brings you where you meant to go." },
    "landmarks": [
      { "id": "tarn", "name": "the mountain lake", "scene": "A tarn lies in a hollow under a crag, so dark it looks bottomless, with a little beach of grey gravel at one end. The wind falls silent here.", "ambience": "A raven croaks from the crag above.",
        "things": [{"id": "beach", "name": "the gravel beach", "seen": "A little beach of grey gravel lies at the tarn's end.", "closer": "At the water's edge the gravel is mixed with chips of a greenish stone, flaked and sharp. Somebody sat here once and worked blades.", "known": "It is axe-stone, the green stone of the high fells, worked here and carried down to the valleys in the time before bronze."}] },
      { "id": "fold", "name": "the sheepfold", "scene": "A round fold of dry-stone walling stands on a shelf of the fell, its gate a hurdle tied with twine. Sheep have been in it lately.", "ambience": "Sheep on the slope above stop chewing to look at you.",
        "things": [{"id": "gate", "name": "the hurdle gate", "seen": "The fold's gate is a hurdle tied with twine.", "closer": "The twine is new. The shepherd's mark is on the gatepost in red, a bar and a ring, and the hurdle has been patched with hazel this year.", "by": "woodcraft", "known": "The droppings in the fold are a day or two old: the shepherd brought the flock in to sort it, and will bring it in again before the weather turns."}] },
      { "id": "crag", "name": "the crag", "view": true, "scene": "A crag stands out of the fellside like a broken tooth, with a ledge you could stand on and a long fall below it. From the top you would see the whole valley.", "ambience": "Ravens tumble in the wind under the crag.",
        "things": [{"id": "ledge", "name": "the ledge", "seen": "A ledge runs out along the face of the crag.", "closer": "On the ledge, out of the wind, is a ravens' nest of sticks and wool, and in the wool a scrap of red cloth and the bowl of a clay pipe.", "by": "woodcraft", "known": "Ravens take whatever catches their eye. The cloth and the pipe came up from the valley, a long way, in a beak."}] },
      { "id": "shieling", "name": "the herders' summer huts", "scene": "Two huts of stone and turf stand by a beck on a green shelf of the fell, where cattle are brought up in summer. One still has its roof.", "ambience": "The beck chatters past the huts.",
        "things": [{"id": "kist", "name": "the kist in the roofed hut", "seen": "In the roofed hut stands a kist with a lid of turf.", "closer": "In the hut are a stone bench, a cheese-press of two flat stones, and the kist, empty but for a horn spoon.", "find": {"kind": "rope", "name": "a coil of rope", "seen": "Coiled in the bottom of the kist is a rope, left there over the winter."}}] },
      { "id": "col", "name": "the high pass", "scene": "A saddle of bare ground between two summits, where the wind comes through hard and the ground is worn to the rock. A cairn marks the way down either side.", "ambience": "The wind never stops.",
        "things": [{"id": "cairns", "name": "the cairns of the way down", "seen": "A cairn marks the way down either side of the col.", "closer": "Each cairn has a long flat stone on top, pointing down its own side of the col: what a traveller caught in cloud would need, set by somebody who had been.", "by": "wayfinding", "known": "The pointing stones are an old kindness of the fells: follow the cairns down and you will come out where people are, whatever the cloud does."}] }
    ],
    "water": [
      { "id": "ford", "name": "the stepping-stones over the {river}", "scene": "The {river} comes down off the fell here in a white rush, and someone has set stepping-stones across where it runs widest.", "ambience": "Spray hangs over the stones.",
        "things": [{"id": "blocks", "name": "the stepping-stones", "seen": "The stepping-stones stand square in the white water.", "closer": "They are not the fell's own stone: they are dressed blocks, square, each with a groove along it where something once ran.", "known": "Grooved for a door or a sluice-gate, they came from a building and were carried up here to be stepped on. Something stood in this valley once that was pulled down for its stone."}] }
    ],
    "view": { "change": "Climb the crag and look out over {zone}", "seen": "From the top of the crag the whole of {zone} is laid out: the paths, the becks, the folds, and the valley road below.", "unseen": "A crack runs up the crag that a careful climber could use." }
  }

data/generation/scenes/wonders.json:
{
  "about": "How each of Orsino's wonders whose effect Kyr can run (orsino-world.json) stands in a generated country: in the wild country or within a work; what it is called when pointed at; how it looks before anyone meets it; how it is approached; what happens to whoever does; and how it is after. Written by hand: Orsino gives a wonder's description and effect, not what it is to meet one.",
  "wonders": {
    "ancient_trees": { "where": "wild", "name": "the great tree", "verb": "Lay a hand on", "seen": "A tree far older than the country round it stands alone here, its roots heaved up out of the ground like the backs of sleeping animals. Close to, the bark seems to move, very slowly, as if it breathed.", "taken": "The bark is warm. Something slow and green comes up out of the roots and through your palm, and old hurts close.", "after": "The great tree stands as trees stand. Whatever answered your hand is asleep in it again." },
    "arcane_clock": { "where": "within", "name": "the clock", "verb": "Wind", "seen": "A clock stands against the wall, taller than a man, its face marked with more hours than a day has. The hand moves, stops, and goes back a little.", "taken": "The key turns once. The clock runs backwards a little, and then you are moving faster than the dust falls.", "after": "The clock has stopped at no hour you know." },
    "arcane_lantern": { "where": "within", "name": "the lantern", "verb": "Take up", "seen": "A lantern hangs from a hook in the wall with nothing in it to burn, and still it gives a light, thin and white, that falls on the stone and shows the joins in it no lamp would.", "taken": "The handle is cold. You lift it, and for a moment everything the light touches is only what it is, every seam and every lie in it plain; when you set it down, your eyes keep something of it.", "after": "The lantern hangs dark on its hook, a lantern and no more." },
    "arcane_symbols": { "where": "within", "name": "the glowing symbols", "verb": "Trace", "seen": "Symbols are cut into the stone in rows, and a light moves along them groove by groove, slow as a pulse.", "taken": "Your finger follows the lines, and the pulse in them goes up your arm; the room goes very sharp and clear.", "after": "The symbols are only cut stone now, dark in their grooves." },
    "arcane_well": { "where": "wild", "name": "the well", "verb": "Drink from", "seen": "A well stands out here with no house near it, its curb worn smooth. The water is a long way down, and smells of rain that has not fallen here.", "taken": "The water is colder than any water here and tastes of somewhere else. Your hurts ease as it goes down.", "after": "The well is dry to the bottom, as if it had only been waiting for one drink." },
    "celestial_fountain": { "where": "within", "name": "the fountain", "verb": "Drink from", "seen": "A fountain plays in a stone basin, and the water coming out of it is full of light, as if it had been out under the sun all day.", "taken": "The water is full of light. It goes down like a warm hand and stays round you like a cloak.", "after": "The basin holds only rainwater now." },
    "celestial_glow": { "where": "wild", "name": "the glow", "verb": "Step into", "seen": "A light lies on the ground here that has nothing to do with the sky: soft, pale, and the shape of a door laid flat.", "taken": "The light is on you like weather. Where it touches, your skin goes hard and faintly scaled, like a fish's.", "after": "The glow has gone up out of the place, and the light here is ordinary light." },
    "celestial_map": { "where": "within", "name": "the star map", "verb": "Study", "seen": "A map is painted over the wall and the ceiling: stars, and the lines between them, and countries that are on no map of this world.", "taken": "The stars on it are not ours. One of them burns as you look, and you understand how: you could call that burning down.", "after": "The map is faded paint, its stars only gilt." },
    "celestial_observatory": { "where": "within", "name": "the star-glass", "verb": "Look through", "seen": "A brass tube as long as a boat lies on a stand under an opening in the roof, pointed at one piece of sky.", "taken": "Through the glass the sky is close and full of falling stones, and you learn the way of bringing them down.", "after": "The glass is cracked across and shows nothing." },
    "color_shifts": { "where": "wild", "name": "the shifting colours", "verb": "Walk into", "seen": "The heather here is the wrong colour, and then another wrong colour: the ground goes slowly through shades no plant has, and back.", "taken": "The colours wash over you, and after them acid and light and worse seem things that would slide off you.", "after": "The colours have gone out of the place and left it its own." },
    "dancing_lights": { "where": "wild", "name": "the dancing lights", "verb": "Follow", "seen": "Small lights move over the ground in twos and threes, weaving round one another, as if dancing to something you cannot hear.", "taken": "You go after them, stepping where they step, and when they go out you are lighter on your feet than you have ever been.", "after": "There are no lights now, only the place." },
    "eerie_chimes": { "where": "wild", "name": "the chimes", "verb": "Listen to", "seen": "Someone has hung chimes of thin metal from a dead tree, and when the wind moves them they ring notes that belong to no tune.", "taken": "There is no wind, and still they ring. The sound goes into you and smooths you down.", "after": "The chimes hang still and do not ring." },
    "enchanted_aura": { "where": "wild", "name": "the shimmer", "verb": "Step into", "seen": "Over a ring of ground here the air shimmers like air over a fire, though it is cold. Nothing grows inside it, and nothing has trodden it.", "taken": "The air shimmers on your skin and stays there, a thin bright skin over your own that blows and spells will slide off.", "after": "The shimmer has gone out of the air." },
    "enchanted_flute": { "where": "within", "name": "the flute", "verb": "Play", "seen": "A flute of pale wood lies on a shelf by itself, with no dust on it, though there is dust on everything else.", "taken": "You have never played, but the flute knows how. The tune goes on in you after you have put it down.", "after": "The flute is a split old reed, and will not sound." },
    "enchanted_grove": { "where": "wild", "name": "the grove", "verb": "Rest in", "seen": "Birches stand here in a ring too regular to have grown that way, and the air inside it is warmer than the air outside.", "taken": "You sit among the trees, and the hum of them goes into you; when you stand, your hurts have closed.", "after": "The grove is only trees, and quiet." },
    "enchanted_mirror": { "where": "within", "name": "the mirror", "verb": "Look into", "seen": "A tall mirror stands against the wall in a frame gone black. What it shows is this room, nearly; the door in it is a little to the left of where the door is.", "taken": "Your face looks back, and then not quite your face: it turns aside a moment before you do. You understand, without being told, how a thing that comes at you can be sent back the way it came.", "after": "The mirror shows the room as it is now, and the door where the door is." },
    "enchanted_statue_garden": { "where": "within", "name": "the statues", "verb": "Walk among", "seen": "Statues fill the court: men and women in old dress, standing as if caught in the middle of something. Look away and back, and one of them is nearer.", "taken": "They turn their heads after you. When you have passed the last one you know how they were made, and how to make more.", "after": "The statues are only statues, and they do not turn." },
    "enchanted_statues": { "where": "within", "name": "the statue", "verb": "Take the hand of", "seen": "A statue of a woman stands here with one hand held out. Each time you look, the hand is held a little higher.", "taken": "The stone hand closes on yours, and stone runs up your arm under the skin and stays there, a ward and a shield.", "after": "The statue's hand is open, and does not close." },
    "enchanted_tapestry": { "where": "within", "name": "the tapestry", "verb": "Step behind", "seen": "A tapestry hangs the height of the wall, woven with a hunt in a wood. The hunters are not where they were when you came in, and one of the deer has gone.", "taken": "Behind it the air is close and smells of wool and leaves. When you come out the room does not seem to see you for a breath, and you know how to be where eyes slide off.", "after": "The tapestry hangs still, the hunt woven fast in it again." },
    "eternal_candle": { "where": "within", "name": "the candle", "verb": "Hold your hands to", "seen": "A candle burns in a niche, its flame quite steady, its wax not run at all. There is no smoke.", "taken": "The flame leans to you, and after it light itself seems a thing that cannot hurt you.", "after": "The candle has gone out, and the wick is cold." },
    "ethereal_fountain": { "where": "within", "name": "the fountain", "verb": "Drink from", "seen": "Water runs here into a basin that never fills, so clear it is hard to see where it stops and the air begins.", "taken": "The water is from somewhere else, and it heals like nothing from here.", "after": "The fountain has stopped. Its basin is dry." },
    "ethereal_music": { "where": "wild", "name": "the music", "verb": "Listen to", "seen": "A tune comes from nowhere you can find, low and sad, played on something with strings. It stops when you stop walking.", "taken": "You stand still and the tune finds you, and puts heart into you.", "after": "There is no music now, only the wind." },
    "floating_disk": { "where": "within", "name": "the floating disk", "verb": "Step onto", "seen": "A disk of grey stone, wide as a cartwheel, hangs a hand's breadth off the floor, turning slowly.", "taken": "It takes your weight and lifts, and when you step off you do not quite come down.", "after": "The disk lies on the floor, a plate of dull metal." },
    "floating_lights": { "where": "wild", "name": "the floating lights", "verb": "Stand among", "seen": "Lights the size of a fist hang in the air here, a dozen of them, drifting in and out of one another's paths.", "taken": "The lights close round your head and go out one by one, and after them your mind is shut like a box: nothing gets in.", "after": "The lights are gone." },
    "glowing_crystals": { "where": "within", "name": "the crystal", "verb": "Hold", "seen": "A crystal as long as a forearm stands in a cleft of the wall, glowing from inside, like a lamp seen through a hand.", "taken": "It warms in your hand and the glow goes into you, and you see three ways round everything.", "after": "The crystal is dull glass now." },
    "glowing_pool": { "where": "wild", "name": "the pool", "verb": "Bathe in", "seen": "A pool lies in the rocks here, and the water in it glows a soft green-white, brightest at the bottom.", "taken": "The water glows round you, and where it touches, hurts close as if they had never been.", "after": "The pool is dark water, only water." },
    "glowing_runes": { "where": "within", "name": "the runes", "verb": "Read", "seen": "Runes are cut round the doorway, and they glow one after another, as if someone were reading them aloud very slowly.", "taken": "You cannot read them, and then you can. They tell you nothing you could say again, but you see more after.", "after": "The runes are dark." },
    "illusory_visions": { "where": "wild", "name": "the visions", "verb": "Look into", "seen": "At the edge of your sight there are people: a woman at a well, a man with a dog, children running. Look straight at them and they are not there.", "taken": "At the edge of sight there are people who are not here. You look at them straight, and they show you what is clear and what is wise.", "after": "There is nothing at the edge of sight now." },
    "levitating_objects": { "where": "within", "name": "the floating things", "verb": "Reach among", "seen": "Things hang in the air of this room as if the floor had been taken out from under them: a cup, a stool, a shoe, a key, all turning slowly.", "taken": "Cups, stones and an old shoe turn in the air round your arm. When you draw it back it moves as lightly as they do.", "after": "Everything that floated lies on the floor where it fell." },
    "living_book": { "where": "within", "name": "the book", "verb": "Read", "seen": "A book lies open on a stand, and the writing on its page is being written, a line at a time, in a careful hand, with no one holding the pen.", "taken": "The book writes while you read it, and what it writes is how to call the lightning.", "after": "The pages are blank, and stay blank." },

data/goings-on/circus/circus.kyr:
Module circus "Wapshott's Peregrine Circus" {
  Description "A travelling circus on a circuit of three towns of the country: Colonel Florian Wapshott's Grand Peregrine Circus and Hippodrama, its ring, its wagons, its people, its debts, and the first beasts of its menagerie. It pitches three days in a town, strikes at first light on the fourth, and is on the road by six.".
  Entity party: group "Your company".

  // ── The circuit: three towns of the country, and the roads between ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  // The first town is where the Goose Fair is held; the second and third are its neighbours along the roads.
  Place town_a "The fair town" is settlement.
  Place town_b "The second town" is settlement.
  Place town_c "The third town" is settlement.
  Place green_a "The fair town's green" is room.
  Place green_b "The second town's green" is room.
  Place green_c "The third town's green" is room.
  Place road_ab "The road from the fair town" is room.
  Place road_bc "The road from the second town" is room.
  Place road_ca "The road from the third town" is room.
  Entity keeper_a: group "Whoever keeps travellers in the fair town".
  Entity keeper_b: group "Whoever keeps travellers in the second town".
  Entity keeper_c: group "Whoever keeps travellers in the third town".
  Entity priest_a: group "Whoever keeps the god in the fair town".
  Entity priest_b: group "Whoever keeps the god in the second town".
  Entity priest_c: group "Whoever keeps the god in the third town".
  Entity merchant_a: group "Whoever sells in the fair town".
  Entity merchant_b: group "Whoever sells in the second town".
  Entity merchant_c: group "Whoever sells in the third town".

  // ── What the circus is, as a concern: its purse, its larder, its canvas, its name in each town ──────────────────
  Kind concern. Entity wapshotts: concern "Wapshott's Circus".
  Measure strongbox(concern). Measure larder(concern). Measure canvas(concern). Measure arrears(concern).
  Measure moveDay(concern). Measure arrivedDay(concern). Measure house(concern). Measure quality(concern).
  Measure takenTonight(concern). Measure nights(concern). Measure feed(concern).
  Initially Set strongbox(wapshotts) to 14. Initially Set larder(wapshotts) to 3. Initially Set canvas(wapshotts) to 2.
  Initially Set feed(wapshotts) to 3. Initially Set moveDay(wapshotts) to 4. Initially Set arrivedDay(wapshotts) to 1.
  // How the circus stands in a town (by its ground there): what fills its benches.
  Measure standing(place).
  Initially Set standing(tober_a) to 2. Initially Set standing(tober_b) to 2. Initially Set standing(tober_c) to 1.

  // ── The grounds: a field outside each town, and the circus's rooms there while it is pitched ────────────────────
  Kind roomkind.
  Entity rk_tober: roomkind "the front". Entity rk_ring: roomkind "the ring". Entity rk_yard: roomkind "the backyard".
  Entity rk_wagons: roomkind "the wagons". Entity rk_beasts: roomkind "the menagerie".
  Relation groundRoom(place, roomkind, place). Relation groundOf(place, place). Relation greenOf(place, place).
  Relation nextGround(place, place). Relation roadOut(place, place).
  Relation here(place). Relation pitched(concern). Relation onRoad(concern). Relation current(concern, place) exclusive.
  Relation onWay(concern, place) exclusive.
  Relation travels(entity). Relation post(entity, roomkind) exclusive. Relation performer(entity). Relation away(entity).
  // Whoever is off the stage of this story for now (a rival not yet come, a lad gone home) is nowhere at all.
  Relation offstage(entity).
  Rule exit_stage when offstage(?p) and at(?p, ?q) { Retract at(?p, ?q). }

  Place tober_a "Wapshott's ground" is room within town_a at 5, 1.
  Place ring_a "the big top" is room within town_a at 6, 1 indoors.
  Place yard_a "the backyard of the circus" is room within town_a at 6, 2.
  Place wagons_a "the ring of living-wagons" is room within town_a at 6, 0.
  Place beasts_a "the menagerie tent" is room within town_a at 5, 2 indoors.
  Place tober_b "Wapshott's ground" is room within town_b at 5, 1.
  Place ring_b "the big top" is room within town_b at 6, 1 indoors.
  Place yard_b "the backyard of the circus" is room within town_b at 6, 2.
  Place wagons_b "the ring of living-wagons" is room within town_b at 6, 0.
  Place beasts_b "the menagerie tent" is room within town_b at 5, 2 indoors.
  Place tober_c "Wapshott's ground" is room within town_c at 5, 1.
  Place ring_c "the big top" is room within town_c at 6, 1 indoors.
  Place yard_c "the backyard of the circus" is room within town_c at 6, 2.
  Place wagons_c "the ring of living-wagons" is room within town_c at 6, 0.
  Place beasts_c "the menagerie tent" is room within town_c at 5, 2 indoors.

  Passage tober_lane_a "the field gate" is gate between green_a and tober_a taking 5 minutes.
  Passage tober_lane_b "the field gate" is gate between green_b and tober_b taking 5 minutes.
  Passage tober_lane_c "the field gate" is gate between green_c and tober_c taking 5 minutes.
  Passage flap_a "the flap of the big top" is doorway between tober_a and ring_a
    opening when here(tober_a) and (not showOn(wapshotts) or admitted(party)).
  Passage flap_b "the flap of the big top" is doorway between tober_b and ring_b
    opening when here(tober_b) and (not showOn(wapshotts) or admitted(party)).
  Passage flap_c "the flap of the big top" is doorway between tober_c and ring_c
    opening when here(tober_c) and (not showOn(wapshotts) or admitted(party)).
  Passage back_a "the way round behind the big top" is path between tober_a and yard_a taking 2 minutes
    opening when here(tober_a).
  Passage back_b "the way round behind the big top" is path between tober_b and yard_b taking 2 minutes
    opening when here(tober_b).

  // The first morning the circus is on the fair town's ground already, come in the evening before; it parades at four.
  Initially Assert pitched(wapshotts). Initially Assert here(tober_a). Initially Assert current(wapshotts, tober_a). Initially Assert onWay(wapshotts, road_ca).

  Query inRing(g: place, r: place) means groundRoom(g, rk_ring, r).
  Query circusRoom(r: place) means groundOf(r, ?g) and distinct(r, ?g).
  Query ringHere(r: place) means groundRoom(?g, rk_ring, r) and here(?g).
  Query atCircus(a: group) means at(a, ?r) and groundOf(?r, ?g) and here(?g).
  Query rehearsal() means pitched(wapshotts) and hour(clock) >= 9 and hour(clock) < 12.
  Query striking() means day(clock) >= moveDay(wapshotts).

  // ── The days: strike at six on the fourth morning, on the road till two, pitch, parade at four, play at seven ─────
  Rule strike_camp when pitched(wapshotts) and current(wapshotts, ?g) and day(clock) >= moveDay(wapshotts) and hour(clock) >= 6
    and hour(clock) < 14 and roadOut(?g, ?w) and nextGround(?g, ?n) {
    Retract pitched(wapshotts). Retract here(?g). Assert onRoad(wapshotts). Assert onWay(wapshotts, ?w). Assert current(wapshotts, ?n).
    Decrease canvas(wapshotts) by 1 or to nothing. Retract paraded(wapshotts). }
  Rule strike_seen near lusk when onRoad(wapshotts) and hour(clock) < 14 and not struckTold(wapshotts) says "Before it is light the canvasmen are at the guy-ropes. The big top comes down in a long sigh of canvas, the king-poles are lowered like masts, and by six the wagons are rolling, Bucephalus first, Colonel Wapshott on the box of the first wagon in his crimson coat, conducting the dawn." { Assert struckTold(wapshotts). }
  Relation struckTold(concern). Relation paraded(concern).
  Rule wagons_on_road when onRoad(wapshotts) and onWay(wapshotts, ?w) and travels(?p) and not at(?p, ?w) and not away(?p) and not travelsWith(?p, party) {
    Assert at(?p, ?w). }
  Rule wagons_pitch when onRoad(wapshotts) and hour(clock) >= 14 and (not wheelOff(wapshotts) or hour(clock) >= 18) and current(wapshotts, ?g) {
    Retract onRoad(wapshotts). Retract struckTold(wapshotts). Assert pitched(wapshotts). Assert here(?g).
    Set moveDay(wapshotts) to day(clock) + 3. Set arrivedDay(wapshotts) to day(clock). }
  Rule troupe_settles when pitched(wapshotts) and current(wapshotts, ?g) and travels(?p) and post(?p, ?k) and groundRoom(?g, ?k, ?r)
    and not at(?p, ?r) and not away(?p) and not travelsWith(?p, party) and not (performer(?p) and (showOn(wapshotts) or rehearsal()))
    and not parading(?p) {
    Assert at(?p, ?r). }
  Rule troupe_to_ring when pitched(wapshotts) and current(wapshotts, ?g) and performer(?p) and (showOn(wapshotts) or rehearsal())
    and groundRoom(?g, rk_ring, ?r) and not at(?p, ?r) and not away(?p) and not travelsWith(?p, party) and not parading(?p) {
    Assert at(?p, ?r). }
  // Whoever is inside when the canvas comes down is put out on the field, unless they ride with the wagons.
  Rule turned_out when circusRoom(?r) and at(party, ?r) and groundOf(?r, ?g) and not here(?g) and not riding(party)
    says "The canvas comes down round you. A canvasman puts you, quite kindly, out on the grass, and goes back for the pole." {
    Assert at(party, ?g). }
  Relation riding(group).
  Rule ride_out when onRoad(wapshotts) and riding(party) and onWay(wapshotts, ?w) and at(party, ?r) and groundOf(?r, ?g)
    and not here(?g) and not at(party, ?w)
    says "You ride out with the wagons, on the tail-board of the cookhouse wagon with Honoria Bulstrode's feet beside you, and the field you slept on goes away behind you, already only a ring of yellow grass." {
    Assert at(party, ?w). }
  Rule ride_in when pitched(wapshotts) and riding(party) and current(wapshotts, ?g) and onWay(wapshotts, ?w) and at(party, ?w)
    says "The wagons turn in off the road at a field gate, one after another, and Gideon Lusk walks into the middle of the field and stands there, and that is where the king-pole goes. By the time the kettle boils the big top is a shape against the sky." {
    Assert at(party, ?g). }

  // The parade: at four on the day it comes, round the town's green with the band.
  Relation parading(entity). Relation parades(entity).
  Rule parade_starts when pitched(wapshotts) and day(clock) == arrivedDay(wapshotts) and hour(clock) >= 16 and hour(clock) < 17
    and not paraded(wapshotts) and parades(?p) and current(wapshotts, ?g) and greenOf(?g, ?green) and not away(?p) and not travelsWith(?p, party) {
    Assert parading(?p). Assert at(?p, ?green). }
  Rule parade_ends when parading(?p) and hour(clock) >= 17 {
    Retract parading(?p). Assert paraded(wapshotts). }
  Rule parade_seen near wapshott when parading(wapshott) and not paradeTold(wapshotts) says "Here is the parade. First comes a drum, then a cornet, then a serpent, which is a black wooden horn that goes three times round a fat man; then Bucephalus, a grey horse of great age wearing a plume, who looks at the town as if he were thinking of buying it and had seen the drains; then the Colonel on foot in a crimson coat, shouting. Behind him a clown in white walks very slowly with a goose under each arm and does not say a word, and every child in the place follows him." { Assert paradeTold(wapshotts). }
  Relation paradeTold(concern).
  Rule parade_reset when pitched(wapshotts) and paradeTold(wapshotts) and hour(clock) >= 17 { Retract paradeTold(wapshotts). }
  Rule parade_draws when parading(wapshott) and current(wapshotts, ?g) and not paradeCounted(?g) and arrivedDay(wapshotts) >= 1 {
    Increase standing(?g) by 1. Assert paradeCounted(?g). }
  Relation paradeCounted(place).
  Rule parade_count_resets when onRoad(wapshotts) and paradeCounted(?g) { Retract paradeCounted(?g). }

  // ── The fields themselves, with the circus and without ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe tober_a_scene at tober_a when true "A grazing field outside {town_a}, sloping a little toward the road, with a five-barred gate and a lime tree.".
  Observe tober_b_scene at tober_b when true "A rough meadow behind the last houses of {town_b}, with a pond in one corner where the geese of the town come to complain.".
  Observe tober_c_scene at tober_c when true "A long field outside {town_c} with an old stone cross at the top of it, worn to a stump, that someone has hung a horseshoe on.".
  Observe tober_up near pole when here(?g) and at(pole, ?g) "The big top stands in the middle of the field, striped red and dirty white, its king-pole flying a pennant that says WAPSHOTT'S in letters gone pink. Guy-ropes run out from it to stakes in every direction, so that walking anywhere is a kind of dance. Before the flap a painted front of boards announces THE GRAND PEREGRINE CIRCUS & HIPPODRAMA, PATRONIZED BY THE NOBILITY, and someone has written under it in chalk, WHICH NOBILITY.".
  Thing pole "the king-pole" at tober_a is scenery {
    State standing "The big top's king-pole stands up through the canvas, and the pennant snaps.".
    State packed "The big top is folded on the canvas wagon, poles and all, under a tarpaulin lashed down with forty knots.".
  }
  Initially Assert travels(pole). Initially Assert post(pole, rk_tober).
  Observe flap_laced near pole when showOn(wapshotts) and at(pole, ?r) and not admitted(party) "The show is on. The flap of the big top is laced back, and a canvasman stands in it with his arms folded; beside it, in the hatch of the ticket wagon, Ada Thripp sits with her cash-box. One coin, and no arguing.".
  Observe tober_bare_a at tober_a when not here(tober_a) "There is a ring of yellowed grass in the middle of the field, and a scatter of old sawdust, and deep ruts going out at the gate.".
  Observe tober_bare_b at tober_b when not here(tober_b) "There is a ring of yellowed grass in the middle of the field, and a scatter of old sawdust, and deep ruts going out at the gate.".
  Observe tober_bare_c at tober_c when not here(tober_c) "There is a ring of yellowed grass in the middle of the field, and a scatter of old sawdust, and deep ruts going out at the gate.".
  Observe ring_scene near ringpost when ringHere(?r) and at(ringpost, ?r) "Inside, the big top is brown and warm and smells of trodden grass, sawdust, horse and oranges. Benches rise on scaffolding round the ring, which is a low wall of painted boards forty-two feet across, because that is the size a horse likes to canter in. High up between the two king-poles a wire is strung, so fine you lose it against the canvas.".
  Thing ringpost "the ring" at tober_a is scenery {
    State ready "The ring's painted boards are scuffed with a hundred towns' boots.".
    State packed "The ring boards are stacked in the back of a wagon like a load of painted fencing.".
  }
  Initially Assert travels(ringpost). Initially Assert post(ringpost, rk_ring).
  Observe yard_scene near cookfire when at(cookfire, ?r) and pitched(wapshotts) "Behind the big top is the backyard, where the circus lives: horse lines, a cookhouse fire with a kettle on a chain, washing on the guy-ropes, a heap of hay, a man asleep in a barrow. Through the gap in the canvas you can hear the ring.".
  Thing cookfire "the cookhouse fire" at tober_a is scenery {
    State lit "Honoria Bulstrode's cookhouse fire burns under a black kettle and a pot the size of a font.".
    State packed "The cookhouse wagon goes along with its chimney smoking, Honoria on the step, and a smell of bacon trailing behind it for a quarter of a mile.".
  }
  Initially Assert travels(cookfire). Initially Assert post(cookfire, rk_yard).
  Observe wagons_scene near wagonring when at(wagonring, ?r) and pitched(wapshotts) "The living-wagons stand in a ring with their shafts down and their steps let down, like a village that walked here: green, yellow, a blue one with stars, a black one with the word SIBYL in gold. Chimneys smoke. On the steps of the biggest, which is crimson and has a brass knocker in the shape of a lion, there is a boot-scraper and a sign: THE COLONEL. KNOCK. WAIT. KNOCK AGAIN.".
  Thing wagonring "the ring of wagons" at tober_a is scenery {
    State standing "The living-wagons stand shafts-down in their ring.".
    State packed "The living-wagons sway along the road nose to tail, their chimneys smoking, washing still pegged on a line between two of them.".
  }
  Initially Assert travels(wagonring). Initially Assert post(wagonring, rk_wagons).
  Rule camp_packs when onRoad(wapshotts) and not state(pole, packed) {
    Assert state(pole, packed). Assert state(ringpost, packed). Assert state(cookfire, packed). Assert state(wagonring, packed). Assert state(beastpost, packed). }

  Topic where_a_b with keeper_a "Ask {keeper_a} where the circus is now" when knows(actor, heard_circus) and not here(tober_a) and (current(wapshotts, tober_b) or current(wapshotts, tober_r)) {
    Says "'At {town_b},' says {keeper_a}, 'or on the road there. They go on to {town_c} after, and they're back here after that. Three days in a town, always, and then six o'clock in the morning and away.'".
  }
  Topic where_a_c with keeper_a "Ask {keeper_a} where the circus is now" when knows(actor, heard_circus) and not here(tober_a) and current(wapshotts, tober_c) {
    Says "'At {town_c},' says {keeper_a}, 'or on the road there; and here next, by the road from {town_c}. Three days a town; ask the carrier which of them it is.'".
  }
  Topic where_b_a with keeper_b "Ask {keeper_b} where the circus is now" when knows(actor, heard_circus) and not here(tober_b) and not here(tober_r) and current(wapshotts, tober_a) {

  Topic where_b_c with keeper_b "Ask {keeper_b} where the circus is now" when knows(actor, heard_circus) and not here(tober_b) and not here(tober_r) and current(wapshotts, tober_c) {

  Topic where_c_a with keeper_c "Ask {keeper_c} where the circus is now" when knows(actor, heard_circus) and not here(tober_c) and current(wapshotts, tober_a) {

  }
  Topic where_c_b with keeper_c "Ask {keeper_c} where the circus is now" when knows(actor, heard_circus) and not here(tober_c) and (current(wapshotts, tober_b) or current(wapshotts, tober_r)) {
    Says "'At {town_b},' says {keeper_c}, 'and here next, by the road from {town_b}. They stop three days, and then the wagons come.'".
  }
  Observe road_wagons near pole when onRoad(wapshotts) and onWay(wapshotts, ?w) and at(pole, ?w) "Wapshott's Circus is on the road: eleven wagons nose to tail, a canvas wagon stacked with poles, the cookhouse wagon smoking as it goes, the living-wagons swaying, the ponies on a string behind, Bucephalus out in front at his own pace, which is the pace of everyone. A painted board on the last wagon says WAPSHOTT'S. WE ARE COMING TO YOUR TOWN. Someone has written under it, IN THE END.".

  // Quirk goes ahead at ten the day before the strike, and is on the next town's green with his paste-pot.

    and nextGround(?g, ?n) and greenOf(?n, ?green) and billOf(?n, ?b) and not away(quirk) {

    Retract away(quirk). Retract quirkAhead(quirk). }

  Rule quirk_bills_more when away(quirk) and current(wapshotts, ?n) and onRoad(wapshotts) and not billedAhead(?n) { Increase standing(?n) by 1. Assert billedAhead(?n). }
  Relation billedAhead(place).
  Rule billed_reset when here(?g) and billedAhead(?g) and day(clock) > arrivedDay(wapshotts) { Retract billedAhead(?g). }

  // ── What the towns say of it, wherever it is ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Entity heard_circus: fact "Wapshott's Grand Peregrine Circus is going round the country, three days in a town: {town_a}, then {town_b}, then {town_c}, and back. It plays nightly at seven, a coin a head.".
  Initially Assert established(heard_circus).
  Topic keeper_a_here with keeper_a "Ask {keeper_a} about the circus" when here(tober_a) once {
    Says "'Wapshott's,' says {keeper_a}, with the face of someone who has had a circus in the house before. 'Out in the field past the green. They'll play tonight at seven, and the Colonel will come in here after and order the best of everything on account. Go and see them. Pay at the flap. Don't lend the Colonel anything; he means to pay you back, that's what makes him dangerous.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, heard_circus). }
  }
  Topic keeper_a_away with keeper_a "Ask {keeper_a} about the circus" when not here(tober_a) once {
    Says "'Wapshott's? Gone round the circuit,' says {keeper_a}. 'They're three days in a town: here, then {town_b}, then {town_c}, and back here again, round and round like a horse in a ring. You'll find them at one of the three, or on the road between, eleven wagons and a horse in front setting the pace. They're always back here for the Goose Fair, if there's a Fair this year. They say this year there is.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, heard_circus). }
  }
  Topic keeper_b_here with keeper_b "Ask {keeper_b} about the circus" when here(tober_b) once {
    Says "'Out on the pond meadow,' says {keeper_b}. 'The geese are beside themselves. Last time they were here a goose got into the big top and went on in the middle of the Sylph and got the biggest hand of the night. I'm going tonight. Everybody's going tonight. My mother's going and she hasn't been out of the house since the flood.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, heard_circus). }
  }
  Topic keeper_b_away with keeper_b "Ask {keeper_b} about the circus" when not here(tober_b) once {
    Says "'Wapshott's?' says {keeper_b}. 'Round and about. Three days in {town_a}, three here, three in {town_c}. A man comes ahead of them with a paste-pot and bills everything that stands still. Last time he billed the vicar's cow. You'll know they're near when the cow says COMING.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, heard_circus). }
  }
  Topic keeper_c_here with keeper_c "Ask {keeper_c} about the circus" when here(tober_c) once {
    Says "'Up at the cross field,' says {keeper_c}. 'They come through every round and we're always the last and the smallest and the Colonel always says we are his favourite, and the thing is, I think he means it. Go tonight. The old clown, Mumchance, doesn't say a word the whole night and you laugh till you have to sit down in the road.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, heard_circus). }
  }
  Topic keeper_c_away with keeper_c "Ask {keeper_c} about the circus" when not here(tober_c) once {
    Says "'They'll be round,' says {keeper_c}. 'Wapshott's goes {town_a}, {town_b}, here, and back; three days a town. If you want them sooner, ask at {town_a}: that's where they winter, when they can afford a winter, and where the Fair is.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, heard_circus). }
  }
  Topic priest_a_circus with priest_a "Ask {priest_a} about the circus" when true once {
    Says "{priest_a} sighs. 'The Colonel came to the shrine last year and asked if the god would care to be patron of a Hippodrama. I said the god does not take patronage. He said in that case he would put the god's name on the bills for nothing, as a courtesy.' A pause. 'He did, too. In quite small letters. I found I did not mind as much as I expected.'".
  }
  Topic merchant_a_circus with merchant_a "Ask {merchant_a} about the circus" when true once {
    Says "'They buy flour, bacon, oats, lamp oil, paint, and candles by the gross,' says {merchant_a}, 'and they pay in coin, mostly, and the rest in tickets, and a man can only see the Sylph of the Wire so many times.' A sniff. 'Nine. A man can see her nine times.'".
  }
}
data/goings-on/circus/isle.kyr:
Module circus "Wapshott's Peregrine Circus" {
  // ── The Isle of Sarn, which the Progress kept ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // A drowned volcano's rim a long way down the sea, laid out by the Household of the Progress four hundred years ago
  // as a preserve for the beasts of the southern sea, kept by wardens until the last Progress, then forgotten by
  // everyone but the Ormes' empty cages. An open place, not a gauntlet: six regions, no order, and a dozen ways to be
  // useful or foolish in each. It is reached only by the brig Sundial, from the fair town's quay once Sir Gervase has
  // chartered her (voyage.kyr).
  Place sarn "The Isle of Sarn" is region.
  Place s_shore "the Progress's shore" is wilderness within sarn at 1, 3.
  Place s_delta "the mangrove delta" is wilderness within sarn at 0, 2.
  Place s_forest "the cycad forest" is wilderness within sarn at 1, 2.
  Place s_plain "the fern plain" is wilderness within sarn at 2, 1.
  Place s_basin "the steam basin" is wilderness within sarn at 1, 0.
  Place s_cliffs "the nesting cliffs" is wilderness within sarn at 3, 2.
  Place pavilion_house "the Preserve-house" is building within s_shore.

  Place landing "the Progress's landing" is room within s_shore at 1, 3 outdoors.
  Place cage_row "the cage-row" is room within s_shore at 2, 3 outdoors.
  Place preserve_hall "the Preserve-house hall" is room within pavilion_house at 1, 2.
  Place delta_edge "the edge of the delta" is room within s_delta at 0, 3 outdoors.
  Place egg_beds "the egg-beds" is room within s_delta at 0, 2 outdoors.
  Place harrow_camp "Captain Harrow's camp" is room within s_delta at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Place channels "the black channels" is room within s_delta at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place forest_edge "the cycad forest's edge" is room within s_forest at 1, 2 outdoors.
  Place cycad_aisle "the cycad aisle" is room within s_forest at 2, 2 outdoors.
  Place hook_den "the hook-claws' hollow" is room within s_forest at 2, 1 outdoors.
  Place kingsfoil_hollow "the sheltered hollow" is room within s_forest at 3, 1 outdoors.
  Place plain_south "the southern fern plain" is room within s_plain at 2, 2 outdoors.
  Place plain_mid "the middle of the fern plain" is room within s_plain at 2, 1 outdoors.
  Place lake_shore "the lake shore" is room within s_plain at 3, 0 outdoors.
  Place plain_ridge "the ridge above the plain" is room within s_plain at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place tyrant_hollow "the tyrant's hollow" is room within s_plain at 2, 0 outdoors.
  Place basin_rim "the rim of the steam basin" is room within s_basin at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place bone_beds "the bone-beds" is room within s_basin at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place tar_pits "the tar-pits" is room within s_basin at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place cliff_foot "the foot of the nesting cliffs" is room within s_cliffs at 3, 3 outdoors.
  Place ledges "the nesting ledges" is room within s_cliffs at 3, 2 outdoors.
  Place cliff_top "the top of the cliffs" is room within s_cliffs at 3, 1 outdoors.

  // The gangways belong to voyage.kyr.
  Passage landing_row "the cage-row" is path between landing and cage_row taking 5 minutes.
  Passage row_hall "the Preserve-house door" is door between cage_row and preserve_hall.
  Passage landing_delta "the shore path to the delta" is path between landing and delta_edge taking 30 minutes.
  Passage delta_beds "the boardwalk to the egg-beds" is path between delta_edge and egg_beds taking 20 minutes.
  Passage beds_camp "the creek path" is path between egg_beds and harrow_camp taking 20 minutes.
  Passage camp_channels "the mangrove roots" is path between harrow_camp and channels taking 20 minutes.
  Passage landing_forest "the old keepers' road" is road between landing and forest_edge taking 40 minutes.
  Passage forest_aisle "the cycad aisle" is path between forest_edge and cycad_aisle taking 20 minutes.
  Passage aisle_den "the track to the hollow" is path between cycad_aisle and hook_den taking 20 minutes.
  Passage aisle_kingsfoil "the game-trail round the hollow" is path between cycad_aisle and kingsfoil_hollow taking 30 minutes hidden until hollow_way_known.
  Passage den_kingsfoil "the dry stream-bed" is path between hook_den and kingsfoil_hollow taking 20 minutes.
  Passage aisle_plain "the forest's far edge" is path between cycad_aisle and plain_south taking 30 minutes.
  Passage plain_cross "the herd-trail" is path between plain_south and plain_mid taking 40 minutes.
  Passage plain_lake "the trail to the lake" is path between plain_mid and lake_shore taking 30 minutes.
  Passage plain_ridge_way "the climb to the ridge" is path between plain_south and plain_ridge taking 30 minutes.
  Passage ridge_basin "the ridge road to the basin" is path between plain_ridge and basin_rim taking 40 minutes.
  Passage mid_hollow "the trampled way to the hollow" is path between plain_mid and tyrant_hollow taking 20 minutes.
  Passage rim_bones "the steaming ledge" is path between basin_rim and bone_beds taking 20 minutes.
  Passage bones_tar "the sulphur flat" is path between bone_beds and tar_pits taking 20 minutes.
  Passage lake_cliffs "the shore track to the cliffs" is path between lake_shore and cliff_foot taking 1 hour.
  Passage landing_cliffs "the strand to the cliffs" is path between landing and cliff_foot taking 1 hour.
  Passage cliff_ledge_way "the ledge path" is path between cliff_foot and ledges taking 30 minutes needing climbing or rope.
  Passage ledges_top "the last pitch" is path between ledges and cliff_top taking 30 minutes needing climbing or rope.
  Passage top_lake "the headland track down to the lake" is path between cliff_top and lake_shore one way taking 1 hour.

  // ── The sights, told as the preserve's own ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe landing_scene at landing when true "A stone quay stands at the mouth of a green bay, built by people who meant it to be seen from the sea. On every post is cut a crowned wheel, and the posts are hung with creeper. The jungle comes down to the quay and stops, as if told to.".
  Observe cage_row_scene at cage_row when true "A row of iron-barred cages along the shore, each as big as a hay-cart and each open, with a bronze plate on its door that was once legible. Every floor is a sheet of fern-green. Something small has been using the nearest cage for a nest, and the bars have been rubbed bright at a height of two feet.".
  Observe preserve_hall_scene at preserve_hall when true "A hall with a vaulted roof of black timber, still sound, and a floor of tiles with the crowned wheel in the middle. Long tables stand along the walls under sheets of rotted canvas, and over the hearth a painted board gives the Rule of the Preserve in letters a hand high. Dust lies on everything, and in the dust, quite recent, there are the prints of small three-toed feet.".
  Observe delta_edge_scene at delta_edge when true "The shore gives out into a delta: mangroves on their stilt roots, black water in green channels, and mud banks marked with the tracks of things that came down to nest. The air is hot, wet and smells of eggs. A boardwalk of old timber runs out over the mud.".
  Observe egg_beds_scene at egg_beds when true "Mounds of sand and rotted leaf rise out of the mud, each as big as a table, each warm to the hand. Eggs lie in rings in the nearest, grey and loaf-big. The ground is covered in the three-toed tracks of the animals that guard them, and there are no animals here now, which is the worst of it.".
  Observe harrow_camp_scene at harrow_camp when true "A camp of tents and a stockade of cut mangrove, with nets drying on poles and a row of crates, some of which are breathing. A flag with a hippodrome painted on it hangs limp over the largest tent. Men in oilskins sit about with mugs and look at you without moving.".
  Observe channels_scene at channels when true "The mangrove roots close overhead into a green tunnel. The water is black and perfectly still. Things have been dragged to the bank and eaten there, and a crocodile's bones, picked clean, are propped against a root as if somebody had thought of it as a warning.".
  Observe forest_edge_scene at forest_edge when true "The jungle begins in a wall of cycads: palms like pineapples on trunks, crowned in fronds taller than a man, and under them ferns to the waist. Light comes down in green coins. Something small runs ahead of you on the path, in short, stopped runs, looking back.".
  Observe cycad_aisle_scene at cycad_aisle when true "A long aisle where something large has pushed a way through the cycads and left it. The ferns are laid flat in a trough as broad as a cart. The air is full of pollen and the click of insects, and ahead the click stops, all at once, and the whole forest is listening.".
  Observe hook_den_scene at hook_den when true "A hollow in the forest floor, trodden bare, with a litter of stripped bones and, in the middle, a clutch-ring of scraped earth, empty. The place is full of the smell of wet feathers. A single great curved claw lies in the dirt where a body has dragged it, as long as a scythe-blade.".
  Observe kingsfoil_hollow_scene at kingsfoil_hollow when true "A sheltered hollow where the cycads open and let in the sun. Nothing in it is large. Moss and low herbs grow on a bank by a spring, and the ground is dry, and every animal on the island seems to have agreed to leave it alone.".
  Observe plain_south_scene at plain_south when true "The jungle opens on a plain of fern to the horizon, flat and green under a wide sky, with the grey rim of a drowned mountain far to the north. Birds like tall grey feathered men are feeding in the ferns, and lift their heads all together as you come out of the trees.".
  Observe plain_mid_scene at plain_mid when true "The herd-trail is a road, broad as a street, trodden into the ferns and into the clay under them, and it has not been made by anything that walks in ones. The wind is steady, and in it, now and then, there is a deep sound from a long way off, like a door the size of a cathedral swinging on its hinges.".
  Observe lake_shore_scene at lake_shore when true "A lake lies in the crater's lap under a rim of low cloud, wide and still. Its southern shore is a fan of cut mud and the footprints in it are a yard across. The ferns go down to the water in a trough, and the cycads at the margin have been stripped clean to the height of a house.".
  Observe plain_ridge_scene at plain_ridge when true "A low ridge of grey rock stands above the plain, and from it the whole of the plain can be seen: the herd-trails like roads, the dark line of the forest, the lake, and a cloud of steam on the north horizon where the ground itself boils. Nothing on the plain is in a hurry. It is the first place on the island where it seems safe to sit.".
  Observe tyrant_hollow_scene at tyrant_hollow when true "A hollow in the plain where the ferns have been flattened into a bed. The hollow is ringed with bones, stripped and split, and the biggest are the ribs of something as large as an ox. Some of the bones have been cracked for the marrow. The ground here is the colour of old blood, and quiet.".
  Observe basin_rim_scene at basin_rim when true "The rim looks down on a bowl of yellow ground, steaming, with pools of every colour from jade to rust. Geysers breathe in the distance. A smell of bad eggs comes up with the heat, and nothing grows on the flat except yellow crust.".
  Observe bone_beds_scene at bone_beds when true "A shelf of ground below the rim where, over a long time, things have come to die. The bones are piled as the sea piles wrack, in drifts, white and black and brown, and the biggest of them are the length of a ship's mast. Among them lie teeth, shed in the ordinary way of things, each as long as a hand.".
  Observe tar_pits_scene at tar_pits when true "A flat of black pitch between yellow crusts, skinned with a rainbow, and in the middle of it something that has been dying for a long while: a three-horned head and a bowed back, sunk to the shoulders, with its eye turned towards you.".
  Observe cliff_foot_scene at cliff_foot when true "The land ends in a wall of black rock a hundred and fifty feet high, rough with ledges, and every ledge is white with droppings. The air over it is full of wings. A fish-smell hangs on the wind, and the sound is a single great quarrel, going on for ever.".
  Observe ledges_scene at ledges when true "A broad ledge in the face of the cliff, a floor of old nests, and eggs in them, long and leathery, in their hundreds. The colony watches with a thousand heads of bony crest and long bills, and does not move. The wind off the sea tears at your coat.".
  Observe cliff_top_scene at cliff_top when true "The top of the cliffs is a green headland open to the whole sky. The colony drops off the edge below in one long unrolling, wing after wing, and catches the morning wind, and the sea is white with their shadows. From here the whole island is laid out like a map.".

  // ── Telegraphs: what tells of a danger before it is met ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe hook_click at cycad_aisle as sound when at(hook_claws, hook_den) and not dead(hook_claws) "Somewhere ahead a hard click, click, like a fingernail on stone, passes along the forest from one side to the other, and then there is no sound at all.".
  Observe tyrant_ground_shake at plain_mid as sound when not dead(tyrant) and (hour(clock) >= 16 and hour(clock) < 21) "Through the soles of your feet, steady, a rhythm: a weight, and a weight, and a weight. The birds in the ferns have gone up in a body. The ferns to the north are laid flat in a line.".
  Observe tyrant_carcass at plain_south when not dead(tyrant) "Half a stilt-runner lies in the ferns, bitten in two. The bite is a yard across, and has taken the bone with it.".
  Observe sail_wing_shadow at cliff_foot as sign when true "A white streak of droppings has been laid across your boots from a great height, and a shadow the span of a cart goes over the strand and comes back.".
  Observe croc_bones at channels as sign when not dead(delta_croc) "A heap of picked bones against the roots, and a long groove in the mud from the water's edge.".
  Observe spoor_runner at forest_edge as sign when true "Tracks the size of a thrush's, three-toed, going everywhere at once, and a place where a nest of leaves has been taken to pieces by hands.".

  // ── Hazards of the island ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Hazard hot_ground "The hot crust" means "Deal (2d6) fire damage to ally unless dexterity save against (13).".
  Hazard sulphur_gas "The sulphur gas" means "Deal (1d6) poison damage to ally unless constitution save against (13). Apply poisoned to ally for 3 turns unless constitution save against (13).".
  Hazard herd_stride "A herd crossing" means "Deal (2d6) physical damage to ally unless dexterity save against (14).".
  Hazard tyrant_rush "The tyrant's rush" means "Deal (5d6) physical damage to ally unless dexterity save against (16).".
  Hazard bog_pitch "The pitch" means "Deal (1d6) physical damage to ally unless strength save against (13).".
}

data/imbar/events.kyr:
Module canon "Imbar and the planes" {
  // ── What may befall ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // World events: what an adventure brings about that any other may read. Each is a fact, what someone who has heard
  // of it knows; befell(event) says that it has happened, which the adventure that brings it about asserts in play,
  // once, and nothing undoes. None has befallen in a world that has just begun.
  // The Grand Tour's, at Sennet: the Rose, the Door of Doors, Cloudgate and the Whelm under it, the Rector, Perrin.
  Entity rose_made_whole: fact "The Rose of the Winds has been made whole.".
  Entity door_of_doors_opened: fact "The Door of Doors, in the House of Doors, has been opened.".
  Entity cloudgate_fell: fact "Cloudgate has come down out of the sky into Sennet bay.".
  Entity whelm_crushed: fact "The Whelm under Sennet bay was crushed when Cloudgate came down on it.".
  Entity whelm_emptied: fact "The merfolk of the Whelm were warned in time to leave it.".
  Entity merfolk_gone_home: fact "The merfolk of the Whelm have gone home through the Water Door.".
  Entity rector_through_the_door: fact "The Rector of the House of Doors went through the Door of Doors, and has not come back.".
  Entity rector_taken: fact "The Rector of the House of Doors has been taken up by the Watch.".
  Entity rector_fled: fact "The Rector of the House of Doors has fled.".
  Entity rector_barred: fact "The Rector of the House of Doors was kept from the Door of Doors, and would not go through it.".
  Entity perrin_lives: fact "Perrin Halyard, who was given out for dead, is alive, and has come up out of the sea.".
  Entity perrin_lost: fact "Perrin Halyard is dead.".

  // Beyond the Door of Doors' house, under the Nexus floor: the black square that opens on the Slack. What befell there.
  Entity slack_opened: fact "The black square in the Nexus floor of the House of Doors has been opened, and the stair under it goes down to the Slack.".
  Entity remainder_harboured: fact "The ship Remainder, out of the Slack, has been given harbour at the House of Doors, and her people have come ashore.".
  Entity remainder_kept: fact "The ship Remainder was left in the Slack, and her people sail on in it.".
  Entity mechanus_seen: fact "A company has stood on the threshold of Mechanus, from the deck of a ship out of the Slack.".
  Entity remainder_steadied: fact "The lens of a lamp that was lent to an island has been fitted to the mast of the Remainder, and her pin is still.".

  // Three small countries' consequences (corpus pass, branch adventure/p2-corpus-b): read by their neighbours' lore.
  Entity scarth_kept: fact "The company crossed the Scarth causeway at noon and left the light burning with its keeper alive in it.".
  Entity scarth_lost: fact "The Scarth light's keeper or the widow who came to it was taken by the sea in the night, and the company walked out without them.".
  Entity calx_opened: fact "The Calx Gate under Tallow Edge has been raised, and the Aeneans' road runs open under the ridge.".
  Entity tallow_names: fact "The fourteen names of the Brasiers' Company's dead have been read aloud, in Swallet or over the stacked boots.".
  Entity sallowfield_held: fact "Sallowfield stood through its three nights, and its green is not burned.".
  Entity sallowfield_burned: fact "Sallowfield's green was burned in the night, and the village is a floor of black timbers.".
}
data/imbar/outer.kyr:
Module canon "Imbar and the planes" {
  // ── The outer planes ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // Orsino's nine, each under its law (the catalog's plane condition: its spell DC is held by everyone fighting
  // anywhere in it), and the Abyss, Nirvana and the Mount of the Exalted, which have none. A module puts no law of its
  // own on them: its laws go on its own places.
  Entity plane_arcadia: law "the law of Arcadia". Entity plane_cthelll: law "the law of Cthelll".
  Entity plane_gehenna: law "the law of Gehenna". Entity plane_hades: law "the law of Hades".
  Entity plane_limbo: law "the law of Limbo". Entity plane_mechanus: law "the law of Mechanus".
  Entity plane_pandemonium: law "the law of Pandemonium". Entity plane_ysgard: law "the law of Ysgard".
  Entity plane_zephyrus: law "the law of Zephyrus".

  Place outer_arcadia "Arcadia" is plane.
  Place outer_arcadia_region "Arcadia" is region within outer_arcadia elsewhere.
  Place outer_arcadia_land "the threshold of Arcadia" is wilderness within outer_arcadia_region at 0, 0 elsewhere.
  Place outer_arcadia_threshold "the threshold of Arcadia" is room within outer_arcadia_land at 0, 0.
  Initially Assert law(outer_arcadia, plane_arcadia).
  Observe outer_arcadia_seen at outer_arcadia_threshold when true "Green country in the light of a spring that does not end, and everything in leaf.".

  // Spelt as the owner spells it; the catalog's condition keeps Orsino's spelling in its id.
  Place outer_cthell "Cthelll" is plane.
  Place outer_cthell_region "Cthelll" is region within outer_cthell elsewhere.
  Place outer_cthell_land "the threshold of Cthelll" is wilderness within outer_cthell_region at 0, 0 elsewhere.
  Place outer_cthell_threshold "the threshold of Cthelll" is room within outer_cthell_land at 0, 0.
  Initially Assert law(outer_cthell, plane_cthelll).
  Observe outer_cthell_seen at outer_cthell_threshold when true "Black water and reeds in a fog that does not lift.".

  Place outer_gehenna "Gehenna" is plane.
  Place outer_gehenna_region "Gehenna" is region within outer_gehenna elsewhere.
  Place outer_gehenna_land "the threshold of Gehenna" is wilderness within outer_gehenna_region at 0, 0 elsewhere.
  Place outer_gehenna_threshold "the threshold of Gehenna" is room within outer_gehenna_land at 0, 0.
  Initially Assert law(outer_gehenna, plane_gehenna).
  Observe outer_gehenna_seen at outer_gehenna_threshold when true "Black slopes of broken rock under a sky of ash, and the smell of sulphur.".

  Place outer_hades "Hades" is plane.
